#### ✅ `.46` SLICE 4 (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0086`, 2026-08-25 session #263) — **(d) DISCHARGED: the all-profile re-audit is CLEAN on every site, and it found THREE defects the single-profile reading could not — including FOUR UNIT TESTS RED ON HEAD, three of them shipped by (c) itself**

###### ⭐⭐⭐ THE ONE-LINE RESULT, AND THE ONE-LINE COST

Every live site is correct under every profile. **Getting there cost four red tests, one refuted
census claim and one false invariant** — none of which the `verilog_2005`-only reading could reach,
and all of which were sitting in the tree while `-0085` published *"ALL 27 PASS"* and five green
gates.

###### [1] THE PROFILE UNIVERSE IS FIVE STATES WIDE, AND `.46` AUDITED ONE

`.46`'s routing evidence audited the live sites under `verilog_2005` alone. The runtime universe is:

| state | how it is reached | what it does to gating |
|---|---|---|
| **unspecified** | no `--grammar-profile` | ⭐ NO gate is applied at all — every rule live |
| `sv_2017` / `sv_2023` / `verilog_2005` | a declared spelling | the ordinary case |
| **undeclared** | an unknown spelling, passed through **un-coerced** (the pinned `profile_alias_unknown_passthrough` combinator) | ⛔ EVERY gated rule absent at once — **427 of 1 537** |

⭐ **Neither of the two extra states can be named in a `@profiles` list**, which is why an audit
driven off the declared list misses both. `unspecified` is safe *by construction* (no gate ⇒ no
vacuity) and that is now measured rather than assumed; `undeclared` is where the sentinel notes live.

###### [2] THE SITE CENSUS, RECONCILED ACROSS BOTH ENGINES — 4 negative + 1 positive source sites, **5** emitted wrappers

| lint note (rule × profile) | polarity | emitted wrapper in `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs` |
|---|---|---|
| `non_keyword_identifier` × undeclared | NEG | `parse_non_keyword_identifier` — `applies(&[], true)` |
| `simple_identifier_no_scope` × {v2005, undeclared} | NEG | `parse_simple_identifier_no_scope` — `applies(&["verilog_2005"], true)` |
| `scope_free_identifier` × {v2005, undeclared} | NEG | ⭐ **TWO** wrappers in `parse_scope_free_identifier` |
| `system_tf_call` × {v2005, undeclared} | NEG | `parse_system_tf_call` — `applies(&["verilog_2005"], true)` |
| `class_scope_type` × v2005 | POS | none — deliberately not bypassed |

⭐⭐ **5 emitted against 4 source negative sites is CORRECT, and the reconciliation is the point.**
Codegen INLINES `simple_identifier_no_scope` into `scope_free_identifier`'s first alternative, so one
source site is emitted twice (line 47507 sits after the regex `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*`, line 47962
after `\\[!-~]+`). **The lint counts SOURCE sites; the parser emits per INLINED site.** A reader
diffing the two counts without this row reads a missing repair.

###### [3] ⛔⛔ THE ROUTING CLAIM *"nothing else in the v2005 grammar can consume `::`"* IS UNSUPPORTED — WHICH IS **NOT** THE SAME AS REFUTED, AND THE FIRST WRITE-UP OF THIS SECTION SAID REFUTED

That is a **census claim**, and no census stood behind it — the same shape
[[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]] corrected twice already in this repository.
Run over all **413** terminals of the grammar (74 quoted + 339 regex, **0** uncompilable, so the
population is closed), exactly **2** rules carry a terminal that can consume a leading `:`:

| rule | `@profiles` | live under v2005? | terminal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `colon` | *(ungated)* | ⭐ **yes** | `":"` |
| `scope_resolution` | `["sv_2017","sv_2023"]` | no | `"::"` |

⇒ **a live v2005 consumer of the first colon exists.**

⚠️⚠️ **AND THAT DOES NOT REFUTE THE SENTENCE — the first write-up of this section said it did, and a
director challenge caught it.** `colon` consumes ONE `:`; consuming `::` by that route needs TWO
adjacent `colon`s at the guarded position, and **whether the grammar admits that is UNMEASURED** —
this leaf says so itself two sections down, so the artifact contradicted itself inside one commit.
⛔ The honest verdict is **UNSUPPORTED**: `.46` published the sentence as the REASON the live sites
were safe, and the census that would establish it was never run. What the census does establish is
that the nearest hazard — a live `:` consumer under the narrow dialect — **exists**, so the margin
was an argument rather than a measurement. Moot for soundness only because (c) shipped and the guard
is now enforced.

⭐ **Why the distinction is worth the words:** *refuted* would mean the live sites were unsafe
pre-repair, which nothing here shows; *unsupported* means the safety rested on an unrun census, which
is exactly what (d) was opened to check. Publishing the stronger word would have been the accepting-
direction error's mirror image — an over-claim in the alarming direction.

###### [4] ⛔⛔⛔ THE DECIDING INVARIANT `.46` SHIPPED IS FALSE OF THIS GRAMMAR, AND IT IS PUBLISHED IN SEVEN PLACES

`.46` published, unqualified and starred: *"gating a rule out of a profile must only ever REMOVE
strings from the language, never ADD them."* Measured on the real grammar:

| input | unspecified (NO gate) | `verilog_2005` (gated) |
|---|---|---|
| `module m; reg class; endmodule` | **reject** | ⛔ **ACCEPT** |

Applying the `verilog_2005` gate **ADDED** that string. That is not a defect — it is the SELECTION
idiom, and (c)'s whole correction was to leave SELECTION alone — but **the invariant that justifies
the repair is contradicted by the idiom the repair was corrected to skip**, and it was stated as a
universal in the lint message, two doc comments, this leaf and **two book pages** (the director's
review surface), each time within a page of the SELECTION table that violates it.

⭐⭐ **THE INVARIANT THE ENGINE ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTS, and the one that survives this audit:**
**gating may remove a PRODUCTION; it may never DELETE a CONSTRAINT.** A negative lookahead derives
nothing, so emptying its body deletes a constraint — the inversion. Swapping a live alternative for a
per-dialect sibling replaces a production — intended, and two dialects' languages are incomparable by
construction. Corrected in all seven locations in this commit.

###### ⭐⭐ THE FIX FOR THE GREEN CONTROL IS THE INTENDED REMEDY, NOT THE CHEAPEST ONE

The cheapest remedy for `the_same_shape_with_the_gate_removed_is_silent` was to relax it to *"1
finding"*. That would have retired the **only arm proving the detector keys on the gate rather than
on the presence of a lookahead** — `-0085`'s own lesson (4), *when a guard fires and you find
yourself explaining why the guard is wrong, check whether you took its cheapest remedy instead of its
intended one*. The intended remedy is to spell gate-free as gate-free: the fixture's
`gated_profiles` became `Option<&str>` and the control passes `None`. The `[wide, narrow]` case it
vacated is now pinned on purpose by a **new** arm,
`a_gate_admitting_every_declared_profile_still_fires_under_the_undeclared_sentinel` — because a set
built from positive declarations cannot name its own complement
([[feedback_ask_the_instrument_the_question_its_founding_case_cannot_answer]]).

###### [6] THE BEHAVIOURAL MATRIX — every input, every profile state, on the REAL grammar

| input | unspec | v2005 | sv_2017 | sv_2023 | undecl |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reg foo;` (control) | accept | accept | accept | accept | ⛔ reject |
| bare `module m; endmodule` (control) | accept | accept | accept | accept | ⛔ reject |
| `$display(1);` (control) | accept | accept | accept | accept | ⛔ reject |
| `assign x = \foo ;` (control) | accept | accept | accept | accept | ⛔ reject |
| `assign x = p::b;` (NARROWING) | accept | **reject** | accept | accept | reject |
| `assign x = \foo ::b;` (NARROWING) | accept | **reject** | accept | accept | reject |
| `$unit::f();` (NARROWING) | accept | **reject** | accept | accept | reject |
| `C::T x;` (POSITIVE, dead path) | accept | **reject** | accept | accept | reject |
| `reg class;` (SELECTION) | ⭐ **reject** | ⭐ **accept** | reject | reject | reject |
| `reg macromodule;` (mirror) | reject | reject | reject | reject | reject |

⭐ **UNDER AN UNDECLARED PROFILE EVEN THE MINIMAL LEGAL MODULE REJECTS.** The four sentinel-profile
notes are therefore **statically real and behaviourally inert**: the guard they describe is enforced,
on a profile that accepts no module. Kept in the report rather than dropped — a note is cheaper than
the census a future reader would otherwise redo. ⚠️ Measured as stated: `module m; endmodule` and
`reg foo;` both reject, the empty input accepts. That is **not** a proof the language is `{ε}` and
is not claimed as one.

- ⚖️ **THE DESIGN ITSELF, RECORDED SO THE 2.5–5× IS NOT LOST — AND IT IS ROUTED, NOT ORPHANED.**
  **L1-LA (layout-aware level-1 admission)**: at a rule-top-level Or site, compute
  `p' = skip_layout(pos)` **once**, then admit each branch on `input[p']` against its FIRST-byte set
  (C1 lane: walk the bounded prefix trie from `p'`). Soundness rests on one identity — every branch's
  first atom would itself have performed the same skip from the same `pos`, and the skip is a pure
  function of `(input, pos)` — so `p'` is the position each branch's first terminal would have begun
  matching at. **Four obligations, each a blocker until discharged:**
  1. **Skip uniformity.** The identity fails for the two `REGEX_ATOM_NO_SKIP_RULES`
     (`string_content_double` / `string_content_single`), for a regex-token first atom under a
     regex-token-sensitive facet, and for a branch opening with a zero-width lookahead that inspects
     `pos` itself. ⇒ a per-branch predicate mirroring codegen's own `skip_leading_whitespace`
     decision, exactly as today's gates mirror the layout facet.
  2. **Furthest-position parity (R1).** The hoist moves *where* a refuted branch's counterfactual
     attempt would have written `furthest_position`. The C1 lane already carries the machinery
     (`with_emulation = 138` under the layout-aware facet) — this is where the design's residual risk
     lives, and it is an emission obligation, not an analysis one.
  3. **The skip must be paid ONCE.** If `p'` is not threaded into the admitted branch, the hoist ADDS
     a skip to the accept path — which this project's peak-speed non-negotiable **rejects rather than
     trades**. (`trivia` at 99.8 % memo hits is evidence the skip is cheap; it is not evidence it is
     free.)
  4. **P2 is out, C1 is in.** 12 105 first-byte overlaps say a whole-site byte-switch is
     unreachable on this grammar; per-branch admission is the only lane with a measured surface.
  ⇒ **ROUTED as new leaf `.58`** (emission + measurement), priced at 2.5–5×, and explicitly **not**
  on `(d)`'s critical path.
- ⚖️⚖️ **RULING — THE LEAF'S OWN ORDERING IS BACKWARDS, AND I AM CORRECTING IT RATHER THAN EXECUTING
  IT.** `(b)` step 2 directed step 3 to design the layout-aware dispatch and routed the zero-memo-hit

- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS, all five named rather than left for a reader to find.** (i) One input SHAPE
  (nested parentheses) per family, one host; a different over-ceiling shape may concentrate
  elsewhere. (ii) Bounds 2 and 3 attribute over `direct_refs` of top-level Or branches **only** — an

#### ⚖️⚖️⚖️ `.44` (d) — **THIRD RULING, FORCED BY A DIRECTOR RE-VERIFICATION CHALLENGE: MY OWN BAR IS DEGENERATE, AND VHDL PASSES IT AT 1.0× BECAUSE ITS *ACCEPT* PATH COSTS 18.6 s. THE ANCHOR GETS A SECOND LEG** (2026-08-28, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0108`)

⭐⭐⭐ **THE CHALLENGE (*"do you stand by your findings?"*) DID NOT MOVE A SINGLE STATIC NUMBER — AND
IT BROKE THE RULING.** Every census in `-0105`, `-0106` and `-0107` re-derives bit-exact. What did
not survive is the one family of numbers I never measured carefully: the RATIOS, and with them the
ruling built on them.

- ⛔⛔ **RETRACTED — THE PUBLISHED RATIOS AND CLIFF DEPTHS, IN BOTH RELEASED FAMILIES.** The accept
  anchor was taken from the deepest rung of a hand-written LADDER and timed ONCE. Bisected and
  timed min-of-five:

  | family | published cliff | **true cliff** | published ratio | **re-derived** |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | systemverilog | 318 (`-0104`) / 320 (`-0105`) | **322** | 82× / 81.1–86.3× | **67–90×** (four anchored runs: 67.0, 70.4, 80.6, 89.5) |
  | vhdl | 310 (`-0104`) / 400 (`-0105`) | **681** | 267× / 198.7–203.7× | **≈1.0× — it PASSES** |

  ⛔ **A ladder reports the deepest depth it happened to TRY.** VHDL's ladder stopped at 400; the
  parser accepts to 681. ⛔ And the SystemVerilog spread is not a measurement — a sub-second anchor
  moves ±30 % between sessions, so **anything more precise than *two orders of magnitude* is noise**,
  and I published three-significant-figure ranges twice.
  ⛔ **My own mid-challenge correction was ALSO wrong**, and it is the cleanest illustration: a first
  re-bisection reported VHDL's cliff at **499** because its search window's upper bound was 500 —
  which ACCEPTS. **A bisection that never verifies its upper bound REJECTS converges to `hi−1` and
  reports it as the answer.** Caught only because a second bisection with a wider window disagreed.
- ⛔ **ALSO RETRACTED: the caveat I attached to those ratios.** `-0105` said *"a ladder brackets the
  accept anchor from BELOW, so every ratio is an UPPER bound — a RED row cannot be a ladder
  artefact."* False. The ladder term and the anchor-noise term point in OPPOSITE directions and the
  noise term is larger. ⭐ A caveat is a claim, and this one was reasoned rather than measured.
- ⛔⛔⛔ **AND THE FINDING THE RETRACTION UNCOVERED, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE RATIO: VHDL'S *ACCEPT*
  PATH PLATEAUS TOO.** Min-of-three, plain FUSED runs, on **accepted** input:

  | family | 300 | 500 | 575 | 600 | 625 | 650 | 675 | 681 (deepest accepted) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | **vhdl** | 0.076 s | 0.131 s | 0.182 s | **0.931 s** | **4.516 s** | **10.277 s** | **17.034 s** | **18.557 s** |
  | systemverilog | 0.122 s | — | — | — | — | — | — | 0.182 s (at its cliff, 322) |

  **A 102× rise between depth 575 and depth 681 on input the parser ACCEPTS.** SystemVerilog is flat
  (0.040 s at 150 → 0.182 s at 322) and has no such shoulder.
- ⚖️ **CONSEQUENCE — THE BAR AS I RULED IT IS SATISFIABLE BY MAKING SUCCESS WORSE, AND VHDL IS THE
  COUNTEREXAMPLE.** *"A rejection may cost no more than 2× the parser's deepest ACCEPTED parse"* has
  the right principle behind it and the wrong anchor: the deepest accepted parse is itself allowed to
  be pathological, and in VHDL it is. Reject 18.735 s ÷ accept 18.977 s = **1.0×, PASS** — from a
  parser that needs nineteen seconds either way on 1.4 KB of input. **A bar that a catastrophic
  parser passes is worth exactly as much as a bar every parser passes**, which is the test `-0104`
  applied to itself and got right on the first ruling.
- ⚖️⚖️ **THE RULING — THE ANCHOR GETS A SECOND LEG, AND BOTH MUST HOLD.**
  1. **RATIO LEG (unchanged in principle, repaired in its anchor):** an over-ceiling rejection may
     cost no more than **2×** the same parser's accepted parse **of the same input shape at the
     deepest depth whose accept cost is still within 2× of a shallow reference accept** — i.e. the
     anchor must come from the parser's *healthy* accept régime, not from its deepest one.
  2. **ACCEPT-PLATEAU LEG (new):** the accept path itself must not exhibit a plateau — **no accepted
     depth may cost more than 2× the accepted depth at 80 % of the cliff.** VHDL reads
     18.557 / 0.182 = **102× and is RED**; SystemVerilog reads 0.182 / 0.128 = **1.4× and is GREEN**.
  ⭐ Leg 2 is what makes leg 1 non-degenerate, and it is derived from the parser exactly as the
  original ratio was — no external authority, no wall-clock constant.
- ⛔ **RE-SCORED UNDER THE REPAIRED BAR**: SystemVerilog **RED on leg 1** (67–90× across four anchored runs), GREEN on leg 2.
  VHDL **GREEN on leg 1** (1.0×) and **RED on leg 2** (102×). ⇒ **both released families are still
  RED**, which was the first ruling's own test of whether a bar is worth having — and they are red
  for *different reasons*, which the single-leg bar could not express.
- ⇒ **`.44` still closes only when both families are GREEN ON BOTH LEGS.** The VHDL accept-path
  plateau is a distinct defect with a distinct owner: **new leaf `.60`**, ROUTED (VHDL is outside the
  SV lane) and parked.
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS**: (i) one input shape per family, one host; (ii) leg 2's *80 % of the cliff*
  reference point is a choice, not a derivation — it is far enough below the cliff to be in the
  healthy régime on both families measured, and it should be re-examined the first time a family
  disagrees; (iii) the SystemVerilog leg-1 figure is deliberately quoted as a RANGE over four anchored runs
  (67.0 / 70.4 / 80.6 / 89.5), because this measurement method does not support more — the accept

  failures be retained?"* — they demonstrably can be, at 87–91× — but **"can a recursion-tainted
  failure be filed in a channel keyed by what it actually depends on?"** ⛔ NOT ESTABLISHED and not
  guessed at here: whether such a key exists, and what share of the 87–91× survives keying it.
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS.** (i) The probe disabled BOTH failure gates at once, so the 87–91× is the
  ceiling for disabling both and **the split between them is unmeasured** — a value-taking flag would
  separate them and costs another 20-minute build. (ii) One input shape, one family, one host.
  (iii) The correctness damage is characterised only on this shape: two depths were seen to flip, and
  no corpus run was made under arm B. (iv) The `126.1×` entries against `87–89×` time on the same
  graph says the entry-share model **over-predicts by ≈1.43×**, which is used in the re-verification
  below to adjust `-0105`'s elision ceilings — and it is one measurement of one intervention, not a
  law.

### ⚠️ `.58` — **L1-LA: THE LAYOUT-AWARE LEVEL-1 ADMISSION EMISSION. DESIGNED AND PRICED AT 2.5–5× BY `.44`(b) STEP 3, AND DELIBERATELY *NOT* ON `(d)`'s CRITICAL PATH** (`todo`, opened 2026-08-27 by `.44`(b) step 3 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0105`, ROUTED + PARKED **behind `.56`**)

> ⭐ **THIS LEAF EXISTS SO A MEASURED 2.5–5× IS NOT LOST BECAUSE IT WAS NOT THE 41×.** `.44`(b)
> step 3 designed the layout-aware dispatch, measured its ceiling, and ruled it insufficient for
> `(d)`'s bar. Insufficient is not worthless: it is the largest single elision win this grammar has
> ever been shown to have, and it is engine-universal.

- **WHAT IT IS.** At a rule-top-level `Or` site, compute `p' = skip_layout(pos)` **once**, then admit
  each branch on `input[p']` against its FIRST-byte set — the C1 bounded-trie lane walking from `p'`.
  Today every one of the four elision gates refuses SystemVerilog for one reason, `terminals skip
  leading layout (R2 raw-byte peek unsound)`, because the emission it models peeks the raw byte at
  `pos`. Hoisting the skip restores the identity the peek needs.
- **WHY IT IS SOUND.** Every branch's first atom would itself have performed the same skip from the
  same `pos`, and the skip is a pure function of `(input, pos)` ⇒ `p'` is the position each branch's
  first terminal would have begun matching at.
- ⛔ **THE FOUR OBLIGATIONS, each a blocker until discharged** (from `.44`(b) step 3):
  1. **Skip uniformity** — the identity fails for `REGEX_ATOM_NO_SKIP_RULES`
     (`string_content_double` / `string_content_single`), for a regex-token first atom under a
     regex-token-sensitive facet, and for a branch opening with a zero-width lookahead that inspects
     `pos`. Needs a per-branch predicate mirroring codegen's own `skip_leading_whitespace` decision.
  2. **Furthest-position parity (R1)** — the hoist moves *where* a refuted branch's counterfactual
     attempt would have written `furthest_position`. The C1 lane carries the machinery
     (`with_emulation = 138`); this is the residual risk and it is an EMISSION obligation.
  3. **The skip must be paid ONCE** — if `p'` is not threaded into the admitted branch the hoist ADDS
     a skip to the ACCEPT path, which the peak-speed non-negotiable rejects rather than trades.
  4. **P2 is out, C1 is in** — `12 105 first-byte overlap between branches` says a whole-site
     byte-switch is unreachable on this grammar; only per-branch admission has a measured surface.
- **THE MEASURED SURFACE IT WOULD UNLOCK** (`…-0105`, `logs/layout_aware_dispatch_census.txt`):
  `FIRSTK` **0 → 1 906** of 1 934 top-level branches, `PREFIX2` **0 → 249** of 535 sites,
  `QUANT-SITE` **0 → 317** of 1 157; `PREFIX2-EXPOSURE` **0 → 29.5 %** of the depth-800 workload.
- ⛔ **THE PRICE, AND WHY IT IS PARKED**: bounds 2/3 cap a perfect L1-LA at **2.54×–5.05×**. `(d)`'s
  exit needs **41×**. `.56` owns the term that can supply it. ⇒ **land `.56` first, then this**, and
  re-price L1-LA against whatever plateau `.56` leaves — a 5× on a smaller number is a different
  proposition from a 5× on 12.4 s.
- **ACCEPTANCE**: the four obligations discharged with evidence; a before→after on the depth-800
  reject AND on the shipped corpus parse cost (the accept path must not regress by a single
  measurable step — obligation 3 is the one that can silently break it); the four gates re-censused
  on the TRACKED grammar reporting the same numbers the facet-flip hypothetical predicted, which is
  the check that the emission matches the analysis rather than merely being fast.


### ⚠️ `.59` — **THE MEMO TRACE SAYS *"at position N"* ON TEN LINES AND MEANS TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES: SIX PRINT THE MEMO KEY, FOUR PRINT WHERE THE BODY ENDED** (`todo`, opened 2026-08-27 by `.56`(a) / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0106`, ROUTED)

> ⭐ **THIS LEAF EXISTS BECAUSE THE DEFECT ALMOST PRODUCED A PUBLISHED FINDING.** `.56`(a) joined
> *"Memo miss for rule R at position P"* against *"Memoized successful result for rule R at position
> Q"* and got two 350-element position sets with **zero overlap** — a striking structural claim that
> is pure instrument artefact. It was caught only because the disjointness was too clean to believe.

- ✅ **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE), over a CLOSED population — all ten `💾` trace lines in
  `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs`, not a sample.** Every one formats
  `self.position`, and the memo KEY is `(rule_id, position-at-entry)`, bound as `key` before the body
  runs. The split is by WHEN the line executes:

  | line | event | prints |
  |---:|---|---|
  | `:9681` | hit — cached failure | ✅ the key |
  | `:9705` | hit — cached tainted failure | ✅ the key |
  | `:9716` | evicting stale tainted failure | ✅ the key |
  | `:9735` | evicting stale tainted success | ✅ the key |
  | **`:9744`** | **hit — reusing cached result** | ⛔ the **END** position — `self.position = entry.end_pos;` runs on the line above |
  | `:9804` | hit — cached depth-gated failure | ✅ the key |
  | `:9817` | miss — computing fresh result | ✅ the key |
  | **`:9994`** | **memoized successful result** | ⛔ post-body `self.position` |
  | **`:10003`** | **memoized TAINTED failed result** | ⛔ post-body `self.position` |
  | **`:10010`** | **memoized failed result** | ⛔ post-body `self.position` |

  ⇒ **six of ten name the key, four name something else, and all ten use the identical phrase.**
- ⛔ **WHY IT IS WORTH A LEAF RATHER THAN A COMMENT.** The trace is the instrument `TOOLBOX.md`
  points a reader at for exactly this class of question, and the natural analysis — *"which keys get
  stored, and are they the keys we keep missing?"* — is the one the wording defeats. The failure is
  silent and in the confident direction: both position sets are well-formed, both are the right size,
  and the join produces a clean answer that is wrong. ⭐ Note the success HIT line is on the wrong
  side too, which makes the trap worse: a reader comparing hits against misses is comparing an END
  position against a key.
- **THE FIX, and it is small**: print `key.1` on the four offending lines, or word them so the two
  positions are distinguishable (`"… keyed at K (body ended at E)"`). ⛔ **It is a CODEGEN change**,
  so it regenerates all 11 parsers and lands under the usual regeneration discipline — priced here,
  not taken in the diagnostic slice that found it.
- **ACCEPTANCE**: every memo trace line either names the memo KEY or names both positions
  distinguishably; `.56`(a)'s arm C reproduces its event counts unchanged (those counts never
  depended on the position field, which is why the finding it supports survives this defect); and the
  store and probe position sets, joined, agree on the keys they share.
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUND**: this is the PROTOCOL graph's `memoized_call`. The fused graph's thin memo
  emits no `💾` lines at all, so it is outside this population — and that absence is its own
  observability gap, already named in `.56`.

### ⛔⛔ `.61` — **THE RECURSION CEILING IS AN *ACCURACY* DEFECT BEFORE IT IS A SPEED ONE: BOTH RELEASED PARSERS REJECT SYNTACTICALLY WELL-FORMED INPUT, AND THE DIAGNOSTIC NAMES THE WRONG CAUSE — ZERO OF THE FIVE WORDS A CONSUMER WOULD LOOK FOR APPEAR IN IT** (`todo`, opened 2026-08-28 by the DIRECTOR'S ACCURACY-BEFORE-SPEED ORDERING / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0109`; ✅✅ **(a) DONE 2026-08-28 `…-0110` — the shipped over-ceiling rejection now NAMES the ceiling on both released families, `0 of 5` → **5 of 5** on this leaf's own term census, with the accept boundary measured UNMOVED (SV 322/323, VHDL 681/682) and the label pinned by a RED-capable control that refuses to fire on an ordinary syntax error; embedding API `1.3.3`. ⭐ The obvious signal was DISPROVED in-slice: depth 322 ACCEPTS while recording 847 ceiling refusals, so `events != 0` is not a discriminator and the wording is conditional by design**; ⛔⛔ **(b) RULING WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28 `…-0112` BY THE DIRECTOR'S POPULATION RULING — the MEASUREMENTS stand, the CONCLUSION does not; re-adjudication owned by `.63`. What it had measured: ZERO of **30 056** real files across BOTH released families contact the ceiling, on the ACCEPT path as well as the reject path, and an independent no-parser oracle puts the deepest real nesting at **22** against a worst-shape capacity of **249** (a 3.3× range across ten shapes, so `.61`'s own `322` was not the binding number). The residual under-acceptance is REAL and stays open — no measured consumer meets it**; ⇒ **(c) SPEED IS NOW UNBLOCKED**: `.56`(d) + `.58`)

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THIS LEAF EXISTS BECAUSE A STEERING CALL RE-READ A MEASUREMENT I ALREADY HAD.** The director's
> ordering — *"right now we need to focus on accuracy and precision, speed will come next"* — was made
> about VHDL's 18.6 s parse. Applied to the whole `.44`/`.56` lane it says something sharper: that lane
> has spent nine slices on how EXPENSIVE an over-ceiling rejection is, and never once on the fact that
> **the rejection is WRONG and its message is MISLEADING**. Both halves were measured on the way to the
> speed numbers and neither had an owner.

- ⛔ **HALF ONE — UNDER-ACCEPTANCE, measured, 3 runs per depth, verdicts deterministic.** Neither
  IEEE 1800 nor IEEE 1076 bounds expression nesting depth, so both inputs below are well-formed:

  | family | deepest ACCEPTED | first REJECTED | the rejected input |
  |---|---:|---:|---|
  | systemverilog | **322** (0.140 s) | **323** | `module m; assign x = (((…1…))); endmodule` |
  | vhdl | **681** (18.641 s, AST 224 913 B) | **682** | `… architecture a of e is begin s <= (((…1…))); end architecture;` |

  ⭐ The accepts are confirmed by a SECOND instrument, not by an exit code: `--parse-dump-ast`
  produces a real AST at depth 675 (222 939 B) and 681 (224 913 B) and fails at 682. ⇒ these are
  genuine parses, and the boundary is genuine.
  ⛔ **This project calls over-acceptance a defect. Under-acceptance is the same defect in the
  direction that breaks a user's working file** — and it is a REJECTION of conforming source, which
  is the strongest failure class a parser has.
- ⛔⛔ **HALF TWO — AND THE DIAGNOSTIC NAMES THE WRONG CAUSE, WHICH IS THE PRECISION HALF.** The
  shipped rejection is indistinguishable from an ordinary syntax error:
  ```
  systemverilog: Parser did not consume full input at position 0   [furthest_position=668, …]
  vhdl:          Parser did not consume full input at position 24  [furthest_position=741, …]
  ```
  ⭐ **CENSUSED, not asserted**: grepping each shipped diagnostic for `depth|ceiling|limit|nest|recursion`
  returns **0 of 5 terms on both families**. ⇒ a consumer is told *"your file has a syntax error near
  the start"* about a file that is **syntactically correct**, and the only true statement available —
  *"this input exceeds the parser's nesting capacity"* — appears nowhere in it.
  ⚠️ The information EXISTS but only behind a diagnostic env var: `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` reports
  `depth-ceiling rejections` on its headline. **That is a debugging surface, not the error an embedder
  receives.**
- ⛔ **WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE PLATEAU, stated plainly.** A slow rejection costs an embedder seconds. A
  WRONG rejection costs them a working design file and sends them hunting a syntax error that does not
  exist — and the message actively points them at the wrong place (`position 0`, `position 24`), which
  is the start of the construct rather than the depth at which the parser gave up.
- **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES**, in the director's order:
  (a) **PRECISION FIRST, because it is cheap and it is a pure win**: the over-ceiling rejection must
      SAY SO — a distinct, labelled diagnostic naming the nesting capacity and the depth reached. The
      engine already counts both (`recursion_depth_block_events`, the guard's own depth), so this is a
      surfacing change, not a new measurement. It does not move the accept set and cannot regress the
      accept path.
  (b) **ACCURACY SECOND**: decide, with evidence, whether the ceiling's LOCATION is defensible — 322
      for SystemVerilog is roughly 4096 frames ÷ ~12.7 frames per nesting level, and whether a
      conforming consumer meets it in practice is a corpus question this leaf must answer rather than
      assume.
  (c) **SPEED LAST** — `.56`(d) and `.58`, explicitly parked behind (a) and (b) by the director's
      ordering, with the measurements already banked (`.56`(c): retention is worth 87–91×).
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS**: (i) one input shape per family; a different construct may hit the ceiling at a
  different depth, and the leaf must not quote 322/681 as the parser's capacity in general — they are
  this shape's capacity; (ii) "syntactically well-formed" is a claim about the LRMs' *grammar*, not
  about semantic validity — `s` and `x` are undeclared, which a parser is right to accept and an
  elaborator is right to reject; (iii) the 0-of-5 term census covers the message these two invocations
  print, not every error path in the engine.

#### ✅ `.61`(a) DONE 2026-08-28 (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0110`) — THE OVER-CEILING REJECTION NOW NAMES THE CEILING, ON EVERY FAMILY, IN THE ERROR AN EMBEDDER ACTUALLY RECEIVES. **0 of 5 → 5 of 5** ON THE LEAF'S OWN CENSUS

- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — reproduced on the SHIPPED release binary before touching anything,
  with `--parser-fingerprint` asserting the binary embeds the parser on disk
  (`systemverilog 240da0a4…` = `shasum` of `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs`). Depth 322
  ACCEPTS; depth 323 rejects as
  `Parser did not consume full input at position 0 [furthest_position=668, …]`, and depth 350 the
  same at 722. `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS=1` on the SAME inputs reports **847** (322, accepted) and
  **1 013** (323, rejected) `depth-ceiling rejections`.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — tool signature, from the shipped rejection itself:
  `Parser did not consume full input at position 0 [furthest_position=668, +668 bytes deeper
  than surface position]` on `sv_323.sv`, cross-read with `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS=1`'s
  `1013 depth-ceiling rejections` on the SAME input, and the accept confirmed by
  `--parse-dump-ast`. ⭐ **That pair IS the diagnosis**: `furthest_position=668` says the parse
  reached the END of the parenthesis run while the message it prints names position **0**, so
  the reported locus is the start of the construct and the real one is 668 bytes deeper.
  **WHY**: the ceiling refusal is a real, correctly-constructed
  `ParseError::RecursionDepthExceeded` (emitted at `ast_based_generator.rs:4299` for the protocol
  graph and `ast_based_generator/cascade.rs:657` for the fused one), but it is raised inside a
  failing ALTERNATIVE and is therefore backtracked away exactly like an ordinary rejection. The
  parse then unwinds to the top with a partial derivation and unconsumed input, and the only site
  that composes a top-level verdict — `parse_full` / `parse_full_from` — had one unconditional
  arm: `InvalidSyntax { message: "Parser did not consume full input", position: self.position }`.
  ⇒ **the information was not missing, it was DISCARDED one frame below the surface.**
  **WHERE**: `ast_based_generator.rs` `generate_parse_method`, the `parse_full` and
  `parse_full_from` failure arms (pre-change `:2604` / `:2629`). Both are engine-universal —
  every one of the eleven generated artifacts routes its top-level verdict through them — which
  is why the fix is one codegen site and not a per-family patch.
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE OBVIOUS SIGNAL IS NOT A SOUND ONE — measured, and it changed the design.** The
  first instinct is "label the rejection whenever `recursion_depth_block_events != 0`". That is
  **wrong**, and the disproof was one command: **depth 322 ACCEPTS and still records 847 ceiling
  refusals.** The counter is not a discriminator; it counts contact on abandoned branches too. ⇒
  the label is scoped to the FAILURE path (where an accept can never reach it) and its wording is
  **conditional** — *"if the input is syntactically valid it exceeds this parser's nesting
  capacity"* — rather than an assertion that the ceiling caused the rejection. **A label that
  over-claimed would have traded a diagnostic that names the wrong cause for one that names a
  wrong cause more often**, which is the same defect this leaf exists to close, pointed the other
  way.
- [x] **FIX** — ENGINE tier, **ZERO grammar bytes**, three source files plus codegen:
  - a new `ParseError::RecursionCeilingContacted { surface, position, ceiling, events }`
    (`ast_pipeline/mod.rs`). It **WRAPS**: `surface` is the diagnostic the parse would otherwise
    have reported, rendered first and unchanged, so the reported position is byte-identical and
    anything already parsing `at position N` or the `furthest_position` suffix keeps working.
  - `label_recursion_ceiling_contact`, emitted once per parser beside
    `discharge_final_phase_obligations`, called from **both** `parse_full` and `parse_full_from`
    on their failure arms only.
  - the reading is a **per-parse DELTA** (`events_at_entry` snapshotted before `self.parse()`),
    because `prepare_parse_state` deliberately does not reset `recursion_depth_block_events` —
    without the delta an embedder reusing one parser would see the first over-ceiling input label
    every subsequent rejection.
  - the ceiling constant is interpolated from `GENERATED_RECURSION_GUARD_MAX_DEPTH`, the SAME
    constant the guard's own `depth >= …` test uses, so the number reported and the number that
    produced it cannot drift apart.
  - the two exhaustive `match`es over `ParseError` extended (`embedding_api::parse_error_position`
    — which returns the WRAPPED position, so an embedder's reported location does not move; and
    `bin/ebnf_dual_run_diff::parse_error_fields`, which carries the contact counts rather than
    hiding them).
- ⭐⭐ **THE WORDING IS MEASURED, NOT STYLED — and the first draft failed its own test.** `.61`
  censused the old message for the five terms a consumer would search (`depth`, `ceiling`,
  `limit`, `nest`, `recursion`) and found **0 of 5**. My first draft scored **4 of 5**: it said
  *"nesting capacity"* where a reader would look for *"limit"*. Re-worded to carry all five, and
  to state that **the number counts PARSER FRAMES, not source nesting levels** — a reader who
  takes 4096 for 4096 levels of source nesting concludes their file is nowhere near the limit
  when it is well over it (SV rejects at 323 parens ≈ 4096 ÷ ~12.7 frames/level).

  would be the more legible design and is what a machine-readable distinction wants. It is
  **not backward-compatible**: every embedder arm that branches on `E_PARSE_FAILURE` today would
  silently stop matching over-ceiling input — a regression handed to consumers in exchange for
  legibility. The code set therefore stays stable, and the structured distinction is carried by
  the typed variant (`ceiling` and `events` as fields) for embedders who want it without string
  matching. Locked by an assertion in the new test.

#### ✅ `.61`(b) DONE 2026-08-28 (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0111`) — **RULING: THE CEILING'S LOCATION IS DEFENSIBLE. DO NOT MOVE IT.** ZERO of **30 056** real-world files across BOTH released families contact it — on the ACCEPT path as well as the reject path

- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — (b) is an ADJUDICATION, so the question is what the evidence
  says, not where a bug is. The instruments: `--parse … --profile sv_2017` under
  `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` for the guard's own refusal counter, `--parse-dump-ast` and
  `furthest_position=` for the boundary bisections, and a source-level nesting oracle that uses no
  parser at all. **WHERE the ceiling lives**: `GENERATED_RECURSION_GUARD_MAX_DEPTH = 4096`
  (`ast_based_generator.rs:31`), read by the protocol guard (`:4281`) and mirrored one-for-one in
  the fused cascade guard (`ast_based_generator/cascade.rs:648`).
- ⛔⛔ **FIRST, A MEASUREMENT THAT CORRECTS `.61`'s OWN FRAMING.** `.61` quoted **322** and its
  honest bound (i) warned it was one shape's capacity. Bisecting **ten** SystemVerilog construct
  shapes shows how far that varies — and 322 is **not** the binding number:

  | shape | deepest ACCEPTED | first REJECTED | frames/level | ceiling-labelled |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---|
  | `cast_paren` — `int'(int'(…))` | **249** | 250 | **16.4** | yes |
  | `ternary` — `a ? b : (…)` | 272 | 273 | 15.1 | yes |
  | `concat` — `{{{…}}}` | 314 | 315 | 13.0 | yes |
  | `paren_expr` — `(((…)))` (`.61`'s shape) | 322 | 323 | 12.7 | yes |
  | `call` — `f(f(f(…)))` | 340 | 341 | 12.0 | yes |
  | `generate_if` | 583 | 584 | 7.0 | yes |
  | `if_nest` | 815 | 816 | 5.0 | yes |
  | `begin_end` | 816 | 817 | 5.0 | yes |
  | `index_sel` — `y[0][0]…` | **> 8192, no cliff** | — | — | iterative, not recursive |
  | `unary_not` — `!!1` | 1 | 2 | — | **NO — different cause** |

  ⇒ **the parser's capacity is a 3.3× RANGE (249–816), not a number**, and the honest bound is the
  WORST shape: **249**. ⭐ Two rows are their own findings. `index_sel` has **no cliff at all** —
  postfix selection is iterative, so it costs no frames per level. And `unary_not` rejects at depth
  2 **without the ceiling label**, which is the control working on a real construct: it is not a
  capacity failure. ⛔ **And that rejection is CORRECT, checked against the in-repo LRM rather than
  inferred** — IEEE 1800-2017 A.8.3 reads `expression ::= primary | unary_operator {
  attribute_instance } primary | …`, so `!` takes a **primary**; `!1` is an *expression*, not a
  primary, so `!!1` is **not derivable** while `!(!1)` is. Rejecting it is LRM fidelity.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT — CEILING CONTACT OVER BOTH RELEASED CORPORA, EVERY FILE, BOTH
  PATHS.** `.61`(a)'s label answers only half the question: it is composed on the FAILURE path, so
  "0 of 16 336 rejections labelled" does not bound contact on ACCEPTS — depth 322 accepts while
  recording 847 refusals. The guard's own counter does bound it:

  | family | files | ACCEPT | REJECT | **files contacting the ceiling** | max refusals seen |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | systemverilog (`--profile sv_2017`) | 16 336 | 9 794 | 6 542 | **0** | **0** |
  | vhdl | 13 720 | 4 369 | 9 351 | **0** | **0** |
  | **total** | **30 056** | 14 163 | 15 893 | **0** | **0** |

  ⇒ **not one refusal, on either path, in either family, across fourteen upstream projects**
  (OpenTitan, Verilator, iverilog, Surelog, slang, verible, sv2v, black-parrot, VeeR, ibex, GHDL,
  VESTS, UVVM, …).
- ⭐ **AND AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE AGREES — one that uses no parser**, so it cannot inherit the
  parser's blind spots: a lexical scan of `()[]{}` depth over the same corpora, strings and
  comments skipped. SystemVerilog **max 22**, p99.9 **8**, median 2. VHDL **max 16**, p99.9 **6**.
  ⇒ against the worst measured shape (249) the margin on the deepest REAL file is **11.3×**, and
  on the 99.9th percentile **31×**.
- ⛔ **THE ORACLE'S FIRST FORM WAS WRONG AND WAS REFUTED BEFORE IT WAS PUBLISHED.** Bracket depth
  misses the three shapes that nest through KEYWORDS (`begin_end`, `if_nest`, `generate_if`), so a
  keyword-block counter was written — and it reported **1 427** on a UVM package, which would have
  been an alarming number. It is an artifact: whole-token counts on that file read `function`
  **4 316** against `endfunction` **3 225**, `class` 580 against `endclass` 378, because
  **prototypes** (`extern`/`pure virtual`/`import "DPI-C"`) and **forward typedefs**
  (`typedef class foo;`) open nothing. A correct keyword-nesting oracle needs real parsing, which
  defeats its purpose as an independent instrument — so the keyword axis is answered by the guard's
  own counter above (which covers every shape by construction), and the bracket oracle is reported
  only for what it soundly measures.
- ⭐ **A NATURAL FALSE-POSITIVE CONTROL, found in the corpus rather than synthesised.**

  location; do not move it.** The constant's own comment (`ast_based_generator.rs:29-30`) says it

  only that **no measured consumer meets it** — not that it is correct.
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS**: (i) ten shapes, not an exhaustive enumeration of SV constructs; the
  observed frames/level range is 5.0–16.4, and a hypothetical 40 frames/level shape would still
  cliff near 102, itself 4.6× above the deepest real file; (ii) both corpora are human- and
  tool-written open-source RTL — **bulk machine-generated RTL is not represented**, and `.60`

  `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS`, which `.56`(b) proved routes the parse onto the PROTOCOL graph — so it

  (iv) the SV arm is `--profile sv_2017`, not the unnamed profile, whose separate defect is `.62`.

### ⛔⛔ `.62` — **SYSTEMVERILOG DECLARES NO `@default_profile`, SO AN UNNAMED PROFILE PARSES THE *UNION* OF EVERY DIALECT: IT ACCEPTS 28 REAL CORPUS FILES `sv_2017` REJECTS, AND ON ONE OF THEM IT DOES NOT TERMINATE IN 181 s WHERE `sv_2017` ANSWERS IN 0.2 s** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED behind `.61`(b), opened 2026-08-28 by `.61`(a)'s own no-regression census / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0110`)

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THIS LEAF EXISTS BECAUSE A REGRESSION CENSUS DISAGREED WITH ITS BASELINE AND I DID NOT
> EXPLAIN THE DISAGREEMENT AWAY.** `.61`(a)'s no-regression arm ran the full 16 336-file external
> SV corpus and compared it to the tracked characterization. It differed on **28 verdicts and 6
> timeouts**. The comfortable reading was available and wrong — *"the baseline is stale, many SV
> slices have landed since, of course it moved"*. The baseline's own instrument-identity block does
> say it no longer describes this tree. But the census also used a **different profile**, and that
> turned out to be the whole difference and a defect underneath it.

- ⛔ **THE MEASUREMENT, three ways, all deterministic on repeat.**
  1. **`grep '@default_profile' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` returns NOTHING**, and the shipped
     `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs` emits no `DEFAULT_GRAMMAR_PROFILE`. So
     `normalize_generated_grammar_profile` answers `None` for an unspecified SV profile
     (`parser_registry.rs:476`) and there is no declared default to fall back to. The parse runs
     with **no `@profiles` gating at all** — the union of `sv_2017`, `sv_2023` and `verilog_2005`,
     which is not a dialect any LRM defines.
  2. **OVER-ACCEPTANCE, 28 of 28, both directions clean.** Every one of the 28 files whose verdict
     differed from the tracked baseline **REJECTS under `--profile sv_2017` and ACCEPTS under the
     unnamed profile**. Not a sample — the whole disagreement set, re-run under both profiles.
  3. **AND IT CAN FAIL TO TERMINATE.** `stimuli/sv/subs/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv`
     (35 306 B, ordinary vendored OpenTitan RTL) answers in **0.2 s** under `--profile sv_2017`
     and produces **no result in 181 s** with no profile — reproduced at 121 s, 151 s (×2) and
     181 s, always a timeout. Three more real files accept but cost **30 s / 30 s / 73 s** under
     the unnamed profile.
- ⛔⛔ **WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A CONFIGURATION FOOTGUN.** The project's north star is that
  **SystemVerilog is 100 % LRM-compliant BY DEFAULT and over-acceptance is a defect**. The unnamed
  profile is precisely the default path, and it is over-accepting against a real corpus by a
  measured 28 files. A caller who names no dialect does not get a permissive-but-honest superset —
  they get a grammar whose accept set corresponds to no publication, at up to ~1 000× the cost.
- ⭐ **AND IT SILENTLY DEGRADES THE PROJECT'S OWN INSTRUMENTS.** `stimuli/run_external_corpus.sh`
  passes `--profile sv_2017`, so every tracked characterization number is a `sv_2017` number. Any
  ad-hoc `parseability_probe --parse systemverilog <file>` — the spelling that appears throughout
  `TOOLBOX.md` and in this tree's own repro lines — measures the union instead, and the two are
  not comparable. That is how this was found: two of my own censuses, taken the same hour on the
  same binary, disagreed.
- **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES:**
  - **(a)** SIZE IT on the corpus, not on the 28: under the unnamed profile versus `sv_2017`, how
    many of the 16 336 files change verdict, and in which direction? ⛔ Do not change the default
    before the number exists — `DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP.15`'s ruling applies (never move a gating
    behaviour over a population nobody has sized).
  - **(b)** ADJUDICATE the 28 by name against the LRMs. `sv_2017` rejecting them is only the
    *right* answer if the constructs really are non-conforming; if any is conforming, this leaf has
    found an under-acceptance in `sv_2017` instead, which is a different and larger defect.
  - **(c)** DECIDE the default. The obvious candidate is declaring `@default_profile: sv_2017` on
    the grammar, which would make the unnamed spelling mean the newest full LRM dialect and make
    the union unreachable except by asking for it. ⚠️ That is a **behaviour change on a shipped
    surface** and needs (a) first.
  - **(d)** the cost half — whether the union's non-termination is the same call-volume term
    `.44`(b) measured or a distinct one. Sequenced last, per the director's accuracy-before-speed
    ordering.
- ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS**: (i) the 28 and the timing figures come from ONE census pair on one host;
  (a) is exactly the arm that replaces them with a full sized number; (ii) *"the unnamed profile is
  the union"* is derived from the absent `@default_profile` plus the measured behaviour, not from
  reading the filter — the filter's own code path is `.47`'s subject and this leaf should re-derive
  it rather than inherit my reading; (iii) the embedding API's `parse_systemverilog_2017` /

  the `parse_grammar_profile`-with-nothing and CLI paths.
- ⛔ **NOT WORKED IN `.61`(a)**: it is not a blocker for the ceiling label (the label census was

#### ✅ `.67`(a) DONE 2026-08-28 (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0120`) — **THE RATIO IS REAL AND REPRODUCES ON A SECOND INSTRUMENT, BUT 7 950× IS THE REAL p99, NOT THE REAL MEDIAN. AND 97 % OF THE CORPUS CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION AT ALL**

Full report + raw data: [`docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67/REPORT.md`](artifacts/eus67/REPORT.md).
Producers, both tracked and re-runnable:

  conclusion does not depend on which floor is chosen.

  RATHER THAN A METHOD ARTEFACT.** This instrument re-measures `.66`/`.67`'s five published
  synthetic figures as 4 062.1 / 1 142.3 / 499.8 / 573.2 / 305.0 MB against their published
  4 064.0 / 1 143.2 / 498.8 / 572.2 / 304.6 MB — **worst disagreement 0.20 %**, on an instrument

  six shapes: `peak RSS = per-item × N + intercept`, intercepts **16.8–36.1 MB** (i.e. the process
  floor itself) and max residual **6.4 MB against an RSS of 4 GB**. ⇒ linear in item count with **no
  fixed parse component**. Per-item cost spans **14×** across shapes — 29.5 KB for a module port,
  412.3 KB for a netlist instance — so "the ratio" is a per-SHAPE constant, not a parser constant.

  1 328 188 B → 2 937 / 3 044 / 3 178 MB) fit with **marginal slope 1 513× and intercept 1 261 MB**
  (max residual 1.8 MB against 3 GB), while their *average* ratio is 2 509× — the marginal byte
  costing **40 % less** than the average byte, the opposite of every synthetic shape. ⛔ **Three
  points from three DIFFERENT files is one degree of freedom, and this instrument cannot tell a
  1 261 MB fixed PARSE cost from 1 261 MB of shared file CONTENT all three chip tops emit.** Handed
  to (b) as the question attribution must answer, because the two readings extrapolate very
  differently at netlist scale.

  `.67`'s own *"~40 000 netlist instances on a 16 GB machine"* re-derives here as **40 551**
  (14 GB ÷ 412.3 KB/instance) — **CONFIRMED**. ⇒ the ingestion bound stands and is **20×–6 000×**
  short of the 10⁵–10⁷-instance, 100 MB–10 GB target population.
- ⛔⛔ **97 % OF THE CORPUS CANNOT ANSWER THIS QUESTION, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN FUDGED.**

  non-positive values with `if x > 0`. On the body that **silently discarded 10.7 % of rows —

  A filter that removes the inconvenient tail of a distribution and says nothing is not a cleanup;
  it is the defect. `parse_rss_distribution.py` now excludes by a NAMED rule and COUNTS the
  exclusion on every run. ⇒ **a subtraction is a claim about its subtrahend: I subtracted a "floor"
  I had not shown to be a floor, and 32 rows were already telling me so.**

##### ⛔⛔⛔ `.67`(b) — **WITHDRAWAL AND QUALIFICATIONS UNDER A DIRECTOR RE-VERIFICATION CHALLENGE, SAME DAY (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0122`). THE MEASUREMENTS STAND. THE HEADLINE INFERENCE DOES NOT.**

- ⛔⛔⛔ **(1) WITHDRAWN — *"a substantial majority is provably NOT the AST arena"*, and its
  director-facing form *"the AST is not where the parse memory goes"*.** The instrument counts
  `size_of::<ParseNode>()` = 48 B per node plus the three side arenas. But
  **`ParseContent::Sequence` is `Vec<&'input ParseNode>` and `Quantified` is
  `(Vec<&'input ParseNode>, _)`** (`mod.rs:1234`/`:1244`) — **every such node owns a SEPARATE heap
  allocation of 8 bytes per child**, and `TransformedTerminal(String)` owns another. Those bytes are
  **AST-owned and outside the arena**, and the census never counted them. ⇒ the published share
  measures **NODE HEADERS, not the AST**, and the residual cannot be attributed away from the AST.
  ⭐ **The two omissions I DID declare (chunk capacity, string payloads) made me feel the bound was
  honest; the one that mattered was the one I never thought to look for** — which is why the fix is
  a declaration at the instrument itself, not in this leaf.
- ⚠️ **(2) THE PREDICTION IS NOT CLEANLY FALSIFIED — 2 of its 3 legs are, the headline one is
  UNDECIDED.** The two COUNT legs are exact and stand: predicted 4–5 M nodes, measured **1 409 813**;
  predicted 100+ nodes/byte, measured **38.4**. The SHARE leg does not: predicted *"> 50 % of peak
  RSS"*, measured 27.9 % of **node headers**, which rises to ≤ 55.8 % under worst-case chunk doubling
  and rises further by an unmeasured amount once child `Vec`s are counted. ⇒ *"prediction falsified"*
  was itself a claim wider than its evidence, published in the same breath as the correction it was
  meant to model.
- ⚠️ **(3) THE CROSS-INSTRUMENT CHECK IS A REPLICATION, NOT AN INDEPENDENT METHOD.** `.66`'s figures
  and mine are both *peak RSS via `/usr/bin/time -l` on the release probe*. Two independently written
  HARNESSES agreeing to 0.20 % rules out a scripting error; it cannot rule out anything the METHOD is
  blind to — and this leaf just demonstrated that peak RSS is blind to *where* the bytes are. The
  phrase *"falsified against an oracle I did not build"* is downgraded to *"replicated by a harness I
  did not build"*.
- ⚠️ **(4) THE 16 GB CEILING IS AN EXTRAPOLATION BEYOND THE MEASURED RANGE.** The largest real file
  measured is **1.9 MB**; *"a 16 GB host tops out at ~1.7–16 MB"* projects a per-byte ratio ~8× past
  it and assumes the ratio holds at that scale, which was verified only on SYNTHETIC shapes to 10 000
  items. It is a projection, not a measurement.
- ⚠️ **(5) THE `ACCEPT` POPULATION IS 59 FILES AND IS NOT A RANDOM SAMPLE OF "REAL SV".** 428 of the
  487 files ≥ 20 KB REJECT, mostly for want of includes/defines, so the ACCEPT subset is exactly the
  large corpus files that happen to parse STANDALONE under `sv_2017`. The percentiles are true of
  that population and are not claimed of any other.
- ⛔ **(6) `.72`'s COUNT IS CORRECTED 248 → 247, AND THE METHOD BUG MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER.**
  `macro_rules!` is **textually scoped**: only call sites AFTER the definition are shadowed. `mod.rs`
  defines it at line 532 and has **one** `eprintln!` above it (`:424`), which reaches stderr
  normally. My census scanned the whole file. Corrected: **171 + 76 = 247** shipped shadowed sites
  (0 inside `#[cfg(test)]`). ⇒ a census over a *scoped* construct must model the scope; here it cost
  one site, in a file where the macro sits near the top — in a file where it sat near the bottom the
  same bug would have inverted the answer.
- ✅ **WHAT STANDS, UNCHANGED.** Every raw measurement: the `.67`(a) distribution and its census; the
  arena item counts and bytes; **1 409 813 nodes / 38.4 per byte**; the **15.1 %** memo-stats routing
  confound; the no-regression deltas; **11/11 byte-identical**; the `.72` root cause and its
  `PGEN_TRACE_VERBOSITY=debug` proof; and both census defects I caught in myself. The surviving
  claim is narrower and still worth having: **`ParseNode` HEADERS alone are a minority of the parse
  footprint (14–36 %), so a node-slimming lever cannot by itself move the ingestion bound** — but how
  much of the remainder is AST is now an OPEN measurement, not a settled one.
- **OWES (new, and it is (b)'s real remaining shape).** Measure the child-`Vec` + `String` heap:
  `typed_arena::Arena::iter_mut` needs `&mut`, so the detail paths must drop the parser before taking
  it — priced, not asserted. ⛔ `--parse-dump-ast` CANNOT substitute: it emits the annotation-SHAPED
  `PgenValue` tree, not the internal `ParseContent` node tree, so it cannot see a `Sequence` `Vec` at
  all (verified on `spi_device_reg_pkg.sv`).
- ⛔⛔⛔ **AND THE ALLOCATOR COMPARISON IS NOT A BUILD FLAG AWAY — A NEAR-MISS WORTH THE SPACE.** I
  built `parseability_probe` with `--features "generated_parsers mimalloc_perf"` (21 min) intending to
  price fragmentation, and **that binary is NOT a mimalloc arm.** `#[global_allocator]` is declared

  `regex_validation_microbench.rs`); `parseability_probe` never installs it, so the feature compiles

  I would have concluded "fragmentation is not the answer" — a confident, false ruling from a silently

- **THE INSTRUMENT — a MODEL, because `-0125` proved a formula cannot exist for two of the four
  arenas.** `ArenaChunkModel` transcribes `typed-arena` 2.0.2's chunk arithmetic (`INITIAL_SIZE`
  1024, `MIN_CAPACITY` 1; `reserve` retires the live chunk WITH its capacity and opens
  `max(2 × cap, next_power_of_two(additional))`) and is driven by the REAL call sequence — one
  `alloc()` per `Arena::alloc`, one `alloc_extend(min_hint, actual)` per `Arena::alloc_extend`.
  ⛔ **Both extend arguments are load-bearing and neither is derivable from the other**: `min_hint`
  is `size_hint().0`, which is what the crate BRANCHES on, and `actual` is what the iterator really
  yielded; the two branches leave different resident capacities, so a model given one number is
  modelling a call that did not happen. `NodeArena` keeps one model per arena and updates it on the
  SAME armed branch as the owned-heap census, so a production parse pays one field load and one
  predicted branch.
- ⭐⭐ **PROVED AGAINST THE ALLOCATOR, NOT REASONED ABOUT.** `arena_chunk_oracle_probe` drives a REAL
  `typed_arena::Arena` under a counting `#[global_allocator]` (the `regex_alloc_census_probe` shape)
  and compares measured live bytes to the model's for **EXACT equality — not a tolerance**:
  **230 cases over 46 scripts × 5 item sizes (1/24/48/64/1536 B), 0 byte mismatches, 0 item
  mismatches.** The scripts include the pair no formula covers — `1000 × extend(1)` versus
  `1 × extend(1000)`, same items, different capacity — and a deliberately SPINE-FREE case, so a
  compensating pair of errors in the chunk model and the `rest`-spine model cannot cancel.
  ⭐ **RED control observed: a model perturbed by ONE 48-byte item is rejected 230 of 230.**
- ⛔⛔⛔ **AND THEN THE ORACLE'S OWN SCOPE IS THE FINDING: IT PROVES THE MODEL REPRODUCES THE
  ALLOCATOR, AND THIS LEAF IS ATTRIBUTING PEAK RSS.** A freshly allocated chunk is untouched
  anonymous memory; its pages enter RSS when first WRITTEN. So the model's number is an **upper
  bound on residency** and the gap is exactly the arena's unused slack. ⚠️ **The oracle cannot see
  this — it measures the allocator too.** Subtracting an allocation figure from peak RSS would have
  attributed that slack to the arena, silently, in the flattering direction, with an exact oracle
  standing behind it.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **SO IT WAS MEASURED, WITH AN EXPERIMENT THAT NEEDS NO FLOOR MODEL AND NO CALIBRATION.**
  `measure_chunk_residency.sh` runs the same `alloc`-only workload at `N` and `N + 1`, where
  `N = 21 × (2²⁰ − 1)` fills the last chunk EXACTLY, so one extra item opens a chunk of twice the
  size and writes one slot in it:

  | arm | items | allocated | written | peak RSS |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `full` | 22 020 075 | 1 008.00 MB | 1 008.00 MB | 1 063 174 144 B |
  | `one_over` | 22 020 076 | **2 016.00 MB** | 1 008.00 MB | **1 063 206 912 B** |

  **Allocated ×2.0000. Peak RSS ×1.0000 — 32 768 bytes, two pages.** ⭐ Run TWICE, an hour apart,
  on different probe binaries: the absolute peak moved between runs (1 063 190 528 → 1 063 174 144
  on the `full` arm, 0.0015 %) and **the delta was 32 768 B both times**, so the invariant is the
  difference and not the level — which is why the numbers above are re-derived from the tracked
  `chunk_residency.tsv` rather than re-typed beside the run that first printed them. ⇒
  allocated-but-unwritten
  chunk slack is **NOT resident**; it is address space, not RAM. The script REFUSES rather than
  scoring if the arms lack the shape the experiment needs, and it NAMES which hypothesis the ratio
  supports instead of assuming one.
- ⭐ **`touched` IS NEITHER `items` NOR `capacity`, and the model tracks it as a HIGH-WATER MARK,
  because a DRAIN is the one operation that lowers a chunk's item count without un-writing its
  pages** (`alloc_extend`'s overflow path moves already-written items forward). Three unit tests pin
  the three shapes: a chunk retired FULL, a chunk retired PARTLY filled by a large extend, and a
  DRAINED chunk whose written slots (36) exceed the arena's live items (20).

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE COLUMN THAT DECIDES THE LEAF IS `writ/item`, AND IT READS EXACTLY 1.000 ON EVERY ROW —
  44 of 44 arena rows over 11 inputs × 4 arenas.** Written slots equal live items, and the reason is
  structural rather than lucky: `typed_arena` retires a chunk either FULL (the `alloc` path, which
  only reserves when `len == capacity`) or at exactly the item count it held (the `alloc_extend`
  reserve path), and the ONLY path that leaves written-but-dead slots behind needs an iterator that
  understates its own `size_hint` — which is what `extend_regrow` counts, and it reads **0 on 11 of
  11**. ⇒ **`-0121`'s arena ITEM bytes were already the resident figure.**
- ⛔⛔⛔ **THE RULING, AND IT REVERSES `-0124`'s: THE 28–71 % BAND WAS AN ARTIFACT OF BOUNDING
  *ALLOCATION* WHEN THE QUESTION WAS *RESIDENCY*.** The band came from `resident ∈ [items, 2 ×
  items]`. The upper half of it is address space that no page ever backed. Measured over the ladder,
  the AST — arena items plus everything a node owns outside them — is **15.6 %–36.3 % of the
  floor-subtracted peak (median 28.6 %)**, at the 14.72 MB floor, and **14.6 %–36.0 %** at 18.86 MB:
  a MINORITY on every input, at both ends of the floor band. ⇒ **the conclusion `-0122` withdrew is
  restored as a MEASUREMENT** — *"a substantial majority of the parse footprint is not the AST"* —
  with the word **provably** deliberately not restored with it, for the one exclusion below.
- ⚠️ **THE ONE EXCLUSION THAT IS NOT ONE-SIDED IN MY FAVOUR, AND WHY THE RESTORED SENTENCE IS
  QUALIFIED.** Two exclusions survive. `ParseNode`s the MEMO owns are memo-leg bytes and cannot move
  the AST share. **TRANSIENT collection `Vec`s can**: a quantifier collects into a local `Vec` that
  is freed once its contents reach the shaped arenas, so those bytes contribute to PEAK and are
  resident nowhere at report time — and they are AST-shaped, not memo-shaped. They are bounded by
  the largest single composite rather than by the total (one such `Vec` is live at a time), which is
  why the qualification is narrow, but it is unmeasured and it is named here rather than left to be
  found. **ROUTED to `.67`(b) leg 4 with the memo leg.**
- ⭐ **PREDICTION 2 CONFIRMED AND WORTH KEEPING: the slack is a `nodes`-arena phenomenon.** The node
  arena is **78.2 %–88.9 %** of allocated arena bytes on every real and synthetic input (100 % on
  `floor.sv`), so the sawtooth is governed by where the `ParseNode` count falls in the 21 × 2ᵏ
  doubling sequence — which is why `syn_netlist_instances` reads 2.5 % slack and `syn_concat_items`
  reads 45.7 % on the same parser.

- ⭐⭐ **THE JOIN IS INSIDE ONE PROCESS, WHICH IS WHY NO PAIRING ASSUMPTION IS NEEDED.** The probe
  calls the same `parse_sample_detail_with_options` entry point `--parse` calls, so with
  `PGEN_REPORT_PARSE_FOOTPRINT=1` legs 1–3 (arena + owned heap, stderr) and leg 4 (allocator,
  stdout) describe **the same parse**. Cross-check: this probe's arena figures reproduce `-0126`'s
  published `attribution_chunks.tsv` **EXACTLY on 11 of 11 inputs** — a different binary, the same
  bytes.
- ⛔⛔ **THE QUANTITY WAS NAMED BEFORE THE NUMBER, WHICH IS THE ONE THING `-0127` SAID TO DO.** This
  probe reads an ALLOCATION quantity; `.67`'s denominator, floor-subtracted peak RSS, is a RESIDENCY
  quantity. So the attribution below is allocation-side throughout — every term, arena included, is
  a requested-bytes term against a requested-bytes denominator — and the one ratio that crosses the
  two is labelled CROSS-QUANTITY wherever it appears.

- ⛔ **THREE ROWS ARE MISSING FROM THAT TABLE AND EACH IS MISSING FOR A STATED REASON, NOT DROPPED.**

  attribution pass refuses those inputs rather than allowing an unconstrained doubling generator.
  `floor.sv` (20 bytes) is reported separately: **70.0 % of its 2.23 MB peak is bulk small

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE FINDING: THE LARGEST SINGLE STRUCTURE IN THE PARSE WAS ON NOBODY'S CANDIDATE LIST

`generated/systemverilog_parser.rs:4390` builds the thin-memo scratch as
`ThinMemoScratchLease::take(); lease.begin(THIN_RULE_COUNT * (input.len() + 1))` with
`THIN_RULE_COUNT = 109` (`:3291`), and `ThinMemoScratch::begin`
(`rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:2426`) does `self.slots.resize(need, 0)` on a `Vec<u64>`.
⇒ **a dense table of `109 × (len + 1)` eight-byte slots — 872 bytes per input byte — sized before
the parse reads a token and independent of what the file contains.**

- ✅ **PREDICTED FROM SOURCE, THEN FOUND BY SIZE, BYTE-EXACT.** On the two inputs whose size class
  holds exactly one live allocation the identification is unambiguous: `pinmux_reg_top.sv` predicted
  `109 × 1 237 144 × 8 = 1 078 789 568` B and class 31 measures **1 078 789 568 B, count 1**;
  `spi_device_reg_pkg.sv` predicted **26 526 240** B and class 25 measures **26 526 240 B, count 1**.
- ⭐⭐ **AND A SECOND, INDEPENDENT COLUMN AGREES — one that knows nothing about size classes.**
  `ThinMemoScratchLease::drop` returns the scratch to a `thread_local`, so it is **NEVER FREED**.
  Measured: `end_live` — live bytes after the parse returns and everything it owned is dropped —
  minus the predicted scratch is **1.56–3.77 MB on 11 of 11 inputs**, against scratch values
  spanning 18 KB to 1 029 MB. The remainder is a flat process baseline. ⇒ **a caller that parses a
  1.2 MB file keeps 1 029 MB resident after the parse returns, for the life of the thread.**
- ⛔ **IT IS ENGINE-UNIVERSAL, NOT A SYSTEMVERILOG DEFECT, AND THE CENSUS SAYS SO**
  (`thin_scratch_census.sh`, tracked): **10 of 11 generated parsers carry one**, at
  `THIN_RULE_COUNT × 8` bytes per input byte — json 48, systemverilog_preprocessor 64,
  rtl_const_expr 104, return_annotation 120, ebnf 192, regex 224, vhdl 232, rtl_frontend 240,
  semantic_annotation 360, **systemverilog 872**; `scratch` declares none. SystemVerilog is the
  worst because it has the most fused-cascade rules (109), not because anything about it is special.
- ⚠️⚠️ **WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, AND IT IS THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE FIX: UTILISATION.** Nothing
  here says the table is waste. It is a dense direct-address memo — the shape that made the
  fused-cascade path fast — and how many of its `109 × (len + 1)` slots a real parse actually writes
  is **not instrumented**. A sparse replacement is only a win if occupancy is low, and that is a
  measurement, not an inference. ⇒ routed to **`.67`(c)** with the rest of the fix pricing; the
  finding here is the COST, and the cost is now a number.
- ⚠️ **RESIDENCY IS ALSO NOT DIRECTLY MEASURED FOR THIS TABLE.** `resize(needed, 0)` writes every
  slot, so it *should* be resident, and the aggregate is consistent with that (see the
  cross-quantity row below). But leg 3 exists because an allocation figure was mistaken for a
  residency figure, and the `N`/`N + 1` experiment that settled it there has no counterpart here.
  Stated as an allocation measurement, and the residency experiment is routed to `.67`(c).

## ⭐⭐ THE DERIV TAPE IS REFUTED AS A CONTRIBUTOR — A CLEAN NEGATIVE ON A NAMED CANDIDATE

`-0121` named three candidates for the residual and both this leaf and
`docs/book/src/inside-parser-performance.md` repeated them: *"the packrat memo, the derivation tape
and allocator overhead"*. Measured, the **deriv tape is 0.00 %–0.55 % of near-peak live bytes** —
below 1 % on every input and exactly zero on six of eight, because
`Vec::with_capacity(((len + 1) × 5).clamp(80, 40960))` is CAPPED at 40 960 words (327 KB) and the
committed derivation never drove it past a megabyte on this ladder. ⇒ **the tape is not where the
memory goes, and the book sentence naming it is corrected in this slice.**

## THE MEMO IS THE BIGGEST LEG, AND ITS PEAK INCLUDES A REHASH

Success and failure tables together are **24 %–52 %** of near-peak live bytes. Every one is
identified by its exact hashbrown layout — `buckets × size_of::<T>() + buckets + Group::WIDTH`, with
`size_of::<T>()` MEASURED by the probe (`memo_bucket=296`, `memo_fail_bucket=16`) rather than
hand-computed from the field list, because `MemoEntry` carries four `Option`s whose niches the
compiler is free to pack.

- ⭐ **TWO SUCCESS TABLES ARE LIVE AT ONCE ON 4 OF 8 INPUTS** — e.g. `t_math_synmul_mul.v` holds
  **622 854 152 B (2²¹ buckets) AND 311 427 080 B (2²⁰)** simultaneously. That is the REHASH window:
  hashbrown allocates the new table before freeing the old, so the memo's contribution to PEAK is
  **1.5× its steady-state size**. The peak of a parse is partly an artifact of *when* the memo
  doubled.
- ⭐ `Group::WIDTH` is **determined, not assumed**: 8, pinned by the large tables where the two
  candidates are 8 bytes apart and the reading is unambiguous, reproduced at 2¹⁸, 2¹⁹, 2²⁰, 2²¹ and
  2²² buckets across four inputs. An earlier cut tried both widths per allocation and was observed
  fabricating — naming the same 64-bucket table twice at two widths on `floor.sv`.

## ⭐ THE TRANSIENT-`VEC` QUALIFICATION IS NOW BOUNDED BY A NUMBER

`-0126` restored its conclusion without the word *provably*, for one exclusion: transient collection
`Vec`s are AST-shaped, contribute to PEAK, are resident nowhere at report time, and were unmeasured.
They are still not individually identified — but they are now **BOUNDED**, because everything else in
the snapshot is named byte-exactly: whatever they are, they lie inside the **unattributed residual,
which is 3.0 %–9.2 % of near-peak live bytes (median 6.1 %)**. ⭐ And the unnamed allocations have a
shape: on every input ≥ 30 KB the residual is dominated by ONE allocation of an exact power of two
between 2 MB and 128 MB — the signature of a doubling `Vec`. **Naming which `Vec` needs a call-site
instrument and is routed; bounding it did not.**

## ⛔ AND THE FRAGMENTATION HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT SURVIVE, ON THIS WORKLOAD

`-0121` priced allocator fragmentation as a residual candidate on the strength of a `vmmap` profile
in the book measuring **~50 %** across ~72 M small allocations on the uvm input. Measured here as a
CROSS-QUANTITY ratio — allocation over residency, labelled as such —
**`peak_live / (peak_rss − floor)` is 0.584–1.230, median 0.974**: requested live bytes and
floor-subtracted resident bytes are the same size to within a quarter, in both directions. There is
no room for a 50 % overhead on this ladder. ⚠️ It does not refute the book's uvm figure, which is a
different input and a different instrument; it says the SV ladder measured here does not show it.

## ⛔⛔ A MEASUREMENT ERROR I MADE AND CAUGHT, RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEXT SESSION WILL MAKE IT

The first publishing ladder was run WHILE a 10 GB LTO build was compiling. Under that memory
pressure `/usr/bin/time -l` peak RSS read **−13.6 %, −27.9 % and −25.8 % LOW** on exactly the three
inputs whose peak exceeds ~1.9 GB, and within ±0.6 % on the other eight — a silent, plausible,
entirely wrong set of numbers. ⭐ **It was caught because `peak_live` is deterministic and RSS is
not**: the allocation-side figures were BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two runs on 11 of 11 while RSS
moved by a quarter. Re-run on an idle machine, peak RSS agrees with the canonical probe's tracked
ladder within **±0.95 % on all ten real and synthetic inputs**. ⇒ **every peak-RSS number in `.67`
is only as good as the machine's idleness at the time, and nothing in the harness enforces that.**
A `peak_live` figure is not exposed to it.

  its parser, its arena and its memo. All true — and irrelevant, because the structure that
  dominates `end_live` is precisely the one whose `Drop` **puts it back** instead of freeing it.
  ⇒ **before predicting that a thing is gone, read its `Drop`.** The three earlier carry-forwards in
  this leaf were about the QUANTITY (`-0126`), the SENTENCE (`-0125`) and the SET (`-0127`); this
  one is about the LIFETIME, and it is the same failure to check the frame one level further down.

run after a large one sees a capacity unrelated to its own cost. `need_slots` is what THIS parse
asked for and what `-0128` priced at 872 B per input byte. (On this harness one parse per process
makes `cap/need` read exactly **1.00** on 11 of 11, so the distinction is latent here and would not
be in a long-lived embedder.)

- ⭐ **`store_calls / distinct_slots` is EXACTLY 1.00 on every input.** Each slot is written once and

  ~28-byte hash entry with its control byte and load factor) and said: at or above it the dense
  table is the right design and `.67`(c) should say so and stop. **Every input ≥ 30 KB measured
  BELOW it — 10 of 10, by a factor of 6 to 400.**

## (ii) RESIDENCY — and the first attempt to settle it was WRONG, which is why it is here

⛔⛔⛔ **A BOUND I BUILT, BELIEVED, AND THEN RETRACTED BEFORE PUBLISHING IT.** The obvious move was to
settle residency from the ladder's own aggregate: take `peak_live` versus `peak_rss − floor`,
subtract the arena chunk slack leg 3 PROVED non-resident, and see what is left for the thin table.
It produced a beautiful answer — **"100 % resident, saturated on 11 of 11 inputs"** — and it is
worthless. The identity is `N_thin ≤ V − 348 MB` on `pinmux_reg_top.sv`, where `V` is the
allocator/non-heap overhead **which nothing here measures**; the table only came out saturated
because I had silently set `V = 0`. ⇒ **a bound with an unmeasured term in it is not a bound, and a
saturated result on every row is exactly when to look for the term you forgot.**

⭐⭐ **SO IT WAS MEASURED WITH AN ISOLATING SHAPE INSTEAD, AND THE SLOPE DECIDES IT.** The table is
sized from input LENGTH alone, so a file that is almost entirely COMMENT makes it huge while the
parse does essentially nothing — no AST, no memo growth, no tape. Three sizes give a slope:

| input B | table MB | slots written | occupancy | peak RSS MB | peak_live MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 262 100 | 218.0 | **14** | 0.000012 % | 241.5 | 227.7 |
| 524 260 | 436.0 | **14** | 0.000006 % | 463.6 | 449.1 |
| 1 048 580 | 872.0 | **14** | 0.000003 % | **906.0** | 891.9 |

**ΔRSS/Δinput = 888.3 and 884.7 B per input byte over the two intervals; overall 885.9, against a
table costing exactly 872.0.** The table is **98.4 % of the marginal resident cost**. A resident
table predicts ~872; a lazy one predicts ~0.

⇒ ⛔⛔⛔ **THE NEVER-WRITTEN PAGES ARE RESIDENT. 914 362 632 BYTES ALLOCATED, 112 BYTES WRITTEN,
906 MB RESIDENT.** `Vec::resize(need, 0)` faults in every page; the parse then writes 0.07 %–4.6 %
of them, and 0.00001 % on this shape. ⭐ The slope is the invariant and the level is not — the same
discipline leg 3's `N`/`N + 1` experiment used, and the reason three sizes were run rather than one.

## ⇒ WHAT THIS DECIDES, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT

- ✅ **The cost is REAL RAM, not address space.** `-0128` could only publish an allocation figure and
  named that gap; it is now closed in the direction that makes it worse.
- ✅ **A sparse structure would be smaller** — occupancy is 6× to 400× below break-even. ⛔ **And it
  is still REFUSED as the fix**, because it trades hashing for the dense table's O(1) and peak speed
  is the non-negotiable half of the north star. A cost is rejected, not traded.
- ⭐⭐ **THE CANDIDATE THAT IS NOT A TRADE, and it is what `.67`(c)(iii) should price first: stop
  faulting in what is never written.** The slot word is `(generation: u32, index + 1: u32)` and the
  generation check ALREADY makes an unwritten slot invalid whatever it contains — so the zero-fill
  is redundant to correctness. Two directions, both preserving O(1) with no hashing: obtain the
  table from a ZEROED mapping the kernel backs lazily (untouched pages never become resident), or
  narrow the word so the same table costs half. ⚠️ Neither is measured here and neither is claimed;
  they are named so (c)(ii) starts from a shape rather than a blank page.
- ⚠️ **`.67`(c)(iii) — the memo REHASH spike — is still owed** (`-0128`: two success tables live at
  once on 4 of 8 inputs ⇒ the memo's contribution to peak is 1.5× its steady state).

## THE INSTRUMENT — A LIFETIME TAPE, BECAUSE A SNAPSHOT HAS NO SUCCESSION IN IT

`-0128` published *"two success tables are live at once … that is the REHASH window, so the memo's
contribution to PEAK is 1.5× its steady-state size"* from the probe's size-class SNAPSHOT. A
snapshot cannot support that sentence, and the reason is not a detail: **it shows CO-RESIDENCY, and
"rehash" is a claim about SUCCESSION** — that *this* table replaced *that* one. It is also taken at
the hysteresis instant rather than at the peak, and it reports a TOTAL PER CLASS, so naming the
individual structures inside it is a subset-sum search over a number with many decompositions.

So the probe now records LIFETIMES: one row per allocation at or above a threshold, carrying the
event at which it was made and the event at which it was released (`18446744073709551615` if the
process never released it). ENGINE tier is not involved — this is a probe bin, **ZERO library Rust,
ZERO grammar, ZERO codegen, ZERO generated bytes**.

- ⛔⛔⛔ **THE FIRST CUT HAD TWO CLOCKS AND WOULD HAVE ANSWERED CONFIDENTLY AND WRONGLY.**
  `ALLOC_CALLS` and `FREE_CALLS` count different events, so an allocation stamped `alloc_ord=988`
  beside a release stamped `free_ord=195` is not out of order — the two numbers cannot be compared
  at all, and `alloc(A) < alloc(B) < free(A)` is meaningless across them. Caught by reading the
  probe's first output, not by any check. ⭐⭐ **AND THE TAPE'S OWN CONTROL COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT
  IT**: "live at instant I" compares alloc ordinals to I's alloc ordinal and free ordinals to I's
  free ordinal, each staying inside one clock, so the control passes while succession is nonsense.
  ⇒ **A CONTROL VALIDATES THE PROPERTY IT IS BUILT FROM.** Succession is a different property and
  needed its own instrument: one `EVENT_SEQ` that every allocation AND every release advances.
- ⭐⭐ **THE CONTROL IS AN EQUALITY, NOT A BAND, AND IT PASSES.** The tape and the size-class table
  are maintained by independent code paths in the probe, so the tape's reconstruction of "live at
  the snapshot instant" must reproduce the class table byte-for-byte in every class at or above the
  threshold. **148 (input, class) pairs checked, 0 mismatched.**
- ⛔ **A TRUNCATED TAPE IS REFUSED BY NAME, NEVER AVERAGED — and that arm fired on the first run.**
  At 2^16 entries `br_gh330.v` — a **36 KB** file — overflowed by **185 902**. Raised to 2^20 and
  re-run, the tape is complete on 11 of 11. ⚠️ **The truncated table was a PREFIX, not a sample**:
  it showed 65 443 allocations of exactly 8 192 bytes where the complete run shows **220 773**.

  live**, and the smaller was freed **after** it. `superseded` is 1 and `co-resident` is 0 on 5 of 5.

  no input lands between, because hashbrown doubles and the old table is exactly half the new one.

  *"The memo's contribution to PEAK is 1.5× its steady state"* holds on **5 of the 10** inputs the
  tape covers and on **5 of `-0128`'s 8**. On the other five it is exactly 1.0. Whether a parse pays
  the spike is decided by **where the last doubling falls relative to the peak**, which is a property
  of the input's shape and not of the engine.
- ⚠️ **THE SAVING IS AN UPPER BOUND AND IS REPORTED AS ONE.** The overlap is what the peak-setting
  instant would lose if the old table had been freed first. The whole-parse peak would fall by **at
  most** that: the tape records only allocations at or above its threshold, so between two recorded
  events it cannot bound the live curve, and the peak may relocate. **8.18 %–15.44 % of `peak_live`,
  median 15.01 % over the five, is a ceiling on the prize, not the prize.**
