## ⛔⛔⛔ AND RUNNING THE PROBE'S OWN UNIT TESTS FOR THE FIRST TIME FOUND A LATENT PANIC IN THE GLOBAL ALLOCATOR

`-0128` wrote a test asserting `class_of(usize::MAX) < CLASSES` and noted that the probe's tests
"compiled but could not be run"; `-0129` closed that gap for the LIBRARY tests, not for this bin's.
This slice ran them, and that assertion **FAILS**: `class_of` returned **64** for a 48-element table.

- **The defect is real and it is in the allocator's hot path.** A `Layout` may carry any size up to
  `isize::MAX`, so a request of 2⁴⁷ bytes or more is REPRESENTABLE even though no host can serve it —
  and `note_alloc` indexes `LIVE_CLASS_BYTES[class_of(size)]` **before** delegating to `System`.
  Rust bounds-checks, so this is a PANIC inside `alloc`, not undefined behaviour — which is worse
  than the impossible allocation simply failing.
- **It cannot have affected one number in `.67`.** The clamp binds only at 2⁴⁷ bytes; the largest
  allocation anywhere on this ladder is 1 078 789 568 B (class 31). The fix is `class_of(…)
  .min(CLASSES - 1)` and the test now pins the SATURATION rather than the false claim, with two
  boundary rows either side of it.
- ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **A TEST THAT HAS NEVER BEEN RUN IS NOT A TEST.** It was written by the same hand as the
  code, agreed with the code's own comment (*"48 buckets cover every allocation up to 128 TiB — far
  past anything a parse can request"*), and was wrong with it: the comment states a REASONED bound on
  what a host can serve, and the array is indexed by what a `Layout` can REPRESENT. Two different
  populations, one sentence. The same shape as this leaf's other findings, met in the test file.

## ⭐⭐ THE THIN TABLE IS NEVER FREED, READ FROM A SECOND INSTRUMENT

`-0128` established this by subtraction: `end_live` minus a predicted scratch size is a flat
1.56–3.77 MB on 11 of 11. The tape reads the release event itself — a different instrument, no
prediction in it — and answers **`free_seq = NEVER` on 11 of 11**, at sizes from 18 312 B to
1 078 789 568 B. ⭐ It is allocated at **`alloc_seq = 782` on every input**, the same position in the
event stream regardless of file size, which is the tape's own confirmation of `-0128`'s reading of
the source: the table is sized *before the parse reads a token*.

## THE FIX PRICING — AND THE MEMO SPIKE IS RULED NOT WORTH REMOVING

The spike costs 50 % of the memo's steady size, and the only way to remove it is to not double near
the peak — i.e. to PRE-SIZE the memo so the final table is allocated once. `memo` is built with
`rustc_hash::FxHashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(256, …)` (`generated/systemverilog_parser.rs:4338`),
a **literal 256 independent of the input**, so a large parse doubles about fourteen times. Sizing it
from input length is the obvious candidate. **It is refused, and the measurement is what refuses it:**

| input | final buckets | buckets per input byte |
|---|---|---|
| `spi_device_reg_pkg.sv` | 32 768 | **1.0772** |
| `pinmux_reg_top.sv` | 2 097 152 | 1.6952 |
| `syn_port_list` 10 000 | 262 144 | 2.0335 |
| `syn_case_items` 10 000 | 1 048 576 | 5.2995 |
| `t_math_synmul_mul.v` | 2 097 152 | 6.3519 |
| `br_gh330.v` | 262 144 | 7.1481 |
| `comp1000.v` | 524 288 | 7.5118 |
| `syn_concat_items` 10 000 | 524 288 | 7.6069 |
| `syn_netlist_instances` 10 000 | 4 194 304 | 7.8305 |
| `syn_netlist_instances` 2 500 | 1 048 576 | **8.0266** |

**The spread is 7.45×.** ⚠️ Honestly qualified: bucket counts are powers of two, so quantisation
alone can produce up to 2× of that; the shape-driven part is about **3.7×**. Either way the
arithmetic is one-sided. **A pre-size only removes the spike if it lands AT OR ABOVE the final
size**, because the peak is set by the LAST doubling — starting higher removes early doublings,
which is a SPEED question, not a peak one. A single length-derived factor big enough to cover
`syn_netlist_instances` would hand `spi_device_reg_pkg.sv` **7.45× the table it needs**, against a
spike that costs **0.5×**. ⇒ ⛔ **RULED: the memo rehash spike is not removable by pre-sizing from
input length, and no cheaper removal is known. It is priced, ruled, and CLOSED — not routed.** The
lever that does scale the memo is its 296-byte `MemoEntry`, which is a different question and is not
opened here.

## ⭐⭐⭐ A FINDING THE PEAK-SNAPSHOT INSTRUMENTS COULD NOT SEE, BECAUSE IT IS ENTIRELY TRANSIENT

Every instrument in `.67` so far reads a HIGH-WATER: the arena census, the owned-heap census, the
size-class snapshot, `peak_live`. An allocation that is made and freed between two high-water marks
is invisible to all of them. The tape is the first instrument here with a time axis, and the first
thing it found is traffic:

| input | file B | size | count | freed | mean lifetime (events) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `br_gh330.v` | 36 673 | 8 192 | **220 773** | 220 771 | 29.4 |
| `br_gh330.v` | 36 673 | 16 384 | **30 561** | 30 560 | 598.0 |
| `comp1000.v` | 69 795 | 8 192 | **43 437** | 43 435 | 861.8 |

**`br_gh330.v` makes 251 334 allocations of two exact sizes on a 36 KB file — 6.85 allocations per
input byte — and frees all but THREE.** They contribute **nothing** to peak RSS or to
`peak_live`, which is why nothing in `.67` had seen them; they are pure allocator traffic. The two
sizes and the count relation are consistent with one buffer per something that grows once
(8 192 = 1 024 × 8 bytes, then 16 384), but ⚠️ **that is a reading of the numbers, not a measurement:
the tape carries no call site**, and naming the `Vec` needs a call-site instrument.

⇒ ROUTED to new leaf **`.75`**, with the producer and the raw histogram tracked. ⛔ It is a SPEED
question, not a footprint one, so it is PARKED behind the director's *"thorough and accurate and
fast (not reached yet, because it is not the focus right now)"* ordering — but it is OWNED, with the
next instrument named, rather than reported and left.

## THE FIX PRICING — THE THIN TABLE. THE MECHANISM IS PROVED AND THE SAVING IS A BRACKET WHOSE LOW END IS ZERO

`.67`(c)(ii) named the one direction that is not a trade: **stop faulting in what is never written.**
`ThinMemoScratch::begin` does `self.slots.resize(need, 0)`, which allocates uninitialised memory and
then WRITES a zero into every slot; the generation stamp already makes an unwritten slot invalid
whatever it contains, so that write is redundant to correctness. The candidate is a zeroed allocation
the kernel backs lazily — in Rust, `vec![0u64; n]`, which specialises to `alloc_zeroed`.

⛔ **Whether that works is a property of the host's allocator, not of the source, so it is measured.**
A standalone probe isolates the mechanism from the engine entirely — one table, one fill strategy,
one write pattern, and the peak RSS the host reports. Table size is **114 295 329 slots =
914 362 632 B**, the exact table `comment_1024k.sv` asks for and the one `.67`(c)(ii) measured at
906 MB resident. Five repeats; **peak RSS is min = median = max in all nine cells**, so the estimator
is not in question here (`-0129`).

| scenario | writes | pages touched | `resize` | `zeroed` | `reserve_only` (control) | cut |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **isolating** — the `(c)(ii)` shape | 14, page stride | 14 of 223 234 (0.006 %) | 873.6 MB | **1.7 MB** | 1.6 MB | **99.81 %** |
| **clustered** — 4.58 %, contiguous | 5 234 726, stride 1 | 10 225 of 223 234 (4.58 %) | 873.9 MB | **41.8 MB** | 1.6 MB | **95.22 %** |
| **scattered** — 4.58 %, one per page | 5 234 726, page stride | **223 234 of 223 234 (100 %)** | 878.2 MB | **878.2 MB** | 1.6 MB | **0.00 %** |

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE CONTROL SETTLES THE CAUSE, AND IT IS THE ZERO-FILL.** `reserve_only` — the same
  914 MB allocated and NOTHING written — costs **1.6 MB resident in every scenario**, a **546×**
  separation from `resize`. So the allocation is free and the fill is the whole cost. Had the two
  read alike, this fix direction would have been refuted outright, which is what the arm is for.
- ⭐⭐ **AND THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED WHERE `(c)(ii)` MEASURED IT**: on the isolating shape the
  same table costs **873.6 MB** filled and **1.7 MB** lazily backed. `(c)(ii)`'s 906 MB is not a law
  of the table; it is the cost of writing zeros into it.
- ⛔⛔⛔ **AND THE SCATTERED ROW IS WHY THIS SLICE DOES NOT IMPLEMENT THE FIX.** At the SAME 4.58 %
  occupancy, one write per page touches every page and the saving is **exactly zero**. Occupancy is
  therefore the wrong quantity: **what decides the fix is DISTINCT PAGES TOUCHED, and nothing in this
  repository measures it.**
  ⭐ **THE CENSUS BEHIND THAT "NOTHING MEASURES IT", RUN RATHER THAN ASSERTED** (`GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS`):
  `git grep -nEi 'distinct_pages|pages_touched|page_touched|SLOTS_PER_PAGE|madvise|mincore' -- 'rust/src' 'scripts'`
  → **0 hits**. The only `madvise` strings anywhere in the tree are inside captured `sample`-profiler
  stack traces under `docs/tasks/artifacts/*/sample_*.txt`, which are recorded output, not code. And
  the census `ThinMemoScratch` DOES carry is enumerable rather than assumed — `ThinMemoScratchStats`
  has six fields (`armed`, `capacity_slots`, `need_slots`, `distinct_slots_written`, `store_calls`,
  `clear_calls`) and none of them is about pages.
  ⚠️ A reading of the layout — `slot = rule_index × (input_len + 1) +
  position`, so a rule firing at a few per cent of positions lands ~20 writes in every 512-position
  page of its own row — points toward the SCATTERED end, i.e. toward the fix being worth little. That
  is a reading, not a measurement, and it is exactly the kind of inference this leaf has been
  correcting all week.
- ⇒ **ROUTED to new leaf `.74`, which owes the PAGE census BEFORE any code**: count distinct
  512-slot pages a real parse writes, over the same ladder, and implement only if the number says the
  fix pays. Landing `alloc_zeroed` on the strength of the isolating shape alone would be pricing a
  fix on a synthetic input — the error `.61`(b) made and `.67`(a) was opened to correct.

  `:2221`/`:2647` (the diagnostic), `:4256`/`:4373` (the protocol arm), `cascade.rs:619`/`:648` (the
  fused arm — the graph a bare parse actually runs).
- ⭐⭐ **THE FIX: THE THRESHOLD BECOMES A SAMPLE POINT, AND THE HOST ANSWERS.**
  `dedicated_parse_stack.rs` records each parse thread's extent (`(base, reservation)`) at thread
  entry; when a guard reaches its current threshold, `RecursionGuard::extend_depth_probe` asks how
  much stack the parse has really spent (`base − current`), divides by the live frame depth to get a
  MEASURED per-frame cost, and moves the threshold out by a quarter of what the remaining headroom
  can still carry. **Why the estimate cannot be optimistic**: `used = prologue + depth × real_cost`,
  so `used / depth = prologue/depth + real_cost ≥ real_cost` — the derived per-frame cost is an
  OVER-estimate by construction, and the guard therefore fires early rather than late.
  **Release and debug size themselves** (`SV-CORPUS-GRAD.8c.3` measured ≈2 KB/frame release and
  ≈17 KB/frame debug; nothing in the fix reads either number).
- ⛔ **EVERY UNKNOWN IS ANSWERED WITH THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, never with a guess**: no recorded extent
  (any thread this process did not create for parsing) → the compiled floor stands; a stack that did
  not grow downward → floor; a spend too small to divide honestly → floor; no headroom → fire. A
  stack overflow ABORTS the embedder and is strictly worse than a diagnosed rejection, which is the
  bound `.63`(c) set on this leaf and it is honoured.
- ⭐ **THE 500 LITERALS ARE GONE BECAUSE THE ARM CLAUSE IS GONE, WHICH IS ALSO THE SINGLE-SOURCING.**
  `check_cycle_id` returns `MutualRecursive` only when the host is genuinely out of headroom, so a
  re-test against a baked-in number could only DISAGREE with the guard that produced the verdict.
  **Closed emission census, 11 of 11 artifacts enumerated from the directory**: every one now carries
  **exactly 1** `4096usize` (the sample floor in `RecursionGuard::new`), **0**
  `if depth >= 4096usize`, and **1** `ceiling: self.recursion_guard.last_ceiling_depth` — so the
  number a rejection reports is now read from the guard that stopped it, which meets `.61`(a)'s
  no-drift requirement more strictly than baking it in did.

### ⛔⛔ `.68` — **THE CYCLE GUARD SCANS THE WHOLE LIVE STACK ON EVERY RULE ENTRY, SO A DEPTH-`D` PARSE IS Θ(D²). WITH THE CEILING NOW AT THE HOST'S STACK, THIS IS THE FIRST THING A DEEP PARSE RUNS OUT OF** (`todo`, opened 2026-08-28 by `.65`'s own AFTER measurement / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0117`)

- **WHY + WHERE**: `RecursionGuard::check_cycle_id` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs`) walks the entire
  `rule_id_stack` on every rule entry looking for a same-id frame, with no early exit and no index.
  `check_cycle` (the legacy name-scan) has the same shape.
- **MEASURED, on the shipped release probe** (`cast_paren`, accept path): 250 → 0.13 s · 500 → 0.40 s
  · 1 000 → 1.43 s · 2 000 → 5.63 s · 4 000 → 22.24 s. Each doubling costs 3.1× → 3.6× → 3.9× → 3.95×,
  converging on 4× — the signature of a quadratic term, and consistent with an Θ(depth) scan per
  entry.
- ⛔ **WHY IT IS A LEAF NOW RATHER THAN BEFORE**: while the ceiling was 4096 frames the quadratic
  term was capped at a few hundred source levels and never dominated. `.65` moved the ceiling to
  ≈4 800 levels for this shape at the default reservation, so the term is now the binding constraint
  on *"any type of RTL files we throw at them"* — the mandate's own words — even though the stack
  bound is satisfied.
- ⭐ **THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS ALREADY VISIBLE, so this is a sizing question rather than a research
  one**: the scan answers two questions — "is `(rule_id, position)` already live?" and "is `rule_id`
  live at a LATER position?" — both of which a per-rule position stack answers in O(1) while still
  yielding the OLDEST matching frame index that `last_block_frame` needs (it is the bottom of that
  rule's own stack).
- ⛔ **SEQUENCING**: this is SPEED, and speed is blocked behind accuracy by standing director
  ordering. It is recorded here so the ordering is a decision rather than an omission, and it sits
  with `.56`(d)/`.58`.
- ⛔⛔ **AND THAT SEQUENCING WAS PUT TO THE DIRECTOR AND UPHELD, 2026-08-29.** Layer A's stored
  `next_action` had named `.68` as the frontier after `.67` closed; reading THIS bullet is what
  surfaced the conflict, and the ruling was explicit: *"functionality, accuracy first, speed work
  should always come after. What is speed if the parser doesn't parse properly?"* ⇒ **`.68` stays
  parked behind `.69` even though it is the larger measured finding** (`.69` is a typed bound the
  capability mandate calls a defect; `.68` is latency). → [[feedback_correctness_before_speed]].
  ⭐ The lesson for the tracker: **a leaf that records WHY it is parked is what makes an ordering
  ruling checkable instead of remembered** — the resume pointer is the copy that goes stale.

  first thing it cannot establish, so a later quantity was never computed rather than computed as
  zero.

  `RecursionGuard`, which the generated parser owns and the parse adapters never hand back

  family's adapter signature — CODEGEN, and a regeneration of all 11 parsers plus a digest-keyed
  `SV-CONTRACT-CURRENCY` churn, for a diagnostic. A thread-local is readable by anything on the parse
  thread; it is carried across the `run_on_dedicated_parse_stack` JOIN (child's reading REPLACES the
  caller's, `None` included) so the spawn-per-call EMBEDDING path sees it too, not only the CLI.
- ⛔ **THE HUMAN SURFACE IS OPT-IN, AND THAT IS A MEASURED DECISION, NOT TIMIDITY.**

  TRACKED measurement surface for every ceiling-contacting file in the 16 336-file corpus.
  `PGEN_REPORT_STACK_PROBE` follows the established `PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS` convention; the
  PROGRAMMATIC surface (`last_stack_probe_refusal()`) is always live and costs nothing.

  scanned the whole file.

- ⚠️ **31 IS A CANDIDATE COUNT, NOT A DEFECT COUNT, and the distinction is the whole leaf.** Those two
  files carry large deliberately-verbose debug dumps, and a `⚠️`/`❌` line *inside a debug dump* is
  correctly gated. What makes any of them a defect is a message a consumer is entitled to see
  unconditionally — the standing rule
  [[feedback_severity_never_gated_by_verbosity]]. The file already defends exactly one banner on
  exactly that argument (`mod.rs` `NON_CANONICAL_BANNER`), which is evidence the class is real and
  was adjudicated once, site by site, and never censused.
- ⛔⛔ **THE FIRST CENSUS I WROTE FOR THIS WAS WRONG AND ITS NUMBER MUST NOT BE QUOTED.** It scanned a
  fixed **6-line window** after each `eprintln!`, so a severity marker belonging to a LATER statement
  was attributed to an earlier one — it scored `eprintln!("File: {}:{}")` as severity-bearing because
  a `⚠️ WARNING` sat two statements below. It read **41** where the statement-accurate version reads
  **31**: a **32 % overstatement**, in the alarming direction. The producer now balances parentheses
  from the macro's own opening delimiter and attributes only what that one statement contains.
- ⛔ **AND ITS `std_qualified` COUNTER READ 0 BY CONSTRUCTION.** It tested the SAME regex match for a
  `std::` prefix — but that regex carries `(?<![:\w])`, which excludes the `:` of `std::`, so a
  qualified call can never match it. The counter reported **0** on a file that demonstrably has
  **2**. ⇒ **a counter that cannot be non-zero is not a measurement**, and it is the same shape as
  the retired `blind_spot_factor` and the `case_items` miscount: an instrument agreeing with a
  plausible expectation because it is structurally blind.
- **OWES**: (a) adjudicate the 31 candidates one at a time into *correctly gated debug dump* vs
  *severity a consumer must see*; (b) fix the second class with `std::eprintln!`; (c) decide whether
  the shadow should be RENAMED (e.g. `trace_dbg!`) so the trap cannot be walked into again — the
  strongest fix, since it makes the gating visible at every call site instead of at one
  `macro_rules!` 4 000 lines away.
- ⛔ **ROUTED + PARKED behind the SV lane** ([[project_nexsim_sv_signoff_delivery_focus]]): no measured
  consumer is blocked by it today, and it is engine-wide rather than an SV-release blocker.

### ⛔⛔ `.73` — **THE SHIPPED SV PARSE PATH RESOLVES ITS STANDARD-LIBRARY BUNDLE FROM A COMPILE-TIME ABSOLUTE PATH, AND A BINARY WHOSE REPOSITORY HAS MOVED LOADS NO STDLIB AT ALL — SILENTLY, AT EXIT 0** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED behind the SV lane, opened 2026-08-29 by `.67`(b) leg 4's own source reading / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0128`)

- **WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN LATER.** The artifact this bears on is the SV parser binary /
  library handed to **Nexsim**, and the director's path doctrine is explicit that the repository root
  *"can be moved around, even on a different filesystem … and this shall not affect the project in any
  way, that is very important, I would say, even critical"* (`CLAUDE.md` §12). This is the one shipped
  runtime site where that is not true.
- **WHERE — one site, not thirty-seven, and the difference is the whole finding.**
  `rust/src/parser_registry.rs:1394` builds `std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))`, walks
  to its parent, and joins `parser_libs/<profile>_std` to preload the SystemVerilog standard-library
  fact records into `semantic_runtime_state` before the parse
  (`preload_systemverilog_stdlib`, called at `:1268` on the `--parse` detail lane).
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN A LIMITATION.**
  `:1399` reads `if !stdlib_path.is_dir() { return Ok(()); }` — no warning, no diagnostic, no
  non-zero exit. A binary built at path A and run after the tree moved to path B therefore parses
  with an EMPTY stdlib fact set, and every `@emit_fact`/predicate that consults a `std::` name
  answers differently, at exit 0. ⚠️ *That the answers differ is inferred from the fact records being
  pushed into the semantic runtime state, not yet measured; the leaf must measure it before the
  severity is fixed.*
- ⭐ **THE CENSUS, because "the codebase is full of them" is the claim that would have been wrong.**
  `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` occurs **37** times in `rust/src/`, and almost all of them are
  harmless: 2 are `include_str!(concat!(…))`, i.e. COMPILE-TIME reads whose content is baked into the
  binary (`embedding_api.rs:5087`/`:5159`), and the large majority of the rest sit in `#[test]` /
  `#[cfg(test)]` harness code (`parse_harness*`, `stimuli_generator`, `ebnf_frontend`,
  `ast_shape_contract`, `round_trip_tests`), which only ever runs from a build of the tree it is in.
  ⇒ **the shipped-runtime surface is `parser_registry.rs:1394` alone**, with
  `parse_harness.rs:253` (an overridable `unwrap_or_else` default) and
  `parse_harness_combinator_suite.rs:1107` (`pub fn default_ast_pipeline_bin`) as two lower-severity
  siblings to adjudicate rather than assume.
- ✅ **THE ABSOLUTE PATH IS IN THE SHIPPED BINARY — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.**
  `strings -a rust/target/release/parseability_probe | grep '/Volumes/SSD/Documents/github/pgen/rust'`
  returns a hit on the canonical `646475a2…` probe.
- **ACCEPTANCE (to be discharged when this leaf is worked).**
  (a) MEASURE the behaviour delta: parse one corpus file that exercises a `std::` fact with the
      bundle present and with it absent, and record whether the verdict or the semantic store differs
      — the severity is whatever that measurement says, not what this routing note guesses.
  (b) Make the absence LOUD before making it robust: an unresolvable stdlib bundle must be a named
      diagnostic, never `Ok(())`.
  (c) Resolve `parser_libs/` from a runtime-derived root (the executable's own location, an explicit
      option, or an env override) with the compile-time path as a last resort, so a moved tree keeps
      working — the same "derive it, never bake it" shape `.65` applied to the recursion ceiling.
  (d) Adjudicate the two siblings above by name.
- ⛔ **PARKED, not abandoned.** Routed out of `.67`(b) leg 4 under the SV lane lock's own rule —
  a finding is routed to a leaf, never worked mid-slice — and it is recorded here rather than in a
  message, per the director's 2026-08-26 standing correction that logging a defect is a property of

### ⛔⛔ `.74` — **THE DENSE THIN-MEMO TABLE'S ZERO-FILL IS WHAT MAKES 95–99.9 % NEVER-WRITTEN PAGES RESIDENT, AND A LAZILY-BACKED TABLE REMOVES BETWEEN 0 % AND 95 % OF IT. THE PAGE CENSUS THAT DECIDES WHICH COMES FIRST** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED behind the SV lane, opened 2026-08-29 by `.67`(c)(iii)'s fix pricing / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0131`)

- **WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so this leaf does not re-derive it.** The table is
  `THIN_RULE_COUNT × (input_len + 1)` slots of `u64`, 872 B per input byte on SystemVerilog
  (`.67`(b) leg 4); it is **95.4–99.93 % never written** (`.67`(c)(i)); it is **resident anyway**
  (`.67`(c)(ii)); it is **never freed** — `free_seq = NEVER` on 11 of 11, read directly from the
  lifetime tape (`.67`(c)(iii)); and the cause is `ThinMemoScratch::begin`'s
  `self.slots.resize(need, 0)`, PROVED by a control in which the same 914 MB reserved and **not**
  filled costs **1.6 MB** resident against **873.6 MB** filled — a 546× separation.
- **THE FIX SHAPE**, and it is not a trade: `vec![0u64; n]` specialises to `alloc_zeroed`, the kernel
  backs the pages lazily, untouched pages never become resident. **O(1) direct addressing is kept and
  no hashing is introduced** — the sparse rewrite `.67`(c)(i) refused stays refused. The generation
  stamp already invalidates an unwritten slot, so removing the zero-fill is correctness-neutral by
  the table's own design.
- ⛔⛔⛔ **WHAT THIS LEAF OWES FIRST, AND WHY NO CODE MAY LAND BEFORE IT: THE PAGE CENSUS.** Measured
  at the same 4.58 % occupancy, the saving is **95.22 %** when the writes are contiguous and
  **0.00 %** when they are one per 4 KiB page. **Occupancy does not decide this; DISTINCT PAGES
  TOUCHED does, and nothing measures it.**
  ⭐ **THE CENSUS BEHIND THAT "NOTHING MEASURES IT", RUN RATHER THAN ASSERTED** (`GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS`):
  `git grep -nEi 'distinct_pages|pages_touched|page_touched|SLOTS_PER_PAGE|madvise|mincore' -- 'rust/src' 'scripts'`
  → **0 hits**. The only `madvise` strings anywhere in the tree are inside captured `sample`-profiler
  stack traces under `docs/tasks/artifacts/*/sample_*.txt`, which are recorded output, not code. And
  the census `ThinMemoScratch` DOES carry is enumerable rather than assumed — `ThinMemoScratchStats`
  has six fields (`armed`, `capacity_slots`, `need_slots`, `distinct_slots_written`, `store_calls`,
  `clear_calls`) and none of them is about pages.
  ⚠️ A reading of the layout
  (`slot = rule_index × (input_len + 1) + position`) points toward the scattered end — a rule firing
  at a few per cent of positions puts ~20 writes in every 512-slot page of its own row — which would
  make the fix worth nearly nothing. **That is a reading, not a measurement, and this leaf exists to
  replace it with one.**
- **THE INSTRUMENT, NAMED**: extend the armed census on `ThinMemoScratch::store` with a distinct-page
  counter (a bitset over `need / 512` bits, or a last-page-touched short-circuit plus a set), report
  it beside `PARSE-THIN-OCCUPANCY:`, and run the tracked ladder. It is the same ENGINE-tier,
  arm-gated, zero-codegen shape `.67`(c)(i) already shipped, so the cost argument is settled prior
  art rather than a new one.
- **THEN, AND ONLY IF THE CENSUS SAYS IT PAYS**: change `begin` to obtain a grown table from
  `alloc_zeroed` instead of `resize`, keeping the thread-local recycling (a recycled table needs no
  re-zeroing — the generation bump already invalidates it, which is the property that makes the
  change safe). ⚠️ Note the recycling caveat that the pricing does NOT cover: pages faulted by an
  earlier parse on the same thread stay resident, so the saving is largest on the first parse of a
  thread and decays as the thread is reused. A long-lived embedder needs the release/`madvise` half
  as well, and that is a second question this leaf must not silently fold into the first.
- ⚠️ **DO NOT PRICE THIS FROM THE ISOLATING SHAPE.** The 99.81 % figure is measured on a synthetic
  comment-only write pattern (14 writes) and is a MECHANISM result, not a value result. Quoting it as
  the saving would be exactly the error `.61`(b) made and `.67`(a) was opened to correct.

### ⛔ `.75` — **A 36 KB INPUT MAKES 251 334 HEAP ALLOCATIONS OF TWO EXACT SIZES AND FREES ALL BUT THREE — 6.85 PER INPUT BYTE, INVISIBLE TO EVERY HIGH-WATER INSTRUMENT IN `.67`** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED behind the SV lane, opened 2026-08-29 by `.67`(c)(iii)'s lifetime tape / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0131`)

- **WHAT IS MEASURED.** `docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67c/tape_histogram_8k.tsv`, from a **complete**
  lifetime tape (`tape_complete=true`, 0 overflow on 11 of 11) at an 8 KiB threshold. ⭐ **The
  artifact's EXISTENCE is the completeness evidence**: `tape_histogram.py` REFUSES to reduce a tape
  any input reports incomplete, by name, rather than producing a histogram that looks whole — so a
  tracked histogram cannot have been derived from a truncated run.

  | input | file B | size | count | freed | mean lifetime (events) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `br_gh330.v` | 36 673 | 8 192 | **220 773** | 220 771 | 29.4 |
  | `br_gh330.v` | 36 673 | 16 384 | **30 561** | 30 560 | 598.0 |
  | `comp1000.v` | 69 795 | 8 192 | **43 437** | 43 435 | 861.8 |

- **WHY NOTHING SAW IT BEFORE, AND IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT.** Every instrument in `.67` reads a
  HIGH-WATER — the arena census, the owned-heap census, the size-class snapshot, `peak_live`. An
  allocation made and freed between two high-water marks contributes to none of them. The tape is
  the first instrument in this leaf with a TIME AXIS, and this is what a time axis is for.
- ⚠️ **WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE NEXT STEP: THE CALL SITE.** The tape carries
  a size and two event numbers, no backtrace. 8 192 = 1 024 × 8 bytes and 16 384 is its double,
  which READS like one `Vec` per something that grows once — but that is a reading of two numbers,
  not a measurement, and this leaf must not inherit it as a premise (`-0127`: a pre-registration
  inherits the frame of the question it was written in).
- **THE NEXT INSTRUMENT, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INVENTED.** A call-site arm on the counting
  allocator: capture a bounded backtrace (or a `#[track_caller]`-style shim on the suspect
  constructors) for allocations of exactly these sizes, on `br_gh330.v` alone, and report the
  distinct sites with counts. Bounded scope, one input, one size.
- ⛔ **PARKED, NOT ABANDONED.** This is a SPEED question — the bytes are never resident — and speed
  is behind the director's *"thorough and accurate and fast (not reached yet, because it is not the
  focus right now)"* ordering. It is owned here so it cannot be re-found from scratch.
- ⚠️ **DO NOT PRICE IT FROM A TRUNCATED TAPE.** At 2^16 tape entries this same input reported 65 443
  allocations of 8 192 B; the complete run reports 220 773. A truncated tape is a PREFIX of the
  event stream, not a sample of it.

### ⛔ `.76` — **`peak_live` INCLUDES THE PROBE'S OWN COMMAND LINE: THE SAME FILE, PARSED IDENTICALLY, REPORTS A DIFFERENT PEAK DEPENDING ON HOW ITS PATH IS SPELLED** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED behind the SV lane, opened 2026-08-29 by an ORPHANED BACKGROUND JOB's overwrite / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0134`)

- ⛔ **THIS DOES NOT RE-OPEN `.67`.** `.67` is CLOSED and its bound stands: the effect is **~2 bytes
  per path character against a 2.34 MB peak — 0.004 %**, four orders below any published digit. What
  is defective is not the bound but the PROPERTY `peak_live` is relied on for. `MEMORY.md` leans on
  it as the DETERMINISTIC control that distinguishes real signal from RSS noise (`-0128`:
  *"byte-identical across both runs on 11 of 11"*). That determinism is real **only while argv is
  held fixed**, and nothing anywhere says so.
- **HOW IT WAS FOUND, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS FOUND AT ALL.** An orphaned `chain.sh` from a
  dead session (scratchpad `d2751264`, no surviving log) re-ran the `.67`(c)(iii) ladder **without**
  `PGEN_EUS67_TAPE_MIN_BYTES=16384` and overwrote three tracked artifacts at the script's default
  `8192`. The diff moved `peak_live` by **exactly −1 on 11 of 11 rows** while
  `peak_at_event_seq` and `peak_at_alloc_calls` were **identical on 11 of 11** and the extra tape
  events ranged **+28 … +220 797**. ⭐ **A recording perturbation scales with the event count and
  moves the sequence numbers; a constant −1 across an 8 000× range of extra events is an OFFSET.**
  Chasing the −1 instead of explaining it away is the whole finding — cf. `.66`, found the same way.
- ✅ **THE DECISIVE CONTROL — `08192`: the same threshold, one more character.** Run on
  `tmp/eus67/floor.sv`, `--profile sv_2017`:

  | argv value | chars | threshold | `peak_live` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `8192` | 4 | 8192 | 2 344 417 |
  | `16384` | 5 | 16384 | 2 344 418 |
  | `08192` | 5 | **8192** | **2 344 418** |
  | `000008192` | 9 | 8192 | 2 344 422 |
  | `0000000016384` | 13 | 16384 | 2 344 426 |

  `peak_live = 2 344 413 + len(argv_value)`, slope exactly **1 byte per character**. ⭐ **The
  hypothesis *the tape threshold perturbs the parse* is REFUTED, not merely unsupported**: `08192`
  and `16384` are DIFFERENT thresholds with IDENTICAL `peak_live`, while `08192` and `8192` are the
  SAME threshold and differ. The varying quantity is the STRING, not the number.
- ⛔ **AND THE INPUT PATH IS IN THERE TOO, AT TWICE THE RATE** (same file, `--tape-min-bytes 16384`
  held fixed): `tmp/eus67/floor.sv` (18 ch) → 2 344 418 · `./tmp/eus67/floor.sv` (20) → 2 344 422 ·
  `././././tmp/eus67/floor.sv` (26) → 2 344 434 · the absolute path (53) → 2 344 488. Exactly
  **2 bytes per character**, linear over a 35-character span. ⇒ **`peak_live` is not a pure function
  of (input, grammar, profile).** Two consumers are affected in principle: any cross-file comparison
  silently compares path lengths, and any re-run under a different working directory shifts.
- ✅ **THE TERM THAT WAS UNATTRIBUTED IS NOW MEASURED AND THE ACCOUNTING CLOSES (`-0135`, under a
  director re-verification challenge).** As first published this bullet read *"48 bytes are
  unaccounted for … NOT a closed accounting"*, and that was the honest state of it: the arithmetic
  compared a REMOVAL against a rate measured only on a VALUE, so the flag NAME's rate was itself an
  unmeasured term inside the caveat (`-0129`, applied to my own qualification). Measured both
  directions on a fixed input, `--profile sv_2017` held: **ADDING** `--hysteresis-bytes 0`
  (18 + 1 = 19 chars) costs **+67 B**; **REMOVING** `--tape-min-bytes 16384` (16 + 5 = 21 chars)
  saves **−69 B**. `67 − 19 = 48` and `69 − 21 = 48` — **the same constant from two independent
  directions**, so it is a FIXED PER-ARGV-ENTRY overhead of ~24 B (the `Vec<String>` slot) beside
  1 B per character for the string body. ⇒ the model is `peak_live = base + Σ(24 + len(arg))`, it
  reconciles every row measured in this leaf, and *"`peak_live` includes argv"* is now a CLOSED
  accounting rather than a confirmed-in-part one. ⭐ It also explains the 1×/2× asymmetry the first
  cut called unexplained: a flag VALUE varies one String body (1×) while the input PATH is allocated
  TWICE (2×), with no `Vec` growth in either case because the argument COUNT is held fixed.
- ⚠️ **THE ONE LEG THAT IS NOT CURRENTLY REPLAYABLE, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT.** The founding
  observation — `−1` on 11 of 11 rows with `peak_at_event_seq` and `peak_at_alloc_calls` IDENTICAL
  on 11 of 11 — was measured against the orphan's overwritten files, and RESTORING them destroyed
  that second sample. A replay (re-run the ladder at the default `8192` into `tmp/`, diff the meta
  against the committed one) was launched under this challenge and KILLED before completion, because
  the director needed to exit and leaving it running would have recreated the very orphan this leaf
  documents. ⇒ **the 11-of-11 row counts stand as RECORDED, not as RE-DERIVED**; the LAW behind them
  is independently verified above and predicts exactly `−1` for `16384 → 8192` on every row. The
  replay is cheap and is the first thing to run when this leaf is next opened.
- **THE FIX SHAPE, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INVENTED.** Latch the live-bytes counter once, after
  argument parsing and immediately before the parse begins, and report the peak RELATIVE to that
  baseline — i.e. give the instrument an explicit measurement epoch instead of letting process
  startup sit inside the measured region. Cheap, local to `parse_alloc_census_probe.rs`, and it
  makes the reported quantity a function of the parse alone. ⛔ It CHANGES every `peak_live` digit
  by a small constant, so it is a re-baselining and must land with its own re-run, never silently.
- ⛔ **PARKED, NOT ABANDONED.** This is instrument HYGIENE, not parser functionality, and the
  director's ordering ruling of 2026-08-29 (third reaffirmation) puts `.69` ahead of everything in
  this family. Owned here so it cannot be re-found from scratch.

- ✅ **promotion: ACCEPTED** — the measurement lesson is promoted to the retrievable layer as
  [`docs/knowledge/an-instrument-inside-its-own-measurement-window-measures-itself.md`](../knowledge/an-instrument-inside-its-own-measurement-window-measures-itself.md),
  carrying the leading-zero control as a reusable technique and its own honest limit (the 48
  unattributed bytes). `KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md` regenerated: 234 → 235 facts.
- **promotion: declined (the orphaned-background-job trap is recorded in THIS leaf, in `CHANGES.md`
  and in `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md` — all durable — and it is an OPERATING-PROCEDURE fact about
  resuming, not an engineering principle about the parser or its instruments; the knowledge layer
  indexes questions asked of the CODE and the MEASUREMENTS, and a card here would be a fourth copy
  of a one-line habit. ⚠️ Promote it if it recurs: a second occurrence makes it a class, not an
  incident.)**
- **promotion: declined (*a restore is proven by re-deriving the consumer, not by `git restore`
  exiting 0* is a genuine rule, but it is an INSTANCE of the already-promoted
  [[a-control-validates-the-property-it-is-built-from]] — the property being validated is
  "these bytes are the ones the published numbers came from", and byte-identical report
  re-derivation is the control built from exactly that property. A second card would split one
  idea across two entries.)**

### ✅ `.77` — **THE HANDOFF BAR GAINS A THIRD ARM: NO BACKGROUND JOB MAY BE RUNNING WHEN THE WORKSPACE IS DECLARED READY** (`done` 2026-08-30, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0136`; OPS tier, ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes, opened the same day by the director on the evidence of `.76`)

- **THE ORDER, verbatim (director 2026-08-30):** *"From now on as a rule please ensure that at a
  handoff point, that is whenever I am ready to /exit, that there is no background job running."*
  Recorded in layer C as [`feedback_no_background_job_at_a_handoff_point`](../decisions/INDEX.md).
- **WHY IT IS A RULE AND NOT HYGIENE — it has a measured data-loss class behind it.** `.76` was
  opened by exactly this: a `chain.sh` from a session that no longer existed ran **1 h 24 m** past
  its parent and overwrote **three TRACKED artifacts of an already-CLOSED leaf** at a different
  measurement configuration, its log gone with the session. ⛔ **Committing first does not protect
  against it** — the corruption lands AFTER the commit, on files the commit already blessed.
- ✅ **DISCHARGED EXECUTABLY, NOT BY RESOLVE**: `scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh`, exit 0 clean /
  1 with the candidates listed. ⭐ **Kill the CHILDREN too** — measured while adopting this: killing
  the ladder's parent left **two `parse_alloc_census_probe` children running**, so a census of the
  parent alone reports clean while the work continues.
- ⛔ **SCOPED OUT DELIBERATELY: not a doctrine, not in `.githooks/pre-commit`.** A commit may
  legitimately land while a job runs — the pause-signal directive's own rule 3 orders completed work
  committed FIRST and the waiting done after. A commit-blocking form would punish the exact
  behaviour that directive asks for. ⇒ handoff-time operator check, nowhere else.
- ⭐ **THE FIRST CUT REPORTED THE OPERATOR'S UNRELATED PROJECTS, WHICH IS HOW A CENSUS DIES.** It
  matched `cargo (build|test|run)` and `rust/target/…` by command line alone and named two running
  `linkedspec` processes. A candidate is now claimed only if its command line names THIS checkout or
  its own **cwd** is inside it. ⚠️ Consequences, both real and stated rather than discovered later: a
  job whose cwd is elsewhere AND whose command line never spells the repo path is MISSED, and a
  process whose cwd cannot be read is treated as NOT ours.
- ⚠️ **AND ITS OWN CALLER-EXCLUSION HAS A KNOWN SOFT SPOT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE.**
  The ancestry walk that stops it reporting itself **can truncate** when an intermediate shell has
  already exited and the caller is reparented — OBSERVED ONCE (it reported the harness's own wrapper
  shell) and not reproducible afterwards; `EXCLUDE` was then verified correct in situ. ⇒ this script
  and the harness wrapper are ALSO excluded BY NAME, so the guarantee does not rest on the walk.
  Neither exclusion can hide a real project job, which is the property that matters.
- ✅ **BOTH ARMS EXERCISED, because a census that says green to everything is worthless**: RED on a
  real project job spawned under the repo (listed, exit 1), GREEN once it is killed (exit 0), and
  GREEN while two unrelated `linkedspec` builds are running.

##### Acceptance Checklist (enforced) — `.77` (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0136`)

- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — **WHY**: a background job is not bound to the session that
      spawned it, so it keeps writing to TRACKED paths after that session is gone (`.76`: 1 h 24 m
      past its own session, three tracked artifacts of a CLOSED leaf rewritten, log lost with the
      session). **WHERE**: the handoff bar has no arm anywhere in the tracked tree that can see a
      running process — CENSUSED, not asserted, over the population that would refute it (every
      hook, CI workflow, Makefile and the doctrine driver):
      `git ls-files | xargs grep -l 'check_no_background_jobs\|pgrep\|background job'` and
      `grep -rn 'check_no_background_jobs' rust/Makefile Makefile .githooks/ .github/ scripts/check_doctrines.sh | wc -l`
      → **0**, with `make -n -C rust -p | grep -c check_no_background_jobs` → **0**. The clean-tree
      and all-committed arms are both blind to it by construction: a process is not a file.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — before→after ON THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF, same machine state:
      the first cut reported **3 rows** (two unrelated `linkedspec` processes + the script itself);
      after cwd/checkout scoping and the pid-trim fix it reports **0**, and **exactly 1** — the real
      job, alone — with a control job spawned under the repo. `bash -n scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh`
      is clean. RED arm observed firing (exit 1, job listed), GREEN arm observed returning (exit 0)
      once the job and its children are killed.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes, so the cert/corpus/
      ast_shape/clippy oracles cannot move and are untouched by construction. The script is wired
      into **nothing**: `git ls-files` + `make -n` census above reports **0** references from any

  which (a)'s census could not see because `caffeinate` was not in its token list. ⇒ **re-running the
  tool would have confirmed the instrument, never its COVERAGE** — the `.61`(b) lesson, paid again.
- ⛔ **THE DEFECT, WHERE IT LIVED**: `PATTERN=` in `scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh` at
  `4cce8d30` (`git log -S'PATTERN='`). Detection was a HARD-CODED VOCABULARY of project tokens
  (`cargo`, `rust/target/`, the probe names …), so anything not on the list was invisible **by
  construction**. A census assembled from the things you thought of cannot see the thing you did not.
- ✅ **MEASURED BEFORE → AFTER, AT PID LEVEL** (exit codes were REFUSED as evidence: the first attempt
  read `OLD exit=1` and looked like a catch, but that 1 was a FALSE POSITIVE — the harness wrapper
  matching `${REPO_ROOT}` from my own command text — while the advisory section was suppressed by the
  blocking row. Comparing exit codes conflates a hit with a false alarm):

  | version | control job `14598` (`sleep 40`, 2 open repo handles, NO project token in its cmdline) | quiet state |
  |---|---|---|
  | OLD (vocabulary) | reports **nothing** — MISSED | reports 1 "STILL RUNNING" — FALSE POSITIVE |

- ⭐ **THE REPLACEMENT IS A PROPERTY, NOT A LIST** — one `lsof -u <uid> -Fpfn` call (0.5 s):
  an **OPEN HANDLE** under the repo (any fd, `txt` included, so a running project binary counts) or a
  command line naming this checkout ⇒ **PROJECT WORK, blocking**; **cwd** under the repo with **zero**
  handles ⇒ **ADVISORY, non-blocking**. ⭐⭐ The cwd/handle split is what stops it crying wolf and it
  is PRINCIPLED rather than an allowlist: **cwd is INHERITED**, so every shell and helper a session
  spawns has one, while a process actually doing project work holds a FILE. Measured: `caffeinate`
  reports `fd=cwd` and **0** handles.
- ⚠️ **WHAT IS STILL NOT SEEN, stated rather than left to be discovered**: the census covers THIS uid,
  so a project job running as another user is invisible; and a process that has finished its writes,
  closed every handle, has a cwd outside the repo and names no repo path in its command line is
  invisible to both arms. ⚠️ A transient child of the caller's own pipeline can appear as an ADVISORY
  row (observed: a `tr` from the measurement itself) — advisory never blocks, so it is noise, not a
  false alarm.

### ⛔⛔ `.78` — **THREE `embedding_api` CEILING TESTS STILL ENCODE THE PRE-`.65` CEILING AND HAVE BEEN RED SINCE `-0117`: 400 NESTED PARENS IS NO LONGER "OVER-CEILING"** (`todo`, opened 2026-08-30 by `.69`(d)'s own no-regression run / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0138`)

- **WHY + WHERE**: `.65` (`-0117`, `56c9d24c`, 2026-08-28 17:59) replaced the fixed **4 096-frame**
  ceiling with a bound derived from the host's stack. Three tests in `rust/src/embedding_api.rs` were
  written against the old number and were NOT updated with it:
  - `:3444` `parser_embedding_systemverilog_over_ceiling_nesting_fails_in_bounded_time` — asserts
    `400` nested parens is REJECTED. **Measured: `400` now ACCEPTS** (debug, default reservation,
    2.58 s, `stack_probe: no_refusal`). Failure text: *"over-ceiling nesting must be rejected, not
    accepted — left: Success, right: Failure"*.
  - `:3498` `parser_embedding_over_ceiling_diagnostic_names_the_recursion_ceiling` — same `400`
    input, asserts a diagnostic is present; there is none, because the parse SUCCEEDS.
  - `:3315` `parser_embedding_systemverilog_deep_nesting_yields_clean_diagnostic_not_process_abort` —
    `2 000` parens × two profiles against `DEEP_NESTING_WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET = 1800 s`. **Measured
    2 920.7 s.** The budget was calibrated when the ceiling was 4 096 frames; `.65` moved the ceiling
    to ~**9 726** frames in debug, so the parse descends far further before refusing — the book
    already records the release form of this (*"37.7 s where it refused in 0.19 s"*).
- ⚠️ **"RED SINCE `-0117`" IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A MEASUREMENT — labelled as such under the same-day
  re-verification challenge.** The suite was NOT run at `56c9d24c`. What IS measured: the `repeat(400)`
  literal was last touched by `-0110` and the `from_secs(1800)` budget by `-0081`, both BEFORE `.65`;
  `-0117` DID modify `rust/src/embedding_api.rs` and left both alone; and frames-per-paren is
  **12.91 … 13.45** (bisected), so 400 parens is **≥ 5 164** frames — comfortably past the OLD 4 096
  ceiling and comfortably short of the new ~9 700. The mechanism therefore predicts a flip exactly at
  `.65`, but the flip itself was not observed at that commit.
- ⇒ **ONE root cause, three symptoms**: the tests pin a CONSTANT the engine no longer has. The
  ceiling now fires between **600** (accept, 5.7 s) and **800** (reject at 9 726 frames, 21.8 s)
  parens in debug at the default reservation.
- ⛔ **WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED FOR TWO DAYS**: the full library suite is not in the ordinary-commit CI
  tier (director CI policy, directive 16 — ordinary commits run a selected set), and no gate in the
  commit path runs `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers`. `make -C rust embedding_api`
  exists (`rust/Makefile:1992`) but nothing in the commit flow invokes it.
- ✅ **NOT CAUSED BY `-0138`, PROVEN BY A/B ON PRESERVED BINARIES, NOT BY ARGUMENT.** The debug

  before the rebuild overwrote it. Same inputs, same reservation, same host:

  | binary | 600 parens | 800 parens | 300 parens at the 96 MiB floor |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | PRE (`-0138` absent) | rc 0, 5.69 s | rc 1, 9 726 frames, 21.76 s | rc 134, stack overflow |
  | POST (`-0138`) | rc 0, 5.66 s | rc 1, 9 726 frames, 21.43 s | rc 134, stack overflow |

  Identical verdicts, identical refusal depth, identical timings. `-0138` is verdict-neutral by
  construction too — all five `return false` arms of `extend_depth_probe` map 1:1 onto `refuse(…)`,

- **OWES**: re-derive each test's input depth and time budget FROM the reservation instead of pinning

#### ✅ `.78` DONE — **THE CEILING LOCKS NOW *MEASURE* THE CEILING INSTEAD OF ASSERTING WHERE IT IS, AND THE FIRST RUN REFUTED AN ARM I HAD WRITTEN FROM AN ENUM RATHER THAN FROM DATA** (2026-08-30, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0140`; TEST tier, ZERO engine / grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

- **WHAT WAS DONE**: all three RED locks, plus the VHDL twin that shared their deleted constants,
  now derive their input depth from a ladder that climbs until `.69`(d)'s depth probe refuses on
  STACK grounds, and their wall-clock budget from `dedicated_parse_stack_bytes()`. Evidence:
  `docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/eus78_ceiling_locks/`.
- ⭐⭐ **THE RUN REFUTED A DESIGN ARM, AND THE ARM WAS MINE.** The ladder's stop condition accepts
  BOTH stack-grounds causes (`BudgetExhausted`, `NoFrameAffordable`). I wrote that from `.69`(d)'s
  enum, defensively, with no instance of the second in hand. Measured: **`Verilog2005` really does
  refuse with `NoFrameAffordable`** (depth 8 668, `used` 251 643 616 B **under** a 251 658 240 B
  budget by 14 624 B = 0.50 frames). Had I taken only `BudgetExhausted` — the cause `.69`(d) itself
  calls *"the ONLY refusal that is a fact about the STACK"* — that ladder would have read its own
  crossing as a non-event and climbed to the 2 048 s hang detector. ⇒ **`.69`(d)'s sentence is true
  about which cause is the cleanest evidence and false as a stop condition; a doc's emphasis is not
  a specification.**
- ✅ **THAT *"WOULD HAVE CLIMBED TO THE HANG DETECTOR"* WAS AN INFERENCE WHEN PUBLISHED; IT IS NOW
  MEASURED** (director re-verification challenge, same day, `-0141`). The open question was whether
  some deeper rung might flip `verilog_2005` to `BudgetExhausted` and let the narrow stop condition
  terminate after all. It does not — the debug probe at three depths returns BYTE-IDENTICAL readings:

  | parens | cause | refusal depth | `used_bytes` | B/frame |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2 048 | `NoFrameAffordable` | 8 668 | 251 651 424 | 29 032 |
  | 4 096 | `NoFrameAffordable` | 8 668 | 251 651 424 | 29 032 |
  | 8 192 | `NoFrameAffordable` | 8 668 | 251 651 424 | 29 032 |

  ⭐ **The mechanism is why, and it generalises**: the refusal depth is `budget / bytes_per_frame` —
  a function of the RESERVATION and the shape, **not of the input's depth**. Past the crossing every
  deeper input refuses at the same frame with the same cause, so the cause is INVARIANT in input
  depth and a `BudgetExhausted`-only ladder would have climbed until the clock stopped it.
  ⚠️ Two wording corrections from the same challenge: the outcome is a lock that FAILS after
  ~2 048 s, not a hang (`require_crossing()` panics naming the budget); and the probe reads
  `used_bytes` **251 651 424** (6 816 B under budget, 0.23 frames), where this leaf first wrote
  251 643 616 / 14 624 B from the in-test observation — the same cause, a different sample.
- ⭐⭐ **AND THE TWO PROFILES OF ONE FAMILY DISAGREE, WHICH IS WHY NO SINGLE LITERAL COULD HAVE
  WORKED**: `Sv2017` crosses at **1 024** levels / **9.70** frames per level / `BudgetExhausted`,
  `Verilog2005` at **2 048** / **4.23** / `NoFrameAffordable`. The deleted locks used ONE pinned
  depth for both, and for VHDL as well.
- ⛔ **VHDL'S ARM DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REQUIRE A CROSSING, and that is a measurement, not caution.**
  Debug probe, default reservation: VHDL accepts **2 000** parens in **17.4 s** and **4 000** in
  **72.4 s**, both `stack_probe: no_refusal`. Its per-level stack cost is ≥ **5.4×** cheaper than
  SystemVerilog's, so at ≈4× per doubling a ladder chasing its ceiling would spend **~1 645 s** to
  give up — more than half of what this leaf exists to remove. `.79`(a) records VHDL's per-frame
  cost as UNMEASURED, so demanding a crossing would assert a quantity nobody has measured, which is
  the move that created these stale literals. Its arm locks `1.3.1`'s per-rung contract instead —
  *a structured verdict, never a SIGABRT* — which holds however far the ladder got, so the smaller
  cap cannot make it wrongly pass.
- ⭐ **THE BUDGET IS SEEDED FROM THE RIGHT DISTRIBUTION, WHICH IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE.** Rung costs
  0.056 / 0.116 / 0.330 / 1.109 / 4.093 s grow ≈3.3–3.9× per doubling; the REJECTING rung costs
  **201.469 s — 46×** its predecessor, because crossing makes the enclosing alternatives re-explore
  (`.68`'s Θ(depth²), the "cost is quadratic in depth" bound the SV contract already publishes).
  ⇒ a budget sized from the accepting rungs would have been sized from the wrong distribution. It is
  seeded from the whole ladder (**207.17 s ⇒ 0.835 s per reserved MiB**) at **8 s/MiB ≈ 10×**.
- ⭐ **A PLAIN `elapsed >= budget` CAP AUTHORISES ≈4× WHAT IT SAYS**, because it is checked only
  between rungs and each rung costs ≈4× the last. The ladder now predicts the next rung from the
  growth IT HAS OBSERVED and stops before buying one it cannot afford: VHDL ended at **99.99 s**
  against a 256 s cap because its own 74.648/18.817 = **3.97×** put the next rung at 296 s. A raw cap
  would have spent **396 s** for the same answer. Reproduced on the independent RED-control run to
  **0.23 %** / **0.63 %**.
- **ACCEPTANCE**: see the checklist below. ⚠️ **HONEST BOUNDS, stated not implied.** (1) The budgets
  scale LINEARLY with the reservation and that is assumed, not measured — the slack covers
  reservations near the default, and one orders of magnitude larger needs re-measuring. (2) Like
  `.43`'s, the budget is checked BETWEEN rungs, so a parse that truly never returns still hangs the
  rung it is in; nothing here can interrupt a running parse. (3) No gate in the commit path runs this
  suite — that half of `.78`'s WHY is NOT closed here and is called out under `.80` below.

  comparison. The depth sweep exists because of that, and it is what found the abort. ⇒ **a ladder
  that chooses its own stopping point is not a controlled variable**, and comparing across a
  parameter with such a ladder compares two things at once.

  parser is being LRM-faithful, which is the north star's *over-acceptance is a defect* holding on

- **WHAT (a) STILL OWES**, unchanged by this slice: the host-derived default itself, (b) the ruling
  on querying an arbitrary embedder thread's extent, and (c) pricing `libc` as a direct dependency.

  and the margin shrinks with the reservation, so **deriving the default without also fixing the
  stride would move small hosts toward the edge.** `.85` must land first or with it.

  and the depth of the first sample are BOTH linear in it, and their RATIO — the safety margin — is

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE ARITHMETIC IS CONFIRMED, NOT MERELY THE VERDICT.** `budget ÷ bytes_per_frame` at the
  floor is `94 371 840 ÷ 25 874` = **3 647.4** frames, and the 300-level rung refuses at **3 647**.
  The ceiling really is the quantity the module says it is.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE 128 MiB ROW IS THE STRONGEST NO-REGRESSION ARM AND IT WAS NOT THE ONE I SET OUT TO
  PRODUCE.** There the first sample HALVES (4 096 → 2 048) and **every refusal depth is unchanged to
  the frame**. The reason is structural: the probe's terminal condition is `used >= budget` (or no
  whole frame affordable), which does not mention the starting threshold at all — the self-measuring
  loop converges to `budget ÷ bytes_per_frame` from wherever it starts. ⇒ **sampling earlier costs
  nothing and moves nothing**; it only changes how many `#[cold]` probe calls happen on the way.
- ⚠️⚠️ **THE HONEST COST, PUBLISHED RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A READER TO FIND: AT THE FLOOR THE FIX
  TRADES A 0.53 s CRASH FOR A 2.5–197 s CORRECT ANSWER.** An abort short-circuits everything; a
  refusal is backtracked and the enclosing alternatives re-explore, which is `.68`'s Θ(depth²) scan.
  This is not new cost introduced here — it is the cost the shipped default already pays at its own
  ceiling (the 256 MiB row's 800-level rung costs 20.96 s) — but at a REDUCED reservation the ceiling
  is met earlier, leaving more input to re-explore, so the same shape costs more. ⇒ **an operator who
  lowers `PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES` to save memory buys a slower rejection, not a cheaper one.** The
  trade is still unambiguously right — an uncatchable `SIGABRT` is never an acceptable answer, and
  `.43`'s hang detector plus `.68` own the cost — but it is a trade and it is named here.

  sample from the reservation, and left (a) — the per-family / per-profile / per-build-mode per-frame
  census — open, because the fix's argument (*a byte floor can only be right for one triple*) was
  asserted from ONE family. This slice measures the population in DEBUG and turns that argument into
  a table. ⛔ RELEASE is NOT in this slice and (a) stays open; see the residual below.
- ⭐ **THE INSTRUMENT, and it is the deliverable as much as the numbers are.**
  `docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/eus79a_per_frame_census/` holds a per-family
  deep-nesting generator and a doubling ladder that climbs until the depth probe refuses on STACK
  grounds, reporting the probe's own `bytes_per_frame`. It runs at the **96 MiB floor** on purpose:
  since (b)(c) the ceiling is proportional to the reservation and crossing cost is quadratic in
  source depth (`.68`), so the floor reaches each family's ceiling far more cheaply than the default
  — while the measured quantity is reservation-INDEPENDENT.
- ✅ **THE CENSUS** (debug, `PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES=100663296`), ordered by cost:

  | family / profile | frames at refusal | cause | B/frame | 4 096 frames cost | margin at the 256 MiB default |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `systemverilog` / `verilog_2005` | 3 248 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **29 046** | 113.46 MiB | **2.12×** |
  | `systemverilog` / `sv_2023` | 3 790 | `BudgetExhausted` | **24 903** | 97.28 MiB | 2.47× |
  | `systemverilog` / `sv_2017` | 3 843 | `BudgetExhausted` | **24 559** | 95.93 MiB | 2.50× |
  | `systemverilog_preprocessor` | 18 020 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **5 236** | 20.45 MiB | 11.73× |
  | `return_annotation` | 19 522 | `BudgetExhausted` | **4 998** | 19.52 MiB | 12.29× |
  | `json` | 32 738 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **2 882** | 11.26 MiB | 21.32× |
  | `semantic_annotation` | 34 766 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **2 714** | 10.60 MiB | 22.64× |
  | `rtl_frontend` | 47 878 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **1 971** | 7.70 MiB | 31.17× |
  | `rtl_const_expr` | 48 120 | `NoFrameAffordable` | **1 961** | 7.66 MiB | 31.33× |

  Margin = `budget ÷ (4 096 × B/frame)` with `budget` = 240 MiB, the spendable share of the shipped
  256 MiB default.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **WHAT IT DECIDES.** (1) **The spread is 14.81×** (1 961 → 29 046), so a byte floor derived
  from ANY single family is wrong for another by more than an order of magnitude — (b)(c)'s design
  argument, now measured rather than reasoned. (2) **The tightest margin at the shipped default is
  2.12×**, and **SystemVerilog is the ONLY family under 11×** — the next-nearest is 5.5× further
  away. ⇒ the default is safe for every measured family, SystemVerilog is the binding case, and
  `.79`'s earlier worry — *"a family whose debug frames cost more than 60 KiB (61 440 B) would reach
  its first sample too late"* — is answered: **the worst measured cost is 29 046 B, less than half

    rather than timing out, so it is cheaper in TIME than the paren shape and still does not reach
    the ceiling. ⇒ the gap is not the cap alone: VHDL's ceiling genuinely sits past 4 096 levels of
    the densest shape tried, so slice 2 needs either a construct with materially more frames per
    source level or a reservation below the 96 MiB floor — and the floor forbids the latter, which is
    the first place that floor has actively BOUNDED a measurement. Owed by `.79`(a) slice 2.

  and the quadratically more expensive that cell is.** Release frames cost ≈8–10× less than debug

### ✅✅✅ `.85` — **THE GUARD *PREDICTED* STACK SAFETY AT A SUBSET OF FRAME PUSHES INSTEAD OF OBSERVING IT, SO A SHAPE WHOSE FRAMES OUTRAN THE PREDICTION RAN PAST THE WHOLE RESERVATION — THE SHIPPED RELEASE PARSER HARD-ABORTED ON A 15 400-BYTE SYSTEMVERILOG FILE AT THE SHIPPED DEFAULT (DEBUG: 2 344 B)** (`done` 2026-08-31 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0154` — the trigger is now a STACK-ADDRESS OBSERVATION; every `rc 134` is gone at both reservations and the ACCEPT SET WIDENED. **SV LANE — worked, not parked**; opened the same day by `.69`(a) slice 1 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0152`)

- **WHY + WHERE (tool-backed, and the tool ran before any source was read).**
  `RecursionGuard::extend_depth_probe`, `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs` (the `max_depth` assignment
  at the end of the function):

  ```rust
  let bytes_per_frame = used / depth;                  // AVERAGE over every frame so far
  let affordable = (budget - used) / bytes_per_frame;
  self.max_depth = depth.saturating_add((affordable / STACK_HEADROOM_STRIDE_DIVISOR).max(1));
  ```

  The guard is consulted only when the live depth reaches `max_depth`. Between two samples the parse
  may push `affordable / 4` frames (`STACK_HEADROOM_STRIDE_DIVISOR = 4`,
  `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:2841`), and those frames are priced at the **running average**. If
  the frames the parse is ABOUT to push cost more than that average, the stride is under-priced and
  nothing re-checks until `max_depth` — so the parse can pass the budget, spend the entire 6.25 %
  reserve, and run off the end of the reservation into the guard page.
  ⇒ **the reserve must absorb `stride × (worst frame cost − average frame cost)`, and nothing in the
  derivation bounds that term.**
- ✅ **MEASURED — the abort, at the SHIPPED 256 MiB default, debug probe, `--profile sv_2017`**
  (`…/eus69a_overshoot_census/depth_sweep_pattern.txt`). Shape: nested assignment patterns,
  `module m; localparam p = '{'{'{ … 1 … }}}; endmodule`:

  | levels | input | rc | overshoot | margin |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 512 | 1 560 B | 0 | 5 069 536 B | 3.31× |
  | 576 | 1 752 B | 0 | 8 760 736 B | 1.92× |
  | 640 | 1 944 B | 0 | 12 397 744 B | 1.35× |
  | 704 | 2 136 B | 0 | 16 038 480 B | 1.05× |
  | **768** | **2 344 B** | **134** | — | **SIGABRT past the reservation** |
  | 832, 1024 | — | 134 | — | SIGABRT |

  ⭐ The margin degrades SMOOTHLY and then the process dies — it does not refuse, it aborts. At the
  **documented 96 MiB floor** the same shape aborts from **288 levels (904 B)**, nine of twelve swept
  depths.
- ✅ **REPRODUCIBLE, AND WITHOUT THE INSTRUMENT.** The 768-level input was re-run **three times** with
  NO environment override at all — the plain shipped default, the plain shipped profile, outside the
  census harness — and aborted **3 of 3** (`Abort trap: 6`, `rc 134`, pids 80136 / 86213 / 99099).
  The reproduction is one command on a tracked 2 344-byte input, not a property of the ladder that
  found it.
- ⛔⛔⛔ **SCOPE — THE SHIPPED RELEASE ARTIFACT ABORTS. THIS IS NOT DEBUG-ONLY.** Re-run with a cap
  sized for `.68`'s quadratic crossing (2 700 s instead of 900 s), the **RELEASE** probe at the
  **shipped 256 MiB default** on **5 120 levels — a 15 400-byte file — dies with `rc 134`** after
  **2 606 s**. Debug aborts at 768 levels (2 344 B) at the same default, and from 288 levels (904 B)
  at the documented floor.
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE FIRST READING OF THAT ROW WAS A TIMEOUT THAT MASKED THE ABORT — THE SAME TRAP
  `-0138` PAID FOR AND LAYER A ALREADY RECORDS.** At a 900 s cap the 5 120 / 6 144 / 8 192 rungs read
  `rc 124` and the honest status was UNRESOLVED; at 2 700 s the same input returns `rc 134`. ⇒ **a
  timeout bounds your patience, never the program** → [[contacting-a-limit-is-not-the-same-as-being-stopped-by-it]].
  ⭐ The caution held where it mattered — those rungs were published as UNRESOLVED and never as
  *"release is safe"* — but the cost of the wrong cap was that a SHIPPED-ARTIFACT abort spent one
  commit looking like a debug-only defect.
- ⚠️ **PROVENANCE OF THE RELEASE ROW, said plainly**: it is **ONE** observation at the time of
  writing (memory-guard marker `guard.82292`, elapsed 2 606 s, peak 5 333 MB). A two-run
  reproduction plus a narrowing sweep for a SMALLER release-aborting input is in flight; until it
  lands this row is single-observation and is labelled so rather than counted as replicated.
- ⛔ **WHY THIS IS NOT `.79` AGAIN.** `.79`(b)(c) fixed the guard's FIRST SAMPLE being unreachable —
  the parse aborted before the guard ever got to ask. Here the guard asks, answers correctly, sets
  its next sample point, and **the parse dies before reaching it**. Same symptom (`rc 134`),
  different mechanism, and `.79`'s fix cannot see it: `-0142` published *"the abort is gone at every
  reservation"*, which was true of the mechanism it measured and is **not true of this one**.
  ⇒ **a fix verified against the shape that motivated it is verified against that shape.**
- **OWES**: ✅ **(a) ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS YES** — the shipped release artifact aborts at
  5 120 levels / 15 400 B; what remains under (a) is the reproduction count and the smallest
  release-aborting input, both in flight; **(b)** fix the stride. The shape of the fix is
  already visible and cheap: the probe has two consecutive samples, so the **MARGINAL** per-frame
  cost over the last stride (`(used − used_prev) / (depth − depth_prev)`) is available for free and
  is exactly what the average hides — price the stride on the worst marginal cost seen so far rather
  than on the mean; **(c)** decide whether the stride divisor should also be bounded in BYTES so a
  single stride can never exceed the reserve, which is the invariant the reserve was supposed to
  have; **(d)** a REGRESSION LOCK on this input, since nothing in the tree would have caught it —
  `.80` already records that the ordinary-commit tier runs no `cargo test` at all.
- ⛔⛔ **NOT PARKED, and the lane lock is the reason rather than an exception to it.** This is
  SystemVerilog, on the shipped default reservation, and it is a hard process abort on syntactically
  valid input — the failure class [[project_rtl_parsers_accept_any_rtl_no_limits_non_negotiable]]
  exists to forbid. It is the SV lane's next action.

#### ✅✅✅ `.85` FIXED — **THE TRIGGER IS NOW AN OBSERVATION, NOT A PREDICTION: EVERY `rc 134` IS GONE AT BOTH RESERVATIONS AND THE ACCEPT SET WIDENED** (2026-08-31, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0154`; ENGINE tier, ZERO grammar / codegen / generated bytes — **MEASURED, not asserted**)

- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE ROOT CAUSE, restated after the fix because the first wording was directionally right and
  imprecise.** The guard did not have a bad estimate; it had an ESTIMATE AT ALL. Two independent
  weaknesses compose, and both are the same disease:
  1. **The trigger was a DEPTH counter, not a stack test.** `stride = affordable / STRIDE_DIVISOR`,
     priced from the running AVERAGE `used / depth`. Closed form, no unknowns: a parse can consume
     its whole remaining budget inside ONE stride exactly when the frames it really pushes cost
     `STRIDE_DIVISOR` (= 4) times the average that priced them.
  2. **The trigger was evaluated only inside `check_cycle_id`.** `enter_id_bare` pushes a frame and
     consults nothing — **106 distinct rules** in the shipped SV parser, including the core
     expression chain (`CONSTANT_PRIMARY`, `EXPRESSION_OPERAND`, `CONDITIONAL_EXPRESSION`,
     `ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN_KEY`).
  ✅ **AND WHICH ONE DOMINATES *IS* NOW ESTABLISHED — the opposite way round from this leaf's first
  emphasis.** Measured with `--dump-rule-outcome-counts-json` on the aborting shape (`pattern`, 64
  levels, `--profile sv_2017`): of **44 259** rule entries only **2 615 — 5.9 %** are in
  bare-entered rules, and the eight highest-entry rules are ALL paired (`trivia` 9 745,
  `non_keyword_identifier` 2 152, `declaration_identifier` 1 110, …), i.e. the guard IS consulted on
  them. ⇒ **(2) is real but NOT the operative mechanism for this shape; (1) is.** The guard's trigger
  is evaluated on ~94 % of entries and still lets the parse run far past the budget, because what it
  evaluates between samples is a PREDICTED depth rather than the stack.
  ⛔ **This corrects the emphasis this leaf was first written with** — the bare-entry census (106
  rules, the core expression chain among them) is a true observation that invited a false weighting,
  and the entry counts are what settle it. The fix removes BOTH regardless, which is why it did not
  have to wait for this number.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FIX DELETES THE ESTIMATE RATHER THAN IMPROVING IT** — the same move `.79`(b)(c) made
  when it deleted a byte floor instead of recomputing one. The guard now carries `stack_floor`, the
  ADDRESS below which the budget is gone, learned once on the parse thread inside the probe that
  already reads the extent; the trigger becomes
  `len() >= max_depth || stack_floor_breached()`. ⇒ the overshoot is bounded by the frames between
  two guard-visible entries instead of by one mispriced stride, and per-frame cost — average,
  marginal or otherwise — leaves the safety argument entirely. `max_depth` survives ONLY as the
  fallback for a thread whose extent the process cannot know, which is exactly `-0144`'s rule.
  ⛔ **A first cut tracked the WORST MARGINAL per-frame cost and clamped the stride against the
  reserve. It was reverted, not layered**: it made the prediction conservative while keeping the
  predictive structure, and leaving it under the address test would strand dead estimation machinery
  in the safety path that a later reader would reasonably think was load-bearing.
- ✅ **BEFORE → AFTER, `pattern`, debug** (`…/eus69a_overshoot_census/depth_sweep_pattern_AFTER.txt`):

  | reservation | levels | BEFORE | AFTER |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 96 MiB floor | 192 / 224 / 256 | `rc 0` at 3.20× / 1.64× / **1.10×** | `rc 0` at 1013× / 272× / 356× |
  | 96 MiB floor | 288 … 448 | **`rc 134` SIGABRT** | **`rc 0`** — they now ACCEPT |
  | 96 MiB floor | 512 … 1024 | **`rc 134` SIGABRT** | **`rc 1`** — clean rejection |
  | 256 MiB default | 512 … 704 | `rc 0` at 3.31× … **1.05×** | `rc 0` at 11 155× … 14 364× |
  | 256 MiB default | 768 / 832 / 1024 | **`rc 134` SIGABRT** | **`rc 0`** — they now ACCEPT |

  ⭐⭐ **THE ACCEPT SET WIDENED RATHER THAN NARROWED**, which is the arm that mattered most: a guard

      highest-entry rules all PAIRED ⇒ the guard is consulted on ~94 % of entries, so the defect is
      the PREDICTED THRESHOLD and not the `enter_id_bare` bypass, which is real but secondary here.
      Closed-form corroboration: crossing the budget within one stride requires marginal ≥
      `STRIDE_DIVISOR` × average; measured, `pattern` travelled **244.8** frames past budget against
      `paren`'s **0.6** on averages 1.05× apart. Captured under the memory guard
      (`guard.95947.marker`, `reason=none`).

### ✅✅ `.87` — **THE CEILING TESTS READ THE PROCESS-WIDE RESERVATION INSTEAD OF PINNING ONE, SO THEIR COVERAGE *AND* THEIR RUNTIME ARE FUNCTIONS OF THE HOST — WHICH IS WHY `.69`(a) HAD TO CAP THE HALF OF THE CAPABILITY MANDATE THAT SAYS A BIGGER HOST ACCEPTS DEEPER INPUT** (`in progress` — ✅✅ **(b) + (c) DONE 2026-08-31 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0159`: the reservation is PINNED, the suite went 316 s → 88 s with one MORE test, and the pin bought a control that was previously unaffordable**; ✅✅✅ **(d) DONE 2026-08-31 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0160`: the clamp is GONE, a 24 GiB host goes 4 813 -> 7 211 accepted nested casts, and the linearity is measured ABOVE the reference for the first time — to 0.010 %**; (e) WITHDRAWN, (f) REROUTED to `.86`(c); ⚠️ (a) DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION — it asked for the ladder's cost at a raised reservation on an idle host, and (b)'s pin removed the host from that cost entirely, so the question no longer has a subject; opened 2026-08-31 by `.69`(a) slice 2 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0157`)

- **WHY + WHERE (established BEFORE the fix it blocks was written, by reading the two tests the
  census named rather than by running into them).** Three sites read
  `dedicated_parse_stack_bytes()` — the process-wide resolved reservation — and derive a test
  parameter from it:

  ```
  git grep -n "dedicated_parse_stack_bytes()" -- rust/src
    -> rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:7108        the terminal-refusal burn test
       rust/src/embedding_api.rs:3579           ceiling_budget_from_reservation (.78)
       rust/src/embedding_api.rs:{3651,3813,3880,4082}  the .78 ceiling ladder arms
  ```

  Until `.69`(a) that number was a LITERAL, so "process-wide" and "known constant" were the same
  thing and reading it was harmless. `.69`(a) makes it a function of the host's physical memory,
  and the two properties come apart.
- ⛔⛔ **CONSEQUENCE 1 — AN EXISTING LOCK GOES VACUOUS, SILENTLY AND IN THE GREEN DIRECTION.**
  `stack_probe_names_the_terminal_refusal_after_a_real_spend` burns `budget/2 + budget/8` of the
  resolved reservation to reach `NoFrameAffordable`, and skips when that exceeds
  `MAX_SAFE_BURN_BYTES = 200 MiB` — a guard written for *"an operator set a big
  `PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES`"*. Arithmetic, deterministic:

  | reservation | `budget/2 + budget/8` | vs the 200 MiB cap | the test |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 256 MiB (the reference) | 150 MiB | under | **runs its body** |
  | 384 MiB (this 24 GiB host, uncapped) | 225 MiB | over | **skips, and stays GREEN** |

  ⇒ an uncapped derivation would have made this lock vacuous on **every host above 16 GiB**, with
  no signal. That is the `.80`/`.86` shape — a gate honestly green about a population that
  excludes the case it exists to cover — reached this time not by a stale identity set but by a
  constant becoming a variable underneath a test that assumed it could not.
  ⚠️ **The vacuity is PRE-EXISTING, not created by `.69`(a)**: any operator setting
  `PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES` above ~341 MiB already skips it today. `.69`(a) would have moved it
  from "a thing an operator can do" to "a thing most hosts do by default", which is a different
  severity, not a different defect.
- ⛔⛔ **CONSEQUENCE 2 — THE `.78` CEILING LADDER'S RUNTIME BECOMES A FUNCTION OF THE CI HOST'S
  RAM, AND IT IS QUADRATIC.** The ladder doubles its nesting depth until the ceiling refuses. The
  ceiling sits at `budget ÷ bytes_per_frame` frames, so it moves with the reservation, and
  crossing cost is Θ(depth²) (`.68`) — `.78`'s own rung table measures the rejecting rung at
  **46×** its predecessor rather than the ≈4× the accepting rungs show. Derived from the measured
  numbers `.78` and `-0138` already record (debug, `sv_2017`, 25 335 B/frame, ≈12.2 frames per
  nesting level):

  | reservation | budget | ceiling ≈ frames | ≈ crossing level | first ladder rung that crosses |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 256 MiB | 240 MiB | ≈ 9 930 | ≈ 814 | **1 024** (measured: 207.5 s, ladder total 213.7 s) |
  | 384 MiB | 360 MiB | ≈ 14 900 | ≈ 1 221 | **2 048** — one doubling deeper |

  `.78` already DERIVES its wall-clock budget from the reservation (8 s per reserved MiB), so the
  arm would stay green — it would just cost a multiple of what it costs today, scaling with
  whatever RAM the runner happens to have. ⚠️ **The crossing-level and rung columns are ARITHMETIC
  over measured per-frame costs, not a timed run.** They were deliberately NOT timed: the host was
  at load 4.3 with an unrelated `rustc` running, and a wall-clock number taken there is indicative
  only (layer A). Timing it on an idle host is this leaf's own first job, precisely so the fix is
  sized against a measurement rather than against this estimate.
