#### ✅✅ `.87`(b) + (c) DONE — **PINNING THE RESERVATION DID NOT COST RUNTIME TO BUY RIGOUR; IT BOUGHT BOTH, BECAUSE CROSSING COST IS Θ(depth²) AND DEPTH IS LINEAR IN THE RESERVATION** (2026-08-31, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0159`; TEST tier, ZERO grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

- **WHY + WHERE (tool-backed, the census ran before any edit).** `git grep -n
  "dedicated_parse_stack_bytes()" -- rust/src` named three consumers that turn the process-wide
  reservation into a TEST PARAMETER: the terminal-refusal burn test
  (`ast_pipeline/mod.rs:7108`) and the `.78` ceiling ladder's budget + arms
  (`embedding_api.rs:3579,3651,3813,3880,4082`). While that number was a LITERAL, "process-wide"
  and "known constant" were the same thing and reading it was harmless. `.69`(a) made it a
  function of host physical memory and the two came apart.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE MECHANISM COST NOTHING TO BUILD BECAUSE THE MODULE ALREADY HAD IT.** A caller already
  on a dedicated parse stack runs INLINE, and the inline path deliberately never touches
  `PARSE_STACK_EXTENT` — verified in source before building on it. So wrapping a whole ladder in
  ONE `run_on_dedicated_parse_stack_with_reservation` makes every nested `parse_grammar_profile`
  inherit the pinned extent: **no parse entry point changes, no reservation threaded through the
  embedding API, ZERO generated bytes.**
- ✅ **MEASURED, and it is the opposite of the trade I expected to have to defend** (wall clock on
  a host at load ≈3.5 ⇒ INDICATIVE, but the ratios are far outside noise and are mechanistically
  explained):

  | suite configuration | tests | wall clock |
  |---|---|---|
  | before — ladder at the resolved default, host-dependent | 1 126 | **316 s** |
  | (b)+(c) pinned at the 96 MiB floor | 1 126 | **109 s** |
  | + proportionality control, pair taken UPWARD (96 → 192 MiB) | 1 127 | **454 s** |
  | **+ proportionality control, pair taken DOWNWARD (48 → 96 MiB)** | **1 127** | **88 s** |

  ⇒ **3.6× faster with one MORE test than before.** Depth is linear in the reservation and
  crossing is Θ(depth²) (`.68`), so pinning at the floor pays ≈(96/256)² ≈ 0.14×. Rigour was not
  paid for with runtime here; controlling the variable was the cheaper option all along.
- ⛔⛔ **AND THE DIRECTION OF THE PROPORTIONALITY PAIR IS A MEASURED DECISION, NOT A PREFERENCE.**
  The first cut compared (pin, 2×pin) and cost **+345 s** — a suite SLOWER than the
  host-dependent one it replaced, which would have been a bad trade shipped quietly. Taking the
  pair DOWNWARD (½pin, pin) makes the expensive arm the one the other ceiling locks already run
  and CACHE, so the marginal cost is the cheap ladder alone, and the ratio under test is
  identical. ⚠️ The smaller arm sits below `MIN_DEDICATED_PARSE_STACK_BYTES` deliberately: `.79`
  re-cast that floor as *"a policy, not a proof"*, the explicit runner applies no floor by
  design, and `.79`(b)(c) makes the first sample reachable at EVERY reservation by construction.
- ⭐⭐⭐ **THE PIN BOUGHT A CONTROL THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY UNAFFORDABLE, AND IT IS THE ONE THE SV
  CONTRACT'S CENTRAL CLAIM RESTS ON.** The contract publishes *"how you can tell it is really
  host-derived and not just a bigger number: vary the reservation and the boundary moves with it,
  linearly"* — 18.82 levels/MiB, flat to 0.14 %. That was measured BY HAND in `.65` and again in
  `.69`(d), and **nothing re-derived it**, so the property the entire derived-ceiling design is
  sold on was a number in a document — on the very axis `.69`(a) had just moved. New
  `parser_embedding_ceiling_depth_scales_with_the_reservation` re-derives it every run.
- ⛔⛔ **IT IS ASSERTED ON THE FRAME DEPTH, NEVER ON THE LADDER RUNG, AND THAT IS `.69`(a) SLICE 1's
  LESSON SPENT RATHER THAN RE-LEARNED.** That slice compared reservations using a doubling
  ladder's stopping rung and got non-monotone nonsense — *"a ladder that chooses its own stopping
  point is not a controlled variable"*, because each reservation was measured on a DIFFERENT
  INPUT. The rung is quantised by `CEILING_LADDER_GROWTH`; the frame depth at refusal is not, and
  `.69`(d) established it is a property of the STACK not the input (two different inputs refused
  at the identical depth **31 568**). So the two ladders may legitimately stop at different rungs
  and still be compared.
- ⭐ **AN EXISTING LOCK WAS UPGRADED FROM A NEAR-TAUTOLOGY IN PASSING.**
  `parser_embedding_recursion_ceiling_is_anchored_to_the_reservation` asserted
  `observed.reservation_bytes == dedicated_parse_stack_bytes()` — **both sides traced to the same
  call**, so it could only fail if the RECORDING were broken. It now compares against a
  reservation the TEST names, so the value flows test → runner → thread → guard → observation with
  the test's copy independent of the engine's. ⚠️ It FAILED first, correctly, when the pin landed;
  that failure is what surfaced the weakness.
- ✅ **THE PIN IS OBSERVED, NEVER ASSUMED**, in both places: the ladder asserts
  `current_parse_stack_extent()` reports the pinned size before climbing, and the burn test
  asserts the refusal's `reservation_bytes` equals what it pinned. ⛔ **RED CONTROL, measured**:
  removing the burn test's pin under `PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES=536870912` FAILS with `left: 0` —
  i.e. the unpinned run produced **no refusal at all**, which is precisely the vacuity `.87` was
  opened for, reproduced on demand.
- ✅ **(c) HAS NO SKIP BRANCH LEFT.** The burn test's `MAX_SAFE_BURN_BYTES` early return is gone,
  not widened: pinning the floor makes the burn **56 MiB** against the 150 MiB it took at the
  reference, so there is nothing left to be too large to control.

  is NOT an engine-wide law about deep inputs, and it does **not** block the SV release. ⛔ That is
  also exactly why it must be a LEAF and not a paragraph: without the control the honest reading

### ⛔ `.82` — **`PGEN_REPORT_STACK_PROBE` REPORTS `no_refusal` FOR A REGEX PARSE THAT DEMONSTRABLY REFUSED: THE READING IS STRANDED ON THE REGEX WORKER THREAD** (`todo`, ROUTED — opened 2026-08-30 by `.79`(a)'s first census run / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0144`)

- **WHY + WHERE**: `LAST_STACK_PROBE_REFUSAL` (`rust/src/dedicated_parse_stack.rs`) is a
  thread-local, and the ONLY thing that carries it back to a caller is
  `run_on_dedicated_parse_stack`'s join. The regex family does not use that path: it dispatches to a
  long-lived `pgen-generated-regex` worker (`rust/src/embedding_api.rs:1709`-`1721`, a
  `std::thread::Builder` worker with `GENERATED_REGEX_WORKER_STACK_BYTES`) and receives the result
  over an **mpsc channel**. The reading is written on the worker and read on the caller, so it is
  never seen.
- ✅ **MEASURED, and the two surfaces contradict each other in one run** —
  `PGEN_REPORT_STACK_PROBE=1 PGEN_PARSE_STACK_BYTES=100663296 parseability_probe --parse regex`
  on 300 nested groups printed:

  ```
  stack_probe: no_refusal (the recursion ceiling was never contacted)
  Error: ... [recursion ceiling CONTACTED: this host's parse stack ran out at 1536 parser
              frames, refusing 1 rule entries during this parse ...]
  ```
  The rejection text is `.61`(a)'s label, driven by `RecursionGuard::last_ceiling_depth`, which is
  written on exactly the path that records a `StackProbeObservation`. ⇒ the refusal happened and the
  instrument denied it.
- ⛔ **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING LINE.** `.69`(d) built this instrument so an operator can
  tell *"this input is too deep for this host"* from *"this parse ran on a thread whose stack size we
  do not know"*. On the regex family it answers neither — it answers *"nothing happened"*, which is
  the one reading that is certainly wrong. And `no_refusal` is the SILENT direction: it looks like a
  clean parse, so the blind spot is invisible unless the rejection text is read beside it, which is
  how this was found.
- ⚠️ **WORSE FOR A LONG-LIVED WORKER THAN FOR A SPAWNED ONE.** The regex worker is a process-lifetime
  `OnceLock` thread, so its reading is a LATCH that accumulates across every regex parse in the
  process and is never cleared by `--parse`'s per-parse `clear_last_stack_probe_refusal()` (which
  runs on the caller). Whatever it holds is stale by construction.
- **OWES**: (a) census the population — every route by which a generated parser runs on a thread the
  caller does not join through `run_on_dedicated_parse_stack`, since regex is the one this slice met
  and a vocabulary of one is not a population; (b) decide the mechanism — carry the reading across
  the regex worker's channel hand-off the way the dedicated join does, or make the observation a
  return value rather than a thread-local, and price both; (c) rule whether `no_refusal` should be
  distinguishable from *"this route cannot report"*, since silently reporting the absence of a
  refusal on a path that cannot observe one is the same defect shape as a zero byte field meaning
  NOT MEASURED, which `.69`(d) went out of its way to avoid everywhere else.
- ⭐ **ROUTED, not worked** — the SV lane lock binds, and this is a regex-path observability defect
  that does not block the SV release. It sits behind `.79`(a) and `.69`(a). ⚠️ It DOES bound
  `.79`(a): the per-frame census cannot measure the regex family through this instrument until (b)
  is done, so regex will be recorded as NOT MEASURABLE-BY-THIS-ROUTE rather than left blank.

### ⚠️ `.47` — `detect_profile_orphans` reads the **FILTERED** profile context and a universe that omits `@default_profile`, so on any grammar declaring a default it has never evaluated the profile that SHIPS (`todo`, opened 2026-08-25 by `.46` slice 2 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0084`)

**WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it was measured against a control rather than read off the source.** While
sizing `.46`(b) the new lookahead arm reported **0** on `grammars/regex.ebnf` over its **95** `!`
occurrences. Two defects in the shared profile-context plumbing made that zero meaningless, and both
of them also sit under `detect_profile_orphans`:

1. ⛔⛔ **THE CONTEXT IS THE FILTERED GRAMMAR.** `run_grammar_lint` builds `rule_profiles` and
   `profile_universe` from `grammar.annotations` — the grammar *after* the load-time profile filter.
   A grammar declaring `@default_profile` has its gated rules removed at load and their `@profiles`
   annotations go with them. Measured on `default_profile_universe_control.ebnf` (a five-rule
   reduction of regex's shape): the lint printed **`profiles=[]`**, an EMPTY universe, on a grammar
   whose runtime verdicts show the defect in both directions (`profile='<unspecified>'` →
   `accepted=true`; `profile='relaxed'` → `accepted=false furthest_position=1`).
2. ⛔ **THE UNIVERSE OMITS `@default_profile`.** It is the union of `@profiles` LISTS, which name the
   profiles a rule is PRESENT in. The profile a gated rule is ABSENT from is, by construction, the
   one that appears in no list — for regex that is `pcre2`, the profile every parse uses unless one
   is requested.
3. ⛔ **AND THE ORPHAN ARM IS SKIPPED BELOW 2 PROFILES** (`if all_profiles.len() >= 2`). With regex's
   universe measuring `{relaxed}` — one entry — `detect_profile_orphans` does not run on regex at all.
4. ⛔⛔ **AND A THIRD, FOUND BY `.46`(c) AND ROUTED HERE: THE UNIVERSE CANNOT EXPRESS AN UNDECLARED
   REQUESTED PROFILE, UNDER WHICH *EVERY* GATED RULE IS ABSENT.** `set_grammar_profile` accepts an
   undeclared spelling and passes it through un-coerced — the book states this as designed behaviour
   (*"An undeclared spelling passes through un-coerced (it simply matches no `@profiles` list)"*). So
   there is always a reachable runtime profile in which every `@profiles`-gated rule is gated OUT
   while every UNGATED rule is live, and **no enumeration of declared profiles contains it.** ⭐ It is
   not hypothetical: `.46`(c)'s codegen-side emission condition had to model it explicitly, because
   an ungated rule guarding a gated one is vacuous under such a profile even when no *declared*
   profile exhibits it. ⇒ every profile-reasoning arm that enumerates declared profiles is an
   UNDER-count by exactly that case, and the fix is one extra hypothetical member, not a bigger list.

⇒ **`profile_orphans=0` on `grammars/regex.ebnf` is an UNEVALUATED arm, not a clean grammar**, and it
has read that way for every commit since the arm landed. The same holds for any future grammar that
declares a default.

**WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN `.46` SLICE 2.** `.46`'s new arm is REPORT-ONLY, so correcting its context
cannot break a build. `profile_orphans` is **ERROR-CLASS and GATING** — it is one of the counters
`--lint-grammar` exits nonzero on. Correcting its context would move a **blocking** counter over a
population nobody has sized, which is exactly what `.46` slice 2 declined to do one paragraph earlier
and what `DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP.15` ruled against. Doing it anyway, in a slice whose subject is a
different arm, would also make the reproducibility and corpus evidence in that slice unattributable.

**Owed:**
- **(a)** SIZE IT FIRST, on the corrected context: what does `detect_profile_orphans` report for every
  tracked grammar once it reads `unfiltered_grammar.annotations`, the universe includes
  `@default_profile`, and the `>= 2` skip is re-derived? ⛔ Do not change the gating arm before the
  number exists — the answer decides whether this is a one-line correction or a campaign.
- **(b)** the correction itself, plus a control that goes RED without it (`.46`'s
  `default_profile_universe_control.ebnf` is the shape; the orphan arm needs its own).
- **(c)** the `>= 2` guard: it encodes the orphan arm's "satisfiable elsewhere" test, which genuinely
  needs two profiles — but the universe it counts is the one measured wrong above. Re-derive the
  guard from the CORRECTED universe rather than deleting it.
- **(d)** a census of which OTHER lint arms read the filtered context, or enumerate only declared
  profiles, and would therefore report an unevaluated or under-counted zero. ⛔ **This is a census
  claim and must carry its census** ([[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]]); all
  three found so far were found by accident, which is the defect.
- **(e)** decide whether `detect_profile_gated_lookaheads` (`.46`(b)) should also model the
  undeclared-profile case. It is a NOTE-class arm post-repair, so the value is low and the cost is
  not zero — priced here rather than done silently in a slice about something else.

⚠️ **PRIORITY: after `.46` closes.** It is a real unevaluated-gate finding, but `.46` is under a
direct director order and this is not a blocker for it.

### ⚠️ `.48` — `SV-CONTRACT-CURRENCY` tier E's CHEAPEST REMEDY IS A RE-STAMP, AND NOTHING FORCES THE RE-STAMPER TO RE-DERIVE THE CLAIM (`todo`, opened 2026-08-25 by `.46` slice 3 / `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0085`, **RE-SCOPED under director challenge the same day**; mechanism owned by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2l`)

⛔⛔ **THIS LEAF WAS OPENED OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY EDITED.** It first
claimed the defect was that a `GENERATOR-ONLY` row's `parser_sha256` is *"an ABSOLUTE pin with no
producer"*. That is not a defect of the doctrine: tier E's stated contract is literally *"the row's
`parser_sha256=<hex>` must equal the sha256 of the shipped `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs`"*, and
`scripts/check_sv_contract_currency.sh:58-60` already carries the HONEST BOUND that tier E compares
against what is PRESENT in `generated/` and composes with `GENERATED-REPRODUCIBILITY` for the rest.
⇒ **a re-stamp after an unrelated codegen change is the DESIGNED response, not evidence of rot**, and
publishing it as rot mis-attributed my own gap to the instrument.

**WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS ABOUT THE WORKFLOW RATHER THAN THE PIN.** When tier E fires, the cheapest
way to make it green is to copy the new hash into the row. That is what `-0085` did. Nothing in the
check, the register or the commit flow asks the re-stamper to re-derive the claim the row actually
makes — *"this grammar revision moved the semantic digest and left the generated parser untouched"* —
and a re-stamp is indistinguishable from a rewrite that quietly makes a false claim true. **A guard
whose easiest remedy is to silence it** is the shape this repository has refused before.

**MEASURED — and the re-stamp turns out to have been CORRECT, which is why it is a workflow finding
rather than a retraction.** Re-derived under director challenge:

```
git show 2e492d08^:grammars/systemverilog.ebnf  ->  regenerate with TODAY's codegen -> 7d03b035…
git show 2e492d08 :grammars/systemverilog.ebnf  ->  regenerate with TODAY's codegen -> 7d03b035…
```

byte-identical, and equal to the value stamped into the row. ⇒ the `GENERATOR-ONLY` claim for
revision `2e492d08` **still holds under the repaired codegen**, re-derived rather than assumed.

⭐⭐ **A REUSABLE TRAP THE RE-DERIVATION EXPOSED: THE EMITTED PARSER CARRIES TWO FACTS ABOUT ITS OWN
INVOCATION, SO A NAIVE TWO-REVISION COMPARISON IS WRONG BY CONSTRUCTION.** The first attempt produced
files 5 bytes apart, the second 10 lines apart, and neither difference came from the grammar:
`-o <path>` is embedded (`ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.19`) and `PGEN_SOURCE_LABEL` is derived from the
GRAMMAR FILE NAME. Both must be held constant — same basename, equal-length output path — before two
revisions can be compared at all. Anyone re-deriving a `GENERATOR-ONLY` row must do this, and nothing
says so today.

**Owed:**
- **(a)** give the re-stamp a PRODUCER: a command that regenerates the row's revision and its
  predecessor with the current codegen, holding the grammar basename and `-o` path constant, and
  writes the resulting hash. Then the row is derived rather than typed, and re-stamping re-verifies
  by construction instead of by discipline.
- **(b)** ⚠️ price it first. It costs **two full SystemVerilog regenerations** per re-stamp (~2 min
  each measured here), so it belongs in the operator tier, not on the commit path — the same
  reasoning that keeps `generated_reproducibility_gate` tier 2 off every commit.
- **(c)** the trap above belongs in `TOOLBOX.md` beside the regeneration entries, whatever (a)
  decides: it is a fact about the emitted artifact, not about this doctrine.

⚠️ **PRIORITY: after `.46` and `.47`.** It blocks nothing — the row is green and its claim is now
re-derived — and the SV lane lock means the owning tree is not being worked.

### ✅ `.53` — **THE SAME `contains_key`-IS-A-PROFILE-PREDICATE CONFLATION SURVIVES IN `mandatory_node_gated` — PINNED, NOT REFACTORED; AND THE ROUTING EVIDENCE'S OWN SAFETY ARGUMENT WAS WRONG, SO THE PIN RESTS ON A MEASUREMENT INSTEAD** (`done` 2026-08-26, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0091`; ENGINE tier, comment-only outside `#[cfg(test)]`, ZERO grammar / codegen / generated bytes. Opened 2026-08-26 by `.51` slice 1's own root cause, censused before routing)

**ROUTING EVIDENCE** (`ROUTING-EVIDENCE` doctrine — what was MEASURED before routing):

⛔ **THIS IS A CENSUS RESULT, NOT AN IMPRESSION — the class was counted before it was claimed.**
`.51` slice 1's root cause was that `!grammar_tree.contains_key(name)` conflates *"the profile filter
removed it"* with *"it was never defined"*. The obvious follow-up question — **how many other sites
do that?** — was measured rather than asserted:

| population | count |
|---|---|
| `grammar_tree.contains_key` / `.get` sites in `stimuli_generator.rs` | **62** |
| … of which turn an ABSENCE into a *verdict* (dead / gated / unreachable) rather than a conservative guard (`continue`, `filter`, a name list) | **3** |
| … of those, already protected: `node_dead_given` (`.51`'s own, behind the `reach_hops_pass` fallback) | 1 |
| … of those, the one this leaf owns: **`mandatory_node_gated`** | **1** |
| … conservative guards needing no change (skip-edge, filter, threshold guard, missing-name list) | the remaining 59 |

⭐ **The honest headline is therefore "one, and it is latent" — not "62 instances of a defect".**
Publishing the raw 62 would have been the census-claim error in its other direction: a population
mistaken for a defect count.

**THE SITE.** `mandatory_node_gated` (`stimuli_generator.rs`), the function `.51` quoted as the model
for correct propagation:

```rust
Some(("rule_reference", name)) => {
    if self.grammar_tree.contains_key(name) {
        self.mandatory_reach_gate(name, available, visited, scope)
    } else {
        true          // <- "absent" read as GATED, exactly the conflation
    }
}
```

An `include(...)` external reference is absent for a reason that has nothing to do with store gates,
and is nevertheless reported as mandatorily gated.

⭐⭐ **WHY IT IS NOT A LIVE DEFECT TODAY, established by tracing the consumer rather than by
assuming.** `mandatory_node_gated` is reached only through `edge_is_store_gated`, whose sole call
site is guarded by `exclude_store_gated_edges`, and the only caller that passes `true` is:

```rust
self.reach_hops_pass(entry_rule, target_rule, true)
    .or_else(|| self.reach_hops_pass(entry_rule, target_rule, false))
```

⇒ an over-exclusion there is recoverable by construction — **the same prefer-then-fall-back shape
`.51` had to add**, arrived at independently by an earlier slice. That is corroboration of the
design rule, not a coincidence to leave unremarked.

**Acceptance:** (a) ⭐ **DECIDED — PIN, do not refactor.** The behaviour is correct today and the
protection is structural; the risk is that a future caller passes `exclude_store_gated_edges: true`
WITHOUT a fallback and silently inherits the conflation. So: a test asserting the fallback exists
(an undefined mandatory reference must not make a target unreachable through the store-gated pass
either), which fails the moment that protection is removed. ⛔ A refactor to "fix" a latent,
protected site would move bytes in the most reach-sensitive function in the engine to buy nothing
measurable — the `GENERATED-LINT-CORRECTNESS.4` bar refuses exactly that trade;
(b) correct `mandatory_node_gated`'s doc-comment, which claims *"mirrors `reach_hops_pass` skipping
that edge"* — ⚠️ **that claim was FALSE when `.51` began and is TRUE now**, so the comment must
either be re-derived against the current code or dropped, never left as a stale assertion about a
second function (this is the `.51`(e) lesson generalised); (c) ⛔ **the 59 conservative sites are
DECLARED OUT, not silently unexamined** — the acceptance is that the classification above is
re-runnable, so a future site added in the verdict class is visible rather than lost in the 62.

#### ✅ `.53` SLICE 1 (`PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0091`, 2026-08-26 session #265) — **(a)+(b)+(c) DISCHARGED, and THREE of this leaf's own routing-evidence claims are REFUTED by re-derivation before any of them was built on**

⛔⛔ **THE HEADLINE IS A CORRECTION, NOT A COMPLETION.** The leaf's ruling — *PIN, do not refactor* —
**stands**, and it is implemented. But the ARGUMENT the routing evidence gave for it does not
survive re-derivation, and two of the three numbers it published are not reproducible. A pin whose
justification is false is a pin that the next reader will remove. So the justification is replaced
with a measured one, in the doc comment itself, where the next reader will meet it.

**REFUTATION 1 — *"its SOLE consumer happens to sit behind a fallback"* is FALSE. `mandatory_node_gated`
is reached by SEVEN functions.** Census over the non-test half of `stimuli_generator.rs`, attributing
every call of the two mutually-recursive entry points to its enclosing `fn`:

| entry point | calling function | line |
|---|---|---|
| `mandatory_node_gated` | `offpath_siblings_gated_along_path` | 4561 |
| `mandatory_reach_gate` | `name_gate_via_mandatory_prefix` | 4882 |
| `mandatory_node_gated` | `name_gate_via_targeted_alternative` | 4915 |
| `mandatory_node_gated` | `node_render_store_gated` | 5019 |
| `mandatory_node_gated` + `mandatory_reach_gate` | `target_forces_positive_store_gate` | 9576 / 9589 |
| `mandatory_reach_gate` | **`edge_is_store_gated`** | 10113 |
| `mandatory_node_gated` | `escape_walk` | 10226 |

⇒ **seven distinct callers; `edge_is_store_gated` is one of them.** The store-free fallback protects
that ONE caller and nothing else. The leaf inferred a reach property from reading one call chain —
which is the shape [[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]] already names, arriving
here in its *"reached only through"* dialect.

**⭐ THE REPLACEMENT ARGUMENT, AND IT IS STRONGER BECAUSE IT COVERS ALL SEVEN.** The conflation can
only produce a WRONG answer for the *never-defined* cause of absence (for the *profile-pruned*
cause, "cannot be rendered, so it is no escape" is correct). So the exposure is bounded by whether
any grammar contains an undefined reference at all — an ERROR-class finding of the well-formedness
lint. Measured over every tracked grammar:

```
for g in grammars/*.ebnf; do PGEN_LINT_DUMP_ALL=1 ./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline "$g" --lint-grammar; done
#   undefined_references=0   on 16 of the 17 grammars/*.ebnf
#   undefined_references=5   on systemverilog_lrm_profiled_wrapper  (the LRM extraction harness,
#                            which has never generated a parser — TOOLBOX 5.1 already records this)
```

⇒ **no grammar that ships can supply the case the site gets wrong**, for any of the seven callers.
That is the durable half of the ruling; the fallback is the local half.

**REFUTATION 2 — *"3 turn an absence into a verdict"* does not reproduce; the classification
re-derives 2, and both of them are the two the leaf already named.** The routing table published a
`3` and then listed sub-rows for only `node_dead_given` and `mandatory_node_gated`. Re-deriving under
the rule the leaf itself states — *verdict* = the absence branch answers in the direction that
RESTRICTS (dead / gated / unreachable), *guard* = `continue` / `filter` / a name list — yields
**2 verdicts and 55 guards over 57 engine sites**. The nearest misses were adjudicated individually
rather than waved past: `mandatory_reach_gate`'s `None => false`, `node_leads_with_rule_reference`,
`rule_leads_with_rule_reference` and `rule_render_is_single_leading_token` all return a
CLASSIFICATION from the absence branch, but every one answers in the *conservative* direction (not
gated / take the general path), which is precisely what the leaf's own wording calls a guard.

⚠️ **The `62` is right, and it is right for a reason the leaf did not state: 5 of the 62 are inside
`#[cfg(test)]`.** The engine population is **57**. Both numbers are now derived, not typed.

**REFUTATION 3 — (b)'s premise is backwards. `git log -S` places the comment's authorship, and the
cross-reference it makes was TRUE when written, TRUE when `.51` began, and TRUE today.**

```
git log --oneline -S 'mirrors `reach_hops_pass` skipping that edge' -- rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs
#   2acad95b PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0115 (leaf GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.5.6.2.2.2) …
git show 2acad95b:rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs | grep -n 'contains_key(site.referenced_rule'
#   5768: if !self.grammar_tree.contains_key(site.referenced_rule.as_str()) {
git show bf76b504~1:… | grep -n 'contains_key(site.referenced_rule'      # the tree .51 began on

```

⇒ the skip that the comment says it mirrors was present at authorship and at `.51`'s start; it lives
in `reach_hops_bfs` today only because `.51` split the BFS out of `reach_hops_pass`, which still
calls it. The leaf's *"FALSE when `.51` began and is TRUE now"* is not reproducible in either half.

⭐⭐ **SO WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE COMMENT — and it is worse than a stale cross-reference.**
The defective clause is the JUSTIFICATION, not the citation: *"it cannot be rendered, so it is no
escape."* That sentence asserts the conflated reading as a fact. It is true for one of the two
causes of absence and false for the other — i.e. the comment did not merely go stale, **it wrote
`.51`'s bug down as the design intent.** A reader repairing this site would have found the code's own
documentation arguing against the repair. That is why (b) is discharged by re-derivation rather than

**ROUTING EVIDENCE** (`ROUTING-EVIDENCE` doctrine — what was MEASURED before routing, and whether it
reproduces outside the family it is being sent to):

⛔⛔ **READ THIS FIRST: THE OBVIOUS ROUTING NOTE FOR THIS FINDING IS FALSE, AND IT WAS CAUGHT BY

([[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]]). **That suppression exists and shipped**:

is a REFINEMENT of a live mechanism, never a missing one, and any fix must extend `-0087` rather
than re-introduce what `H.12.3` withdrew.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND.** `.51` slice 1 repaired the reach PLANNER, which had been routing
`kw_macromodule_df04b866` through a profile-dead branch. The plan is now correct end to end:

```
[reach-path] target='kw_macromodule_df04b866' hops=[…, ("module_declaration_sv_2017", "root/o0/s0"),
    ("module_ansi_header", "root/s1"), ("module_keyword", "root/o1")]
```

and the target is **still `UNKNOWN`** — now the sole `verilog_2005` union residual. Plan correct,

two instruments are different.

⭐ **THE SHORT-CIRCUIT IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — TWO INDEPENDENT CARRIERS EACH EMITTED THEIR OWN
`@sample` VERBATIM.** Under `verilog_2005`, with the corrected plan:

| probe pass | sample | that string is |
|---|---|---|
| `[plannable-probe]` | `module m(input wire a);endmodule` | `module_ansi_header`'s rule-level `@sample` + `endmodule` |
| `[carrier-div-probe]` | `module m(a,b);endmodule` | `module_nonansi_header`'s rule-level `@sample` + `endmodule` |
| `[target-own-probe]` | `//x\nmodule m(input wire a);//x\nendmodule//x\n` | the same, trivia-injected |

Two *different* carriers, each reproducing *that* carrier's sample exactly. All four fallback passes
hit the same wall, so this is not one pass misbehaving.

**ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE), read off the source rather than inferred.**
`ReachPlan::needs_rule_body_descent`, `rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs:1708`:

```rust
    fn needs_rule_body_descent(&self, rule_name: &str) -> bool {
        self.directives.keys().any(|(r, _)| r == rule_name)
            || self.forced_quantifier_min.keys().any(|(r, _)| r == rule_name)
    }
```

Both key sets are built from the hop's `node_path`: `directives_along_path` (`:10732`) emits one
entry per **`o{i}`** segment, `quantifier_sites_along_path` (`:10760`) one per **`q`** segment.
⇒ **a hop whose path is a pure mandatory Sequence element yields NEITHER.**

Our hop is `("module_ansi_header", "root/s1")`. `module_ansi_header := attribute_instance*
module_keyword ( declaration_lifetime_sv_only )? module_identifier …` — `module_keyword` sits at
sequence position **1**: mandatory, no alternation to force, no quantifier to expand. The plan
therefore records **nothing** keyed on `module_ansi_header`, `needs_rule_body_descent` returns
`false`, and the rule-level literal override at `:11409` fires and emits the canonical sample.

⭐⭐ **WHY `-0087` WORKS FOR ITS OWN EXAMPLE AND NOT FOR THIS ONE — the discriminator is what kind of
node the path crosses, and it is a one-word difference.** `-0087`'s M1a routes descend
`module_ansi_header` → `( list_of_port_declarations )?` → … : an **OPTIONAL**, which contributes a
`q` segment and therefore a forced quantifier site, so the stand-down sees the rule. This route
descends to a **MANDATORY** element, which contributes nothing. The predicate is not wrong about
decisions; it is being used to answer a question about PATH MEMBERSHIP that it cannot see.

⇒ **the plan knows the answer and is not being asked**: the hop chain already names
`module_ansi_header`. ⭐ `H.12.3`'s reverted infra was called `on_path_rules` — this is the
measurement that was missing when it was withdrawn, and it now exists.

⛔ **IT REPRODUCES OUTSIDE SystemVerilog BY CONSTRUCTION.** The predicate is grammar-agnostic and
gates every rule-level `@sample`/`@probe_sample` in every not-yet-fully-certified grammar. Any rule
carrying a rule-level sample whose reach path enters it through a mandatory sequence element is
exposed. ⚠️ Today SV is the only shipped grammar that is not fully certified, so it is where the
cost is visible — but that is a fact about the roster, not about the defect.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE DESIGN — ONE INVARIANT REPLACING THREE PROXY PREDICATES (decided 2026-08-26)

⛔ **THIS IS THE FOURTH TIME THE SAME PLAN HAS BEEN SHORT-CIRCUITED, AND THE PATTERN IS THE ARGUMENT
FOR STOPPING THE POINT-PATCHING.** Each previous repair widened a *different proxy* for the same
question:

| slice | what short-circuited the plan | the proxy that was widened |
|---|---|---|
| `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.3` (`-0078`) | a BRANCH-level `@sample` on the exactly-forced branch | `forced_branch_for(rule, node_path) == selected` |
| `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.5.5.2.2` (`-0087`) | a RULE-level `@sample` on a rule the plan forces a decision inside | `needs_rule_body_descent` = has a directive or a quantifier site |
| ⛔ **`.52` (this leaf)** | a RULE-level `@sample` on a rule the plan crosses through a MANDATORY element | — none of the above fires |

⭐ **Every one of those proxies is trying to answer the same question — *"is this rule on the active
plan's path?"* — using whatever the plan happened to record.** `H.12.3` keyed on a forced branch
because that is what a branch plan records; `-0087` keyed on directives + quantifier sites because
that is what a rule plan records. Neither is the question; both are artefacts of the plan's storage.

⛔⛔ **AND THE PLAN ALREADY KNOWS THE ANSWER — IT IS BEING THROWN AWAY.**
`compute_reach_path_with_quantifier_sites` returns `(chain, quantifier_sites, hops)`, and
`install_reach_plan_from_hops` already iterates `hops` to build the chain:

```rust
for (hop_rule, hop_site_path) in hops {
    chain.extend(Self::directives_along_path(hop_rule, hop_site_path));
    quantifier_sites.extend(Self::quantifier_sites_along_path(hop_rule, hop_site_path));
}
```

`directives_along_path` emits only for `o{i}` segments and `quantifier_sites_along_path` only for
`q` segments, so **`hop_rule` itself is discarded whenever its hop path is a pure `s{i}`** — which is
exactly the case that leaks. The membership fact is in hand at the one place that could record it.

⭐⭐ **THE DECISION: record path membership as a first-class field and make the invariant explicit.**
`ActiveReachPlan` gains `on_path_rules: HashSet<String>`, filled from `hops` (plus the target rule)
in `install_reach_plan_from_hops` — the **single** builder both public entry points funnel through,
so the two paths cannot drift, which is a property that file already documents and relies on. The
invariant then reads, once, in words a reader can check:

> **While a reach plan is installed, no literal short-circuit may fire for a rule the plan's path
> crosses.** A `@sample` renders a rule INSTEAD of its body; the plan exists to steer THROUGH that
> body; the two are unconditionally in conflict.

`needs_rule_body_descent` becomes membership ∪ (directives, quantifier sites) — the union, not a
replacement, because the existing keys also cover sub-plans that carry no hop chain, and dropping
them would silently narrow `-0087`.

⭐ **WHY THIS IS NOT A REVIVAL OF WHAT `H.12.3` WITHDREW, which is the obvious objection and deserves
answering before the code is written.** `H.12.3` built an `on_path_rules` gate FIRST and reverted it
with the reason recorded verbatim: *"the rule-level gate + `on_path_rules` infra explored first were
REVERTED once the dump proved the short-circuit is branch-level (targeted-fix discipline — no code on
a hypothesis)."* ⇒ it was withdrawn for lacking EVIDENCE, not for being wrong. That evidence now
exists and is specific: a measured target, a measured hop (`("module_ansi_header", "root/s1")`), a
measured probe output reproducing two different carriers' samples verbatim, and a named reason the
existing predicate cannot see it. **The discipline that reverted it is the same discipline that
reinstates it.**

⚠️ **THE SCOPE RISK, PRICED BEFORE THE EDIT.** `-0087`'s analogous widening moved SV `UNKNOWN` by
**28**, so this is NOT presumed small: the blast radius must be measured on all three profiles at
seeds `[0,7,42]` and every moved rule attributed by name. ⭐ It remains INERT off-reach by
construction — `on_path_rules` is empty when no plan is installed, and sub-plans built from a bare
`sub_chain` carry an empty set, so their behaviour is byte-identical.

| field | slice 1 (`.51`) | after `.52` | attribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| `total` | 1131 | **1131** | unmoved |
| `proof` | 356 | **356** | unmoved |
| `witness` | 761 | **762** | ⭐ **`kw_macromodule_df04b866`**, the founding target of the whole chain |

> Or-aware (gated iff EVERY alternative is gated), **Sequence-aware (gated iff ANY element is, since

⇒ **the mirror is asymmetric, and the asymmetry IS the defect.** The escape analysis is

**WHAT LANDED.** `reach_hops_pass` now PREFERS a route whose every hop sits in a branch the active
profile can still render, via `collect_renderable_rule_reference_sites`, and FALLS BACK to the
unpruned walk when the target is unreachable under pruning. The renderability verdict is a fixpoint
(`compute_unrenderable_rules`) computed ONCE in `new()`, carrying the semantics
`mandatory_node_gated` already documents with the store-gate half removed.

⛔⛔ **THE FALLBACK IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DEFENSIVE PADDING — AND THE FIRST CUT WITHOUT IT SHIPPED A
REGRESSION THAT A UNIT TEST CAUGHT.** A rule is absent from `grammar_tree` for **two** reasons the
generator cannot tell apart, because `apply_grammar_profile_filter` (`main.rs:2657`) prunes
`rule_order` **as well as** the tree, leaving no residue to discriminate on:

| why the rule is missing | what it means for routing |
|---|---|
| the profile filter removed it | genuinely unrenderable — prune |
| it was never defined here (an `include(...)` external reference) | ⛔ **NOT a profile fact** — `node_satisfiable` deliberately treats it as ⊤, *"no false positives"* |

The first cut treated both as dead and took
`spurious_store_entry_block_keeps_its_own_rule_witness` **RED** — its fixture reaches its target
through an UNDEFINED `epsilon`, so the whole branch was pruned and the plan would not install.
⭐ **The control that caught it was a pre-existing test I did not write, and it was right**: verified
by reverting to `HEAD` (test passes) and re-applying (test fails), so the attribution is measured,
not assumed. With the fallback, pruning can only ever IMPROVE a route — a target reachable both ways
takes the renderable one, a target reachable only through a dead branch is planned exactly as before,
and a grammar using includes is untouched. Pinned by
`an_undefined_reference_must_not_prune_a_route_the_way_a_profile_gate_does`.

⚠️ **HONEST BOUND ON THAT SECOND ROW, because it would be easy to overstate the danger.** The four
tracked grammars that use `include(` RESOLVE it at load — SV's lint reports
`undefined_references=0` — so no *shipped* grammar carries a dangling reference today. The
undefined-reference case is exercised by test fixtures, and the fallback exists because the
generator **cannot tell the two apart**, not because a shipped grammar currently needs it. That is
the right reason to keep it: the discriminator is absent by construction, so a future grammar or a
mid-refactor tree would hit it silently.

⚠️ **THE DESCENT RULE IS NOT THE PROPAGATION RULE, and that is the second design subtlety.**
`( dead )?` does NOT make its container unrenderable — it renders empty — but a site INSIDE it is
still unroutable, because reaching that site requires the quantifier to render a copy. So deadness
propagates upward through min≥1 quantifiers only, while descent requires a renderable element at
EVERY quantifier. Both directions are pinned by
`a_min_zero_quantifier_does_not_kill_its_container_but_does_block_descent`.

NOT FEARED.** Answering renderability lazily re-walked the referenced rules transitively at every
alternative of every rule the BFS visited, which on a 1 537-rule grammar pushed this command past
**600 s**. Hoisting it to a fixpoint in `new()` — the same shape as the lint's own
`compute_sat_by_profile`, so the two agree by construction rather than as two hand-kept models —
brings it back under three minutes of the pre-change figure. ⚠️ **THE PUBLISHED `+15 %` IS WITHDRAWN
— it was one run per arm.** The measurement that stands is the gate's own `elapsed`, which now has

within-arm spread is 70 s, so the between-arm difference is not resolvable at this sample size. What
IS established is the direction of the earlier problem: the lazy implementation pushed the same
command past **600 s** where the fixpoint keeps it near four minutes — an order-of-magnitude signal
that survives any reasonable spread, unlike a 15 % one. ⭐ `unrenderable_rules` is
**empty** for any grammar with nothing missing from its tree, which is every grammar declaring no
`@profiles` — so the whole mechanism is inert there by construction, not merely by measurement.

| probe pass | sample | that string is |

| `[plannable-probe]` | `module m(input wire a);endmodule` | `module_ansi_header`'s rule-level `@sample` + `endmodule` |

`@sample` override is firing on a rule the plan is descending THROUGH.

⛔⛔ **AND THE FIRST ROUTING NOTE FOR THIS WAS WRONG, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS PUBLISHED.** The obvious
reading — *"nothing suppresses a rule-level `@sample` on an interior hop"* — is a CENSUS claim
([[an-x-is-checked-by-nothing-claim-is-a-census-claim]]), and the census refutes it: **that
suppression exists and shipped**, as `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.5.5.2.2`
(`PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0087`, SV `UNKNOWN 121 -> 93`), whose own worked example is
`module_ansi_header` — the very rule here. `H.12.3` had even built a rule-level gate first and
REVERTED it as unproven; `-0087` brought it back with evidence.

⭐⭐ **THE REAL MECHANISM IS NARROWER AND SHARPER: THE STAND-DOWN ASKS THE WRONG QUESTION.**
`needs_rule_body_descent` (`stimuli_generator.rs:1708`) returns true iff the plan holds a forced
OR-**directive** or a forced **quantifier site** keyed on the rule:

```rust
    fn needs_rule_body_descent(&self, rule_name: &str) -> bool {
        self.directives.keys().any(|(r, _)| r == rule_name)
            || self.forced_quantifier_min.keys().any(|(r, _)| r == rule_name)
    }
```

and those keys are built by `directives_along_path` (one per `o{i}` segment) and
`quantifier_sites_along_path` (one per `q` segment). **A hop whose path is a pure mandatory Sequence
element yields NEITHER.** Our hop is `("module_ansi_header", "root/s1")` — `module_keyword` sits at
sequence position 1, mandatory, no `o`, no `q` — so the plan records nothing for the rule, the
stand-down cannot see it, and the sample wins.

⇒ **the predicate asks *"does the plan force a DECISION inside this rule?"* when the question that
matters is *"is this rule an on-path HOP at all?"*** `-0087`'s own canonical route descends through
`( list_of_port_declarations )?` — an OPTIONAL, which registers a `q` site — which is exactly why it
worked there and is invisible here. ⭐ `H.12.3`'s reverted infra was even named `on_path_rules`; this
is the measurement that was missing when it was reverted. ⇒ routed as **`.52`**.

⛔ The `verilog_2005` cert baseline is therefore re-attributed to **14**, not to 13 — the residue is
OWNED and still WATCHED, not quietly dropped.

**ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE).** `apply_plan`
(`rust/src/ast_pipeline/indirect_lr_elimination.rs`) copies `@profiles` onto BOTH helpers from the
BASE rule:

```rust
if !base_profiles.is_empty() {
    annotations.semantic_annotations.insert(plan.helper_base_rule.clone(),   base_profiles.clone());
    annotations.semantic_annotations.insert(plan.helper_suffix_rule.clone(), base_profiles.clone());
}
```

`casting_type` declares no `@profiles`, so `base_profiles` is empty and `casting_type_lr_suffix` gets
nothing — while every one of its alternatives is gated. ⛔ **The two helpers are not the same kind of
rule and must not share a rule**: `X_lr_base` carries the BASE's alternatives (the base's gate is
right for it); `X_lr_suffix` is an ordered choice over the ROUTES (the routes' gate is).

**THE DESIGN, BUILT AND MEASURED.** `node_satisfiable`'s own `Or` law: a choice is satisfiable where
SOME alternative is, so the suffix helpers take the **UNION** of their branches' gates — and only
when **EVERY** branch carries one, because a single unconstrained branch makes the choice universally
satisfiable and gating it then would be an **under-acceptance invented by the rewrite**.
`X_lr_guard{v}_suffix := X_lr_suffix &( residual )` references the wrapper MANDATORILY, so it
inherits the same union. On the tick+7 grammar this reads **`profile_orphans` 3 → 0, lint rc 1 → 0**,
with `unhandled=0`, `eliminated=4`, `unreachable_rules=0`, `undefined_references=0`,
`ordered_choice_shadowing=0` and 1537 rules throughout — ⇒ **the 17th gate then lands cleanly, at 8
source tags rather than the 24-28 `(c4)` priced.** A unit control was written and observed RED
without the derivation (`left: None / right: Some(["a", "b"])`).

directive whose only authoritative spelling is the grammar's."* Two things answer it. **First, the
clone is not an authored rule.** The pass already synthesizes `X_lr_base` / `X_lr_suffix_rN`, which
no author wrote and no author can annotate; a gate on a clone therefore has no authored spelling to
be *second* to. **Second, the gate is DERIVED, not invented.** The intersection is already computed
by this function and already trusted enough to REFUSE the whole candidate on — the pass is willing
to act on that value, just not to write it down. ⇒ the provenance rule protects against inventing a
constraint the grammar never expressed; the intersection is exactly what the grammar expressed,
composed. **(b) implements (i)**, and owes the codegen lockstep it implies: a clone carrying a
synthesized `@profiles` moves generated bytes, so the rebaseline is deliberate rather than
incidental.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED HERE, and (c) still owes it**: a parser GENERATED from the breaking grammar,
observed rejecting `a = int'(2)'(3);`. The census counts REFUSALS, not lost derivations, and the
interpreter cannot settle the difference — TOOLBOX 1.5b marks its verdicts untrustworthy exactly
when `left_recursion_unhandled > 0`, which is the state under test. ⇒ *"the strict profiles lose
derivations"* remains a well-supported INFERENCE.

#### ✅ `.50` (d) — **PRICED AND BUILT: the counter that moved 0 → 15 at exit 0 is now a RATCHET, and GIT IS THE BASELINE so there is no artifact to rot** (2026-08-26, `PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0095`; OPS/ENFORCER tier, ZERO Rust / grammar / codegen / generated bytes)

**(d) ASKED FOR A PRICE, AND THE PRICE DECIDED THE DESIGN.** *"A grammar that has always had
surviving cycles is a different fact from one whose count moved 0 → 15 in a single commit. A RATCHET
on this counter would have blocked the whole thing; the WARNING did not. Price it."*

⛔ **THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE NUMBER.** `left_recursion_unhandled` is a WARNING and
`--lint-grammar` exits **0** on it, while `profile_orphans` — the ERROR-class counter an operator
would actually quote — went to **0** in the same edit. Every registered doctrine stayed GREEN.
Nothing in the repository read this counter, which `.54` confirmed by census (**0** consumers of the
sibling `left_recursion_eliminated` across `scripts/`, `rust/scripts/`, `rust/Makefile`,
`rust/test_data/`, `.github/`).

**⭐⭐ THE DESIGN: GIT IS THE BASELINE.** The repo's established ratchet shape
(`PARSE-COST-RATCHET`) pins a tracked baseline and offers a `--rebaseline` remedy — which brings an
artifact, an identity block, a staleness budget, and `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.35`'s
*records-its-own-parent* defect. None of that is needed here: the comparison is **staged content vs
`HEAD` content of the same file**, so the baseline cannot go stale, needs no verification, and both
sides are linted with the SAME binary — which isolates the GRAMMAR axis by construction rather than
by argument.

| | priced |
|---|---|
| no `grammars/**.ebnf` staged (the common case) | inert |
| a staged grammar reading `unhandled=0` | **ONE** lint (short-circuit: it cannot have risen INTO 0) |
| a staged grammar with survivors | two lints (~10 s for `systemverilog`) |

⭐ The short-circuit is not a micro-optimisation — it is the whole cost model, because **0 is every
grammar that generates a parser**, so the ordinary SV grammar commit pays one lint and never
reconstructs HEAD.

⛔⛔ **IT BLOCKS, WITH NO ENV ESCAPE, AND THAT IS FREE ON DAY ONE FOR A STATED REASON.**
`SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.11` established the rule: *a guard is safe to make blocking over its whole
population exactly when the FIX PRECEDES IT.* `.50`(b) shipped that fix one commit earlier, so the
population is at 0 and a blocking ratchet fires on nothing. If a rise is ever genuinely right, the
remedy is a leaf that changes the pass or the grammar — the posture `BASELINE-IDENTITY` took when it
**deleted** the env escape its first design needed. ⚠️ `systemverilog_lrm_profiled_wrapper` sits at
**23** and is NOT excluded: the ratchet compares a file with ITSELF, and 23 → 23 is not a rise. An
exclusion list would have been a second population to maintain, for nothing.

⭐⭐ **RED CONTROL PROVEN THROUGH THE DRIVER, and the fixture is FOUR LINES.** The `.50`(b) repair
means the founding reproducer no longer rises, so the control needed a fresh rise — an indirect cycle
whose hop carries a residual and no return annotation, which the pass refuses for a DIFFERENT reason
and therefore leaves unhandled. Appended to `grammars/json.ebnf` (`lr_a := lr_b "z"` /
`lr_b := lr_a "y" | "q"`) and STAGED:

```
LR-ELIMINATION-RATCHET: RISE — 'grammars/json.ebnf' raises left_recursion_unhandled from 0 to 2.
  ✗ FAIL  LR-ELIMINATION-RATCHET — …
doctrines: ✗ one or more doctrines FAILED — commit/merge blocked. Fix above, do not bypass.   (rc 1)
```

and after restoring the file, `ALL 29 enforced doctrines PASS`. ⭐ The message names the two
diagnostic commands (`--lint-grammar`, `PGEN_INDIRECT_LR_GATE_DUMP=1`) rather than only the verdict,
because a ratchet that says *"you may not"* without saying *"here is how to look"* gets bypassed.

⚠️ **HONEST LIMIT, PRICED AND DECLINED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED.** This is staged-scope-aware on
GRAMMARS, so an ENGINE change that raises the counter without touching a grammar is **not** caught
here. That axis has partial coverage — the elimination pass's unit tests assert
`detect_left_recursion(...).is_empty()` after rewriting, and `GENERATED-REPRODUCIBILITY` notices when
generated bytes move — but neither is a census of this counter. Widening to engine sources costs two
SV lints (~10 s) on a large share of commits; declined, and named in the check's own header so the
gap is visible rather than implied.

  | `kw_posedge_7529558b`, `kw_negedge_c77fbc5c` | entries | +52 each | the 52 re-entries the memo used to answer now re-run both sibling terminals |

### ⛔ `.89` — **THE EXISTENCE PREDICATES ARE STORE-WIDE: A FACT EMITTED INTO A SCOPE THAT HAS SINCE CLOSED STILL SATISFIES `has_fact` FROM THE SCOPE OUTSIDE IT, SO A GRAMMAR CANNOT USE `@emit_fact` + `@open_scope`/`@close_scope` TO DECLARE A NAME *ONLY INSIDE* A REGION — THE BOOK SAID IT COULD** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED, not SV-blocking — opened 2026-09-03 by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` / `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0347`)

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND — by the fix the leaf had pre-registered going RED on its own invalid pin.**
  `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` had to make `CrossValType` / `CrossQueueType` type names *in the body of a
  cross and nowhere else* (IEEE 1800-2017 §19.6.1.3, `section-19-functional-coverage.md:1307`). The
  pre-registered shape was the typedef idiom scoped: `@open_scope: { kind: cross }` on a `{` marker,
  two `@emit_fact: { kind: type_name, … }` on the same marker, `@close_scope` on the `}` marker. The
  fixed pins flipped to ACCEPT — and so did the invalid pin
  (`stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_cross_predefined_type_after_cross.sv`, `CrossQueueType q;`
  at module level AFTER the endgroup).
- ✅ **MEASURED (interpreter, `PGEN_TRACE_VERBOSITY=high`, the grammar with the emits in place):**
  `🔓 @open_scope kind=Custom("cross") name=None new_id=ScopeId(1) parent=Some(ScopeId(0)) new_depth=2` ·
  `📥 @emit_fact kind=type_name name=Identifier("CrossValType") scope_depth=1 scope_id=ScopeId(1)` ·
  `📥 @emit_fact kind=type_name name=Identifier("CrossQueueType") scope_depth=1 scope_id=ScopeId(1)` ·
  `🔒 @close_scope OK id=Some(ScopeId(1)) frame=Some((Custom("cross"), None)) new_depth=0` · and then, from
  the module scope, `🔍 has_fact(kind=type_name, name=Identifier("CrossQueueType")) → true`. The scope
  machinery did everything the book describes; the QUERY ignored it.
- **WHY + WHERE (source, not inference):** `rust/src/ast_pipeline/semantic_runtime.rs` —
  `"has_fact" => … self.fact_index.any_with_name(expected_kind, &expected_name)` and `any_with_name`'s
  own doc comment: *"O(1)-average existence check across the whole store: is there any fact of `kind`
  with this `name` (in any scope_depth)?"*. The index is keyed `(scope_depth, name)`, not by scope id,
  and nothing in the existence family (`has_fact`, `lacks_fact`, `has_fact_attribute`,
  `fact_attribute_equals`, `lacks_fact_attribute_equals`, `fact_count_at_least`) consults
  `active_chain`. The scope-aware primitives are `has_fact_in_current_scope` (DEPTH-keyed via
  `any_with_name_at_scope` — a closed sibling at the same depth still matches), `in_scope_kind` /
  `not_in_scope_kind` (walk `active_chain`, `active_scope_chain_has_kind`) and `resolve_path`.
- ⛔ **THE BOOK OVERSTATED IT.** `docs/book/src/semantic-store.md` §2 read *"When you query for a
  fact, the store walks the active scope chain from innermost to outermost — exactly the visibility
  rule you'd want"* and §6 captioned `has_fact` *"Does any fact of this (kind, name) exist in scope?"*.
  `docs/proposals/CONTEXT_AWARE_PARSING_DESIGN.md:69` states the same intent (*"queries walk the scope
  chain from innermost to outermost"*). Corrected in the book by `-0347` to what the engine does; the
  design document keeps its intent and this leaf is the gap between the two.
- ⛔ **NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, AND WHY: a grammar DEPENDS on the store-wide reading.** `grammars/regex.ebnf:572`
  `@predicate: { name: has_fact, args: [regex_defined_capture_name, $ref], phase: final, view: shaped }`
  checks at parse completion that a named back-reference names a group that was DEFINED — and a
  group defined inside a lookaround (`(?=(?<n>a))\k<n>`) is emitted inside a `lookaround` scope that
  closed long before `final` runs. Making `has_fact` chain-visible would turn valid PCRE into a
  rejection. So the store-wide semantics are load-bearing, and the missing thing is a SECOND,
  opt-in, chain-visible existence query (or a per-`@fact_kind` `visibility:` declaration — default
  `store`, opt-in `lexical`), never a change to `has_fact`'s meaning.
- **PRICED (not built):** (a) a `has_fact_visible(kind, name)` primitive = any fact of `kind`+`name`
  whose `scope_id ∈ active_chain` (the record already carries `scope_id`; `find_fact_position_by_name_in_scope`
  is the one-scope form of it) plus the `lacks_`/`_attribute_equals` twins the SV grammar's
  `type_name` gates use at ~12 sites; (b) a `visibility: lexical` field on `@fact_kind` so a kind
  declares chain-visibility once and every existing query respects it (zero grammar edits at the
  use-sites; regex's kinds keep the default). Either needs `DESIGN-PRIOR-ART` (a new annotation
  surface), the 1.8 interpreter-parity suite extended with a closed-scope arm, and the book. (b) is the
  smaller blast radius for SystemVerilog, whose facts today ALL live in `ScopeId(0)` — no existing
  verdict can move — and it is the shape SystemVerilog will need anyway the day modules, classes
  and packages open scopes (today a typedef declared in one module is visible in the next).
- **WHY PARKED:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` shipped without it. Containment (`in_scope_kind(cross)` as a
  `post` predicate on a terminal recognizer) is the sound spelling for two names the LRM predefines, and
  it has no leak by construction. This leaf becomes SV-blocking only when a construct needs a
  *file-declared* name to be region-scoped — none is in the axis-2 bar today (`.13w`'s 199
  `residual:not_parsed_with_declarations` rows are the population to watch).
- ✅ **REPRODUCED OUTSIDE SYSTEMVERILOG, AND BANKED** —
  `docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/eus89_store_wide_has_fact/probe.sh` (`scope_leak.ebnf`,
  six rules: `{x}` opens a `region` scope, emits `(nm, T)` into it, closes it; `T` is gated by
  `has_fact(nm, T)`): input `{x}T` → `accepted=true`; the RED control `scope_ctrl.ebnf` (same gate, no
  region) on `T` → `accepted=false`. **`eus89 probe: 2/2 as declared (fail=0)`**, interpreter, no codegen.
  Re-run it when this leaf lands: arm A1 must then flip to REJECT, and the expectation is flipped
  deliberately, never silently.
- **ROUTING EVIDENCE lives in the opening tree** (`docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md`, *ROUTING EVIDENCE*
  section, `.3.29` → `.89`).

### ⛔ `.90` — **AN ORDERED CHOICE ENTERS A RULE WHOSE FIRST TERMINAL CANNOT MATCH, AND A `pre` PREDICATE THAT READS THE STORE ON THE REFUSAL PATH EPOCH-TAINTS EVERY CALLER'S CACHED FAILURE — the two engine-tier costs a scope-gated recognizer pays, measured on `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` and PRICED here** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED, not SV-blocking — opened 2026-09-03 by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` / `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0347`)

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND — by `PARSE-COST-RATCHET` refusing three spellings of one two-name recognizer.**
  `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29` admits `CrossValType` / `CrossQueueType` at the two unscoped type use-sites
  only while a `cross` scope is open. Every spelling that checks the two names at a type position
  costs something outside a cross, because `checked_type_identifier` REFUSES most of its attempts
  (on `opentitan/…/pinmux_reg_top.sv` it commits on none of 22 889) and the check must run where it
  refused. Three cuts, each measured on the pinned sample:
  1. a dispatcher rule tried FIRST at every use-site — `entries` +2 419 875 (+0.59 %), `memo_hits`
     +1 162 020 (+0.63 %): a dispatcher entry plus a recognizer entry per attempt (22 889 each on
     `pinmux_reg_top.sv`);
  2. the recognizer as an ORDERED second branch at the callers, its scope check a `pre` predicate —
     `entries` +2 154 348 (+0.52 %), `memo_hits` +1 162 020: the recognizer's own 264 259 entries plus
     ~44 900 re-entries of EVERY `data_type` alternative, `trivia` +316 881, and deep parents LOSING
     replays (`named_parameter_assignment` −23 336, `ordered_parameter_assignment` −7 899,
     `data_type` −2 801) — the `.88` eviction shape from a different cause;
  3. the same, the scope check a `post` predicate — on the three heaviest pinned files (debug probe,
     protocol-graph counters, deterministic): entries **+55 867 / +53 338 / +49 978** over the
     tracked per-file baseline, memo hits **+18 971 / +18 172 / +17 020**, versus cut 2's
     **+168 592 / +89 890** on the lightest of the three; on the whole pinned sample (release probe,
     the ratchet's own table): `entries` **412,344,580 → 412,979,398 (+634 818, +0.15 %)** in exactly
     three rules — `cross_predefined_type_identifier` **+219 314**, `cross_predefined_type_name`
     **+207 752**, `trivia` **+207 752** — `memo_hits` **+219 314** (trivia +207 752, recognizer
     +11 562), `committed` **0**, no rule fell. The residual is the recognizer, its terminal and the
     terminal's layout read, once per refused type attempt; ACCEPTED through
     `contained_in_introduced_subgraph` (two rows in `accepted_rises.tsv`, exact from/to, this leaf as
     the elimination owner).
- ✅ **WHY + WHERE, cut 2 (the taint):** `MEMO-STORE-SOUNDNESS.2` stamps a cached FAILURE with the
  store's `write_epoch` when the failing parse READ the store, and replays it only while the epoch is
  unchanged (`memo_fail_tainted` in the generated `memoized_call`). A `pre` `in_scope_kind` evaluated
  on the refusal path is such a read, so the callers' failures — cached UNSTAMPED before the change,
  because `checked_type_identifier`'s `has_fact` read is rolled back with its rejected transaction —
  became epoch-stamped, and every later `variable_binding` emission re-ran them. That is not a bug in
  the memo (the stamp is what keeps the memo sound under scope changes); it is a cost the grammar
  author cannot see and the toolbox did not name. Now named: **put a store-reading predicate on a hot
  refusal path only as `post`, so the store is read once the text has matched.**
- ✅ **WHY + WHERE, cut 3 (the residual):** the ordered choice at `known_unscoped_data_type_identifier`
  ENTERS `cross_predefined_type_identifier` (a rule entry, counted) and then its terminal
  `cross_predefined_type_name := trivia /(?:CrossValType|CrossQueueType)\b/` (a second entry, plus the
  layout read) at every position where branch 1 refused, although the terminal's FIRST set is two
  literal spellings and the text there almost never begins with either. A PEG engine that computed
  FIRST sets for ordered choices and skipped a branch whose first terminal cannot match at the current
  byte would make cut 3 cost **zero entries** outside a cross — and would remove the same class of
  refused entries across every ordered choice in every grammar (`data_type`'s twelve alternatives are
  tried in sequence at every declaration-shaped position today). That is the engine-tier
  elimination; nothing at the grammar tier removes the last entry.
- **PRICED (not built):** (a) FIRST-set prediction for ordered choices — derive per-branch first-byte
  /first-regex sets in the generator (the fusibility census, TOOLBOX 5.3, already knows which rules
  begin with a terminal), emit a byte-class guard before the branch call, and keep it OUT of the
  protocol/fused-graph equivalence by construction (a skipped branch could not have matched); the
  ratchet is the oracle — expected to read an IMPROVEMENT, promoted deliberately. (b) Classify
  `in_scope_kind` / `not_in_scope_kind` reads as CHAIN reads and stamp them with a scope epoch
  rather than the fact epoch, so a `pre` scope gate on a refusal path taints only until the NEXT
  scope open/close — a smaller, exact fix for the taint alone. (a) subsumes (b) for this recognizer;
  (b) is the general answer for any `pre` scope gate. Either is an agnostic engine change and needs
  its own arms (TOOLBOX 3.7b) before a number is quoted.
- **WHY PARKED:** `.3.29` ships cut 3 with the residual ACCEPTED through the ratchet's coded, re-derived
  `contained_in_introduced_subgraph` invariant (its `accepted_rises.tsv` rows carry the exact
  from/to and this leaf as the owner of the elimination); the accept-set and the AST are exactly
  what the LRM asks, and the cost is confined to the construct that caused it. This leaf is the
  measurement that says the rise was confined, NOT that it was unavoidable — the honest bound the
  invariant's own docstring states.

### ⛔ `.91` — **`--lint-grammar` ACCEPTS TWO RULES WHOSE NAMES DIFFER ONLY BY CASE, AND THE GENERATOR THEN EMITS ONE `RULE_…` CONSTANT TWICE — the grammar lints green and the parser does not compile** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED, not SV-blocking — opened 2026-09-03 by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.30` / `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0349`)

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND.** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.30` added fourteen UDP table-symbol terminals named after their
  character — `udp_sym_x` and `udp_sym_X`, `udp_sym_b` / `udp_sym_B`, `udp_sym_r` / `udp_sym_R`, … — exactly as
  IEEE 1800-2017 A.5.3 spells them. `--lint-grammar` exited **0** (`1561 rules … unreachable_rules=0`), the
  interpreter parsed every pin as designed, `make focus_systemverilog` regenerated the parser, and the debug
  `ast_pipeline` build stopped with **six `error[E0592]: duplicate definitions with name RULE_UDP_SYM_X`**
  (`_B`, `_R`, `_F`, `_P`, `_N`): the generator uppercases a rule name into its `RuleId` constant, so two rules
  that differ only by case collapse onto one identifier. The grammar's own convention already works around
  it — every case-differing keyword pair carries a hash suffix (`kw_x_11f6ad8e` / `kw_X_c032adc1`) — but nothing
  documents the constraint and nothing checks it before the compile.
- ✅ **WHY + WHERE:** `generated/systemverilog_parser.rs:654-665` (first cut) — `const RULE_UDP_SYM_X: RuleId =
  549u16;` immediately followed by `const RULE_UDP_SYM_X: RuleId = 550u16;`; the emitting site is the
  generator's rule-constant loop (`ast_based_generator.rs`, `format_ident!("RULE_{}", name.to_uppercase())`
  shape). The lint (`grammar_wellformedness.rs`) has no arm for name collisions under case folding.
- **PRICED (not built):** one lint arm — refuse (error, not note) when two rule names are equal after
  `to_uppercase()`, naming both — plus a generator-side assertion at the constant loop so a grammar that slips
  past an older lint still fails at generation with the rule names rather than at `rustc` with the constant
  name. Two RED controls (a synthetic pair; the SV grammar minus its hash suffixes) and a GREEN control.
  A `TOOLBOX.md` 5.1 line and a sentence in the grammar-authoring chapter of the book.
- **WHY PARKED:** `.3.30` shipped by naming the upper-case twins `udp_sym_<c>_upper`; the class cost one
  regeneration and one 90-second build, not a corpus verdict. It is an engine-authoring ergonomics gap, not an
  SV release blocker.
- **ROUTING EVIDENCE lives in the opening tree** (`docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md`, *ROUTING EVIDENCE*, `.3.30` → `.91`).

### ⛔ `.92` — **A RULE SPLIT FROM ITS TWIN SO THAT ONE CALLER CAN WIDEN IT LOSES THE TWIN'S MEMO REPLAYS — the memo is keyed by RULE, so two rules that agree on every iteration but the last parse the shared iterations twice; measured on `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.31` and PRICED here** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED, not SV-blocking — opened 2026-09-03 by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.31` / `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0357`)

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND — by `PARSE-COST-RATCHET` pricing a caller split that moves its work ONE FOR ONE.**
  `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.31` widens the index of an array element whose member is then selected
  (`clist[b[0]++].m <= 1;`): the `{ identifier constant_bit_select . }` path of `hierarchical_identifier`
  spelled the index as `constant_bit_select → constant_expression`, which lacks exactly the two A.8.3
  `expression` alternatives `inc_or_dec_expression` and `( operator_assignment )`. The fix is a CALLER
  SPLIT — `hierarchical_bit_select`, a twin of `constant_bit_select` whose operand adds the two
  alternatives, referenced at the ten hierarchical-path sites, while `constant_bit_select` keeps its other
  callers (`bind_target_instance`, `constant_select`, the typedef-through-instance path). On the pinned
  sample the ratchet reads `entries` **+1,344,489** (+0.33 %), `memo_hits` **+694,442** (+0.38 %),
  `committed` **exactly 0** — and the per-rule table (`rule_costs.tsv`, promoted baseline vs `HEAD`) says
  where: `constant_bit_select` **−881,589** entries / **−38,027** committed ↔ `hierarchical_bit_select`
  **+881,591** / **+38,027**. The moved work is conserved to within two entries; the rise is NOT the spelling.
- ✅ **WHY + WHERE (read in the per-rule table, then in the emitted parser):** the generated `memoized_call`
  keys a memo cell on `(rule id, position)`. Before the split, every caller that reached a hierarchical name
  at a position — the several `primary` / `variable_lvalue` / `hierarchical_tf_identifier` attempts the
  tournament makes there, and `constant_select` — entered ONE rule and replayed one cell: `constant_bit_select`
  lost **872,207** memo hits while `hierarchical_bit_select` gained only **573,997**, i.e. **298,210 replays
  became executions**, and the loop body they re-ran is exactly the riser list: `lbrack` **+357,103**,
  `trivia` **+120,109**, `rbrack` **+65,125**. Nothing about that is SystemVerilog: two rules whose bodies
  agree on every iteration a narrow index can take differ only in the iteration it cannot, and the memo has
  no notion of one rule's success seeding another's.
- **The second component is `.90`'s mechanism 1, not a new one:** `hierarchical_index_operand` is a four-way
  choice entered **72,635** times, and the ordered choice enters EVERY alternative with no FIRST-terminal test
  — `unary_operator` +69,885, `inc_or_dec_expression` +71,510 (`plus_plus` / `minus_minus` /
  `inc_or_dec_operator` +17,203 each), `lparen` +71,340, `constant_primary` +69,875 (all replays:
  memo +69,911), then the expression tails `binary_operator` +69,552 and `question` +67,578 — one attempt per
  kind per indexed position, ~70 k positions. It is priced there; this leaf owns the memo loss only.
- **PRICED (not built):** an engine-tier declaration `hierarchical_bit_select @widens constant_bit_select`
  (or its inference: two `( … )*` rules whose bodies differ only by ADDED alternatives in one operand):
  a FAILURE of the wide rule at `p` is a failure of the narrow one (subset), and a SUCCESS of the narrow
  rule at `p` SEEDS the wide one — it resumes its loop at the narrow span's end instead of re-parsing the
  iterations both rules derive identically. A RED control: this grammar, `entries` on the pinned sample
  equal to the pre-split `412,979,398` plus the operand tournament alone (the `hierarchical_index_operand`
  sub-graph's ~+420 k), with the three loop-body risers at **0**; a GREEN control: a twin whose LAST
  iteration differs (`[b[0]++]`) still parses to the wide span. Whether the seed is sound under
  commit-once / no give-back (`.15` / `.17`) is the leaf's first question — a narrow success that COMMITTED
  inside the loop must be a wide success on the same prefix, which holds when the wide operand is a superset
  tried in the same order.
- **WHY PARKED:** the rise is +0.33 % of `entries` on the pinned sample with `committed` conserved exactly;
  no corpus verdict depends on it; the alternatives were refused first — an ordered choice that keeps
  `constant_bit_select` first commits to `b[0]` and never sees the `++` (commit-once), and a lookahead
  cannot see a postfix `++` without parsing the lvalue. It is an engine-authoring cost model gap, not an
  SV release blocker. ACCEPTED in `accepted_rises.tsv` under the new `caller_split_containment`
  invariant (`scripts/parse_cost_containment.py`, 8 self-test arms), which admits a rise only when the
  moved committed count is conserved one for one and every entries-riser lies in the introduced sub-graph.
- **ROUTING EVIDENCE lives in the opening tree** (`docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md`, *ROUTING EVIDENCE*, `.3.31` → `.92`).

### ⛔ `.93` — **THE GENERATED LAYOUT SKIPPER ACCEPTS AN UNTERMINATED BLOCK COMMENT — `/*` with no `*/` before EOF is consumed as layout, so a file that is nothing but `/*` PARSES; measured on `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.35` and routed here** (`todo`, ROUTED + PARKED, not SV-blocking — opened 2026-09-04 by `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.35` / `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0364`)

- ⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND.** The axis-2 bar's 21 `unexplained_accepts_invalid` rows were triaged by construct; sv2v `test/error/block_comment_eof.sv` — a file whose whole content is `/*` and a newline — is ACCEPTED by the release probe under every profile (`parse_full passed`, an EMPTY description). IEEE 1800-2017 §5.4 (`docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-5-lexical-conventions.md:58`): *"A block comment shall start with /* and end with */."* The grammar's own `block_comment := /\/\*([^*]|\*+[^*\/])*\*+\//` requires the terminator — and never sees these bytes.
- ✅ **WHY + WHERE (read in the emitted parser's generator, not inferred):** `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs` emits a LAYOUT SKIPPER with built-in comment arms unless the grammar claims the introducer as a non-comment token (`CommentArmSuppression`, `:96-115`; `claims_block_comment`, `:6907`). The block-comment arm (`regex_block_comment_arm`, `:7585-7600`, and the terminal twin `:7726`; the scanner at `:9416-9426`) advances past `/*` and `while i + 1 < len && !(bytes[i] == b'*' && bytes[i + 1] == b'/') { i += 1; }` then `if i + 1 < len { i += 2; }` — at EOF without `*/` the loop simply ends and the bytes are consumed as layout. Nothing about that is SystemVerilog: every grammar that leaves `/*` to the skipper accepts an unterminated comment. Probes: `/*\n` ACCEPT, `/*/\nmodule t; endmodule\n` ACCEPT, `/* x` (no newline) REJECT — the newline matters because the trailing scan differs, which is a second smell.
- **PRICED (not built):** the skipper's block-comment arm REFUSES at EOF without `*/` — it must not consume the bytes (leave the cursor at `/*` so the grammar's terminal/regex fails there with a `furthest_position`), or emit a lexical error. RED control: `/*\n` REJECTS for every generated parser whose grammar does not claim `/*`; GREEN controls: a terminated comment at EOF, `/* x */` mid-file, and a grammar that claims `/*` (unchanged). One generator change, parser-agnostic; the `.3.35` pin `invalid_unterminated_block_comment.sv` is the SV witness and stays `REJECT`-expected only once this lands (until then it is recorded as an `accepts_invalid` bar row owned here).
- **WHY PARKED:** one corpus row; the fix is engine-tier (the grammar cannot see layout bytes), so it is not a grammar slice and not an SV release blocker; a Rust change carries its own ceremony (clippy, the generated-parser reproducibility baseline, every family's regeneration).
- **ROUTING EVIDENCE lives in the opening tree** (`docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md`, *ROUTING EVIDENCE*, `.3.35` → `.93`).
- ⭐ **THE FIX WAS BUILT, VALIDATED AND REVERTED on 2026-09-09** (recorded in `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.56`'s `.3.57` session history, demoted there from `MEMORY.md`): `consume_layout_for_terminal` / `consume_layout_for_regex` in `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs` AND `rust/src/parse_harness_interpreter.rs` track whether `*/` was found, reset the cursor and STOP if not — the three negative tests reject, `ast_moved=0`, 0 regressions on the three SV lanes. Reverted because it moves ALL 10 parsers' layout skipper and needs per-family `make -C rust focus_<grammar>` regeneration (NOT `regenerate_generated_parsers`) + a full rebuild + every family's gates: the ceremony this leaf owes, in a focused ENGINE session.

### ✅✅ `.94` — **`done`** 2026-09-04 (landed with `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0366`, leaf `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.37`) — **`PARSE-COST-RATCHET` HAD NO SHAPE FOR AN ADMITTED ALTERNATIVE NET OF RETIRED WORK: two keyword terminals the standard requires (`null` as a primary, `local ::` as a class qualifier) are tried at every position their ordered choice reaches and almost never match, while two footnote re-spellings in the same tree retire more entries than they move and `committed` FALLS — the terminal identities need `committed` flat, containment refuses any fall, the profile-split predicate refuses a rise on a pre-existing name.   | `kw_null_2be88ca4` | 2 580 308 → 3 063 800 (**+483 492**) | the admitted `primary` alternative, tried last in the ordered choice — only where every earlier alternative failed — and almost never matched |
  | `kw_local_939bb46a` | 623 519 → 1 097 708 (**+474 189**) | the admitted prefix alternative, one attempt per hierarchical primary |
  | `trivia` | 88 980 877 → 89 847 394 (**+866 517**) | the memoized prefix lookup each terminal attempt buys (≤ the terminals' +957 681) |

The gate's own breach text — *"accepting a rise of a NEW SHAPE is a code change with its own task leaf"* — is this leaf.
- **THE INVARIANT (`scripts/check_parse_cost_ratchet.sh`, `_net_of_retired_work_verdict`, pure so the self-check drives it with dicts).** Per rule and over the run: (1) every DECLARED pre-existing name is a TERMINAL in the measured grammar's reference graph (its only reference is `trivia`) — a nonterminal's rise cannot be waived by declaring it (a declared nonterminal RAISES); (2) every rule name new to the GRAMMAR is declared; (3) `trivia`'s rise ≤ the declared terminals' rises; (4) every other pre-existing rise ≤ the entries the change retired; (5) `committed` did not rise. Cheaper spellings were priced and refused in the row: `null` folded into `primary_literal` is tried at EVERY primary (more entries); `local ::` folded into the package-scope prefix is the same attempt count on a dearer rule.
